This is the weak, almost-everywhere version of the perturbations in Proposition B.4, where the positive-integral hypothesis is needed for the cell unknowns. Membership $\alpha\in\mathcal K$ is imposed by callers, not by this package.
Breakdown.CertCell.AdmissibleTuple.summary: For a parameter $\alpha$ and coefficient $c$, a one-periodic solenoidal perturbation $v$ with weak derivatives, transport derivative $g$, forcing coefficients $\beta$ and square-integrable $F$ equal to the linearized operator on solenoidal tests: the weak form of Proposition B.4's perturbations.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.AssemblyEntr.text: For each cell of the finite mesh this supplies the matrices, row coefficients, harmonic sources, positive-weight candidates and error allowances used to compare the cell matrix with the analytic quadratic form. Each matrix is indexed by that cell's own resolved, auxiliary, forcing and constraint coordinates, so different cells may have different sizes. These are the local choices entering (B.26) and the proof of Proposition B.4. The definition supplies data only; it does not assert any matrix comparison, approximation bound or common consistency across cells.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.AssemblyEntr.summary: For each mesh cell, the matrices, row coefficients, sources, weight candidates and error allowances comparing the cell matrix with the analytic form, indexed by that cell's own coordinates. These are the local choices in (B.26) and Proposition B.4; nothing is asserted.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.AssemblyRegu.text: This requires the reference field, Hessian, harmonics, multiplier bounds, forcing fields and mesh to satisfy the analytic conditions for the cell assembly. It also requires all mode charges to be measurable and uniformly bounded on each cell, with the prescribed two-sided length bounds. Finally, every component of every forcing or constraint pairing profile, and every entry of every local $12\times12$ lower matrix, must be measurable and bounded on its cell. The last bounds may depend on their displayed indices; the charge bounds are uniform over harmonic labels. These conditions justify the finite-cell integrals in (B.26) and Proposition B.4. The declaration assumes them and does not derive them from finite point samples.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.AssemblyRegu.summary: The fields, multipliers, forcing and mesh satisfy the analytic cell conditions; mode charges are measurable and uniformly bounded on each cell with two-sided length bounds; pairing profiles and local $12\times12$ lower matrices are measurable and bounded. These justify the integrals in (B.26).

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.CellBlocks.text: This supplies three complex matrices on the cell unknowns: the retained stretching form, the retained forcing-and-constraint form, and the highest-degree subtraction. For eliminated harmonics it supplies twelve weights, twelve-component sources for the two pairings, a linear approximation to the eliminated field and a slack number. The row data comprise a row count, coefficient matrix, eliminated-mode test vectors, two row-weight matrices, a harmonic and polynomial-test index for every row, and twelve-component resolved-remainder test vectors. A finite set of further harmonics carries curl, gradient and velocity allowances. For each harmonic there are separate gradient, curl and velocity costs for stretching, pairings and rows, a tail budget, a highest-degree block and a positive row-error weight to be checked later. The forcing approximation supplies model fields, an active harmonic set and cost and error numbers. Additional numbers control inverse-period errors, residual errors, discarded forcing terms and the low and high angular parts; two further functions allocate curl and velocity costs to eliminated harmonics. These are the data behind the explicit forms and error terms in (B.26) and (B.33). All counts are finite; validity, signs and quantitative bounds are separate hypotheses, including those named after Proposition B.14.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.CellBlocks.summary: The data of one cell: three complex matrices on the cell unknowns, elimination weights, sources and slack, row data, per-harmonic costs and tail budgets, forcing approximations and error numbers. These lie behind the forms and errors in (B.26) and (B.33); bounds are separate.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.CellVars.text: For one cell this is the finite index set consisting of its resolved-harmonic polynomial and boundary coordinates, its auxiliary coordinates, and the two coefficient families for $\beta$ and $\zeta$. The cell matrices act on complex vectors indexed by this set. It is the local vector of unknowns described before (B.26); the later embedding expresses it through the two sets of real global unknowns. The declaration only names this index set and adds no assumptions on coordinate values or on their relation to a perturbation.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.CellVars.summary: The finite index set of one cell: its resolved-harmonic polynomial and boundary coordinates, auxiliary coordinates, and the coefficient families for $\beta$ and $\zeta$. It is the local vector of unknowns before (B.26), on which the cell matrices act; no assumptions are added.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.ConjDatum.text: This identifies two coordinates from possibly different layouts as conjugate counterparts. Polynomial gradient and velocity coordinates must have the same cell, basis, components and polynomial degrees, and opposite angular indices. Side coordinates must have the same directed segment, component and test index, with opposite angular indices; pressure moments use the same pressure segment. Corner coordinates use the same corner and auxiliary opposite corner, with the same component and opposite angular index. Stream coordinates use the same two corner points. The remaining polynomial coordinate alternative likewise requires the same cell, basis and indices with opposite angular label. Different kinds of coordinates never match. This is an exact equality-of-data condition supporting reality of the fields in Appendix B.3; it does not itself state equality of their assigned values to complex conjugates.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.ConjDatum.summary: Identifies two coordinates as conjugate counterparts: same kind and geometric data (cell, basis, degrees, segment, corner or stream points) with opposite angular indices; different kinds never match. It is an exact equality-of-data condition supporting reality of the fields in Appendix B.3.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.CouplingEntr.text: For every cell this supplies both the matrices, harmonic groups and balancing constants for its stretching estimate and the finite harmonic weights and coefficient matrices for its forcing-and-constraint pairing estimate. The first family may have a cell-dependent coordinate size; the second always acts on the two coefficient families of size $n$. These data produce $\mathsf P_{\mathsf Q}$ and $\mathsf B_{\mathsf Q}$ in (B.26). The definition simply provides the choices and asserts none of the inequalities or identities required for their validity.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.CouplingEntr.summary: For every cell, matrices, harmonic groups and balancing constants for its stretching estimate, and harmonic weights and coefficient matrices for its forcing-and-constraint pairing estimate. These produce $\mathsf P_{\mathsf Q}$ and $\mathsf B_{\mathsf Q}$ in (B.26); nothing is asserted.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.EliminationC.text: For each cell Q, choose a specified class S_Q of permitted complex vectors x. The formal condition requires Re⟨(A_Q−E_Q)x,x⟩≤Re⟨(P_Q+B_Q−T_Q)x,x⟩+b_Q(x)+e_Q(x) for every x∈S_Q. Here a complex quadratic value means Re(x*Ax); no Hermitian symmetry of every displayed matrix is assumed. The mesh must be valid. For each eliminated harmonic, the nine gradient weights are positive, the three velocity weights are nonnegative, and its azimuthal frequency k satisfies k≠0 and k²≠1. The elimination slack satisfies 0≤δ<1. If δ=0, then at every point, for every permitted x and every gradient component, the transformed source must equal the corresponding positive weight times the prescribed eliminated field. This makes the residual numerator zero before the expression |residual|²/(weight·δ) is evaluated. Division by zero is assigned zero; the zero-slack equality is essential to the argument. The source, eliminated-field and row-coupling components are measurable and bounded on the cell. The row weight matrix is positive definite, and the enlarged row matrix is at least that weight matrix plus (1−δ)⁻¹ times the eliminated-mode row Gram matrix in the Hermitian order. These hypotheses justify the inverse row form and the elimination estimates. The first comparison is (B.26); the other clauses specify the conditions under which it can be used.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.EliminationC.summary: For every cell and permitted complex $x$, $\mathrm{Re}\langle(A_Q-E_Q)x,x\rangle\le\mathrm{Re}\langle(P_Q+B_Q-T_Q)x,x\rangle+b_Q(x)+e_Q(x)$, which is (B.26), with no Hermitian symmetry assumed. Further clauses fix weights, $k\ne0$, $k^2\ne1$, $0\le\delta<1$ and exact sources if $\delta=0$.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.EntryCharges.text: On each cell, each harmonic's curl, gradient and velocity charges and the four functions used in the stretching bound must be measurable. One real constant for that cell must bound, uniformly over all harmonics and points, the absolute values of the three charges, the stretching constant, and the three reference-field majorants. The balancing length must lie between the reciprocal of that same constant and the constant. These are uniform boundedness assumptions for the integrals in Proposition B.4. Positivity of the constant is not stated here as a separate hypothesis; division by zero is taken to be zero, and the positive-length condition comes from the other hypotheses. The paper names these regularity and absorbed-error requirements after Proposition B.14.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.EntryCharges.summary: On each cell, the harmonic charges and stretching functions are measurable, and one constant bounds them uniformly, with the balancing length between that constant and its reciprocal. These are boundedness assumptions for Proposition B.4; division by zero is taken to be zero.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.ExteriorCove.text: This supplies finitely many regions equipped with integrated exterior tests of the type (B.30), finitely many regions equipped with pointwise tests of the type (B.29), and a finite selection from their union for every harmonic. It also gives one common collection of curl, gradient and velocity charges and a stretching constant for all these regions. The data concern the complement of the mesh in the quarter plane. They do not yet require coverage, disjointness, measurable regions or valid inequalities; those are exactly the further hypotheses needed to add the regional estimates in Proposition B.8.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.ExteriorCove.summary: Finitely many exterior regions with integrated tests of type (B.30) or pointwise tests of type (B.29), a finite selection for every harmonic, and common charges and stretching constant, off the mesh. Coverage, disjointness and the inequalities are further hypotheses.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.ExteriorCove.text: For one index of the exterior cover, this returns the supplied set of integer harmonic labels for the corresponding integrated or pointwise regional test. Such a set may be infinite even though the inventory of tests is finite. It encodes the harmonic sets over which the bounds before (B.29) hold uniformly. The selection rule for a particular harmonic is valid only when that harmonic belongs to every test chosen for it; this membership is required separately.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.ExteriorCove.summary: For one exterior-cover index, the supplied set of integer harmonic labels for its regional test, which may be infinite. It encodes the harmonic sets over which the bounds before (B.29) hold uniformly; membership of each selected harmonic is required separately.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.ExteriorCove.text: An exterior-cover index specifies either a region with an integrated estimate at infinity or a region with a pointwise estimate. This returns that supplied subset of the meridian plane, preserving its type of test. It is used to express the covering and disjointness conditions for the regions of (B.29) and (B.30). The definition imposes no geometric condition itself: membership in the exterior and measurability are required by the cover-validity statement.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.ExteriorCove.summary: For an exterior-cover index, the supplied subset of the meridian plane, keeping whether its test is integrated or pointwise. It expresses the covering and disjointness conditions for the regions of (B.29) and (B.30); no geometric condition is imposed here.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.FarFieldCond.text: The compactified-coordinate parameters must be valid. At every point of the mesh exterior in the open quarter plane, at every time and angle, the reference strain quadratic form is bounded by the supplied scalar strain majorant times $|u|^2$, and the oscillating vorticity gradient applied to $u$ is bounded by its majorant times $|u|$. The mean vorticity-gradient matrix has the supplied Euclidean operator bound. For every harmonic the three functions used in the exterior charges must equal these represented majorants. The balancing length is positive and independent of harmonic, and the mean and oscillating majorants are nonnegative. These are the exterior versions of the bounds defining (B.25). They are pointwise hypotheses on functions, stronger than agreement at finitely many exterior sample points.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.FarFieldCond.summary: On the mesh exterior in the open quarter plane, at every time and angle, the reference strain and vorticity-gradient terms are bounded by the supplied majorants, which equal the exterior charge functions. These are exterior versions of the bounds defining (B.25), required pointwise.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.FarFieldValu.text: This supplies the radial compactification parameters and three scalar functions represented in those coordinates: an upper strain bound, an upper bound for the mean vorticity gradient, and an upper bound for its oscillating part. They provide $s_1,s_2,s_3$ of (B.25) on the complement of the mesh. The data definition does not assert validity of the coordinate change, nonnegativity or any bound on the actual reference field. Those are the conditions of the exterior estimate used in Proposition B.4.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.FarFieldValu.summary: Radial compactification parameters and three scalar functions in those coordinates bounding the strain, the mean vorticity gradient and its oscillating part. They give $s_1,s_2,s_3$ of (B.25) off the mesh; validity, signs and bounds are not asserted.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.FieldRegular.text: The mesh must be valid and the symmetry order at least one. The reference field must be jointly $C^1$, one-periodic and solenoidal, with a measurable one-periodic weak Hessian and bounds $|W^{\mathrm r}|\le C/(1+|y|)$, $|\nabla W^{\mathrm r}|\le C/(1+|y|)^2$, $|H|\le C/(1+|y|)^3$. Its field, gradient and Hessian must equal finite harmonic sums from one set closed under negation, and the supplied Hessian must be symmetric pointwise. Uniform constants must give all multiplier-admissibility conditions for every parameter: positive period and weight, coefficients between zero and one, mode and transport bounds, and bounds on multiplier weights and their derivatives. The majorants must be measurable and the required rotation-and-plane symmetries present. Every forcing field has finitely many allowed harmonics, is measurable, one-periodic, bounded and supported in a fixed ball, has a square-integrable weak gradient and satisfies those two symmetries almost everywhere. These are the analytic hypotheses of the cell assembly in Proposition B.4. They use a weak Hessian and $C^1$ reference field, the regularity permitted by the piecewise-polynomial description in Appendix B.1.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.FieldRegular.summary: The analytic hypotheses of the cell assembly in Proposition B.4: a valid mesh, a $C^1$ one-periodic solenoidal reference field with weak Hessian, decay bounds and finite harmonic expansions, uniform multiplier constants, symmetries, and bounded compactly supported forcing fields.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.FluxChoice.text: This supplies the symmetry-related harmonic to use and optional real and imaginary global coordinates for the stream function at each of the two endpoints of a side. They are the data from which a zero-angular normal velocity moment is recovered by a flux identity. This is one of the relations used to build the global unknowns in Appendix B.3. The definition does not require the side to be radial or axial, validate the endpoint assignments or establish the divergence equation; those are requirements of the corresponding row condition.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.FluxChoice.summary: The symmetry-related harmonic and optional real and imaginary global coordinates for the stream function at the two endpoints of a side, from which a zero-angular normal velocity moment is recovered by a flux identity in Appendix B.3. Side type and the divergence equation are checked elsewhere.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.InRowRange.text: A complex vector of unknowns on one cell is admitted when all its used harmonic entries equal a prescribed linear function of real global determined coordinates, plus linear combinations of pressure-gauge directions and constant-pressure directions. Its two coefficient blocks corresponding to $\beta$ and $\zeta$ must have zero imaginary parts. Unused harmonic entries are unconstrained by this definition. Thus the permitted local vector need not literally equal $\mathsf X_{\mathsf Q}x_{\mathrm g}$. Identifying their quadratic values uses separate conditions that the cell form annihilates the gauge and constant-pressure directions. This explains the qualification about a vector on which the form does not depend in the proof of Proposition B.4.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.InRowRange.summary: A local complex vector is admitted when its used harmonic entries equal a linear function of real global coordinates plus pressure-gauge and constant-pressure directions, with real $\beta,\zeta$ blocks. It need not equal $\mathsf X_{\mathsf Q}x_{\mathrm g}$; annihilation conditions fix the forms.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.Internal.Rem.text: For every real linear map $M:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ and vectors $x,\psi\in\mathbb R^3$, the formal statement gives $\langle Mx-c\times x,\psi\rangle=\langle M^Tx,\psi\rangle$, where $c=(M_{32}-M_{23},M_{13}-M_{31},M_{21}-M_{12})$. This is finite-dimensional algebra, with no smoothness or divergence assumption. Setting $M=\nabla W$ and $x=W$ identifies $c$ with $\operatorname{curl}W$ and $M^TW$ with $\nabla(|W|^2/2)$ for differentiable $W$. The theorem supplies the algebraic identity needed for the pressure adjustment in (C.1); it has no conclusion about a numerical discretization.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.Internal.Rem.summary: For real linear $M$ on $\mathbb R^3$ and $x,\psi$, $\langle Mx-c\times x,\psi\rangle=\langle M^Tx,\psi\rangle$ with $c=(M_{32}-M_{23},M_{13}-M_{31},M_{21}-M_{12})$. With $M=\nabla W$, $x=W$ this relates $\operatorname{curl}W$ and $\nabla(|W|^2/2)$ for the pressure adjustment in (C.1).

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsBoundedOnC.text: For a complex function on the meridian plane and a fixed mesh cell, this requires measurability with respect to Lebesgue measure restricted to the cell and a real constant $C$ with $|f(r,z)|\le C$ at every point of its closed rectangle. The constant is existential and may depend on the function and cell. This is the boundedness hypothesis for the matrix and source entries integrated in Proposition B.4. It is stronger than an almost-everywhere bound because the displayed inequality holds on the whole cell; no continuity is required.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsBoundedOnC.summary: A complex function on the meridian plane is measurable for Lebesgue measure on a mesh cell and satisfies $|f(r,z)|\le C$ at every point of the closed rectangle for some $C$. This is the boundedness hypothesis for entries integrated in Proposition B.4, stronger than an almost-everywhere bound.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsExteriorCo.text: For every parameter in $\mathcal K$, every integrated region must satisfy the exterior conditions of (B.30) and every pointwise region the conditions of (B.29). All regions use exactly the same three charges and stretching constant. For each harmonic, its selected regions contain that harmonic in their mode sets, lie in the mesh exterior intersected with the open quarter plane, cover that exterior, and have pairwise intersections of Lebesgue measure zero. Every region in the inventory is measurable. The common charges are nonnegative everywhere and dominate the exterior stretching requirements; they and all harmonic-dependent stretching majorants and lengths are measurable. One constant bounds the three charges, stretching constant, three majorants, and the products of the oscillating-gradient majorant with the balancing length and its reciprocal, throughout the exterior and uniformly over harmonics. These assumptions permit the integrals to be added exactly once in Proposition B.8. They are stronger than geometric coverage alone and do not supply a numerical verification of the regional inequalities.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsExteriorCo.summary: For every parameter in $\mathcal K$, measurable exterior regions satisfy (B.29) or (B.30); each harmonic’s selected regions cover the exterior with null overlaps. Common nonnegative charges and the specified majorants have uniform bounds, allowing the integrals to be added once.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsKeyEvaluat.text: A proposed representation of a trace with harmonic $\iota$ is valid in exactly four cases: the same label with no conjugation and sign one; the negative label with conjugation and sign one; the reflected label $\iota^\flat$ without conjugation and with the coordinate's reflection sign; or $-\iota^\flat$ with conjugation and that sign. The last two require that the coordinate lie on $z=0$. This is the exact use of reality and (B.24) in the global-coordinate relations. The predicate concerns representation data; the validity of the underlying field symmetry is supplied separately.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsKeyEvaluat.summary: A representation of a trace with harmonic $\iota$ is valid in four cases: the same label; the negative with conjugation; $\iota^\flat$ with the reflection sign; or $-\iota^\flat$ with conjugation and that sign. The last two need $z=0$. This is the exact use of reality and (B.24).

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsKeyVar.text: This requires a chosen determined global variable to have neither a direct cell-coordinate assignment nor a forcing-coefficient assignment, and to carry exactly the prescribed harmonic and shared trace label with the prescribed choice of real or imaginary part. It identifies a real coordinate of the global vector with one component of a complex trace. This supports the shared unknowns used in Appendix B.3. It is a consistency condition on the assignment; no numerical trace value is specified.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsKeyVar.summary: A chosen determined global variable has no direct cell or forcing assignment and carries exactly the prescribed harmonic, trace label and real or imaginary part. It identifies a real global coordinate with one component of a complex trace in Appendix B.3; no value is specified.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsOffModeCov.text: For every parameter in $\mathcal K$, every cell and every harmonic not resolved there, each selected regional test must satisfy the scalar coefficient and nonnegativity conditions leading to (B.29). Its harmonic set must contain the selected harmonic, and its regions must cover the cell's intersection with the open quarter plane. At points common to a cell and one of its selected regions, that region's curl, gradient and velocity charges must be at least the charges already allocated by the cell, and its stretching constant must equal the cell's constant. This gives the pointwise lower bound for the unresolved part in Lemma B.5. Overlap is allowed inside a cell; the cover uses pointwise inequalities and does not add repeated integrals.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsOffModeCov.summary: For every parameter in $\mathcal K$, cell and unresolved harmonic, the selected regional tests satisfy the conditions leading to (B.29), contain the harmonic, cover the cell in the open quarter plane, and dominate the cell's charges. This gives the pointwise lower bound in Lemma B.5.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsRegionChar.text: For a region $Z$ in the meridian plane, the formal statement prescribes, for every harmonic and every point of $Z$, an upper bound $s_1$ for the strain quadratic form, an operator-norm bound $s_2$ for the time and angle mean of $\nabla\operatorname{curl}W^{\mathrm r}$, and an operator-norm bound $s_3$ for its difference from that mean. The mean is taken in the cylindrical frame. The inequalities for the strain and the oscillatory difference hold for all times, angles and real vectors. It also requires $s_2,s_3\ge0$ and a positive balancing function $h$ common to all harmonics. The data may depend on the harmonic; the paper uses common bounds. Trace-freeness, which implies $s_1\ge0$ for an actual strain, follows from divergence-freeness in the surrounding field assumptions.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsRegionChar.summary: On a meridian region $Z$, per harmonic: a bound $s_1$ on the strain quadratic form, operator-norm bounds $s_2\ge0$ on the time and angle mean of $\nabla\operatorname{curl}W^{\mathrm r}$ and $s_3\ge0$ on its oscillation, and a positive balancing $h$. The paper uses common bounds.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.KeyEvaluatio.text: This supplies a time-angle harmonic label, a choice of whether to conjugate its complex value, and a real multiplicative sign. It records how a trace of one harmonic is to be represented by a trace of the same, negative, reflected or negative-reflected harmonic. Those are the possibilities supplied by reality and (B.24). The data definition permits arbitrary labels and signs; the validity predicate restricts them to the appropriate four cases and requires plane geometry for reflection.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.KeyEvaluatio.summary: A time-angle harmonic label, a choice of conjugation and a real sign, recording how a trace is represented by that of the same, negative, reflected or negative-reflected harmonic, as reality and (B.24) allow. Arbitrary labels and signs are permitted here; validity is checked separately.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.OffModeCover.text: This supplies finitely many proposed pointwise mode tests, each with its meridian region, harmonic set and scalar bounds, and a finite selection of those tests for every cell and every integer harmonic label. The label set itself is infinite; only each selected family and the common test inventory are finite. The data implement the regional cover used in (B.29) for harmonics not resolved in a cell. Coverage, admissibility of the scalar inequalities and inclusion of the selected harmonic are separate requirements.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.OffModeCover.summary: Finitely many pointwise mode tests, each with a meridian region, harmonic set and scalar bounds, and a finite selection of tests for every cell and integer harmonic. These implement the regional cover of (B.29) for unresolved harmonics; coverage and admissibility are separate.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PairingCondi.text: The mesh and local calculus conditions must hold. On every allowed cell vector, the retained pairing matrix must lie below the explicit polynomial pairing minus its weighted quadratic error bounds. For each eliminated harmonic in the pairing list, the linear source must have gradient part equal to half the pairing profile and velocity part zero; outside the list it must be zero. For each harmonic in the common pairing list that is resolved and has a component nonzero on a set of positive measure, that harmonic must occur in the finite error list, have positive weight at most its assigned gradient cost, and have its squared polynomial-projection remainder bounded by its coefficient matrix for every real vector of pairing coefficients. Each such nonzero profile at a harmonic in the common pairing list outside the resolved and eliminated sets must belong to both the error list and the further error-mode set, with positive weight at most that mode's gradient allowance and a matrix bound for its full weighted squared norm. Every error-list matrix is nonnegative on real coefficient vectors and has positive weight; all gradient error allowances are nonnegative. These are the exact norm bounds behind $\mathsf B_{\mathsf Q}$ in (B.26). The restrictions to nonzero profiles are almost-everywhere tests on the cell. The paper describes these error allocations without displaying their full quantified form.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PairingCondi.summary: On every allowed cell vector the retained pairing matrix lies below the explicit polynomial pairing minus weighted quadratic errors, with conditions on sources, error lists, weights and matrix bounds: the norm bounds behind $\mathsf B_{\mathsf Q}$ in (B.26), stated more fully than in the paper.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PairingData.text: This gives a finite set of harmonics, a real weight for each harmonic, and a complex square matrix for every integer harmonic label, each acting on two copies of the $n$ coefficient indices. The two families represent $\beta$ and $2\zeta$ in the pairing with $\nabla b_i$ and $\Xi_i$. Their matrices bound the norms of the portions of those profiles not retained in the cell polynomial projection. These are the weighted errors in the form $\mathsf B_{\mathsf Q}$ of (B.26). Positivity of the weights and nonnegativity of the matrices on real coefficient vectors are separate conditions.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PairingData.summary: A finite set of harmonics, a real weight for every harmonic, and a complex matrix for every harmonic on the two $n$-component families representing $\beta$ and $2\zeta$. The selected matrices bound projection errors in $\mathsf B_{\mathsf Q}$ of (B.26); validity is separate.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PartBound.text: If a real or imaginary trace part has an assigned global variable, that variable must carry exactly the specified harmonic, trace label and part. If no variable is assigned, the part must be one of those omitted by reality, plane parity or pressure normalization, or it must be a stream-function value on the axis. Thus absence of a coordinate needs a mathematical reason. This is a detailed global-unknown condition named after Proposition B.14. The axis-stream alternative requires radius zero but does not itself impose any height or regularity condition.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PartBound.summary: An assigned trace part carries exactly the specified harmonic, label and part; an unassigned part must be omitted by reality, plane parity or pressure normalization, or be an axis stream value. So a missing coordinate needs a mathematical reason, among the conditions after Proposition B.14.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PotentialCon.text:
These are conditions for the stretching part $\mathsf P_{\mathsf Q}$ of (B.26), for every cell and every vector in its specified allowed set. The mesh and all local calculus conditions must hold. The retained matrix form must lie below the explicit polynomial coupling form after subtracting ordinary, orthogonal and remote-angular model errors. The matrix assigned to projection remainders must dominate the sum of their squared norms divided by the positive gradient and velocity balancing numbers. Every group balance and both balancing lengths are positive; group strain and vorticity-gradient bounds and ordinary error bounds are nonnegative. Each group's stretching constant is exactly $\sqrt{7/2}$ or $\sqrt{9/2}$.

The gradient and velocity costs assigned to the resolved remainders must dominate their local absorption allowances, their projection balances and the reciprocal Young costs of the orthogonal model error, multiplied by the maximum complementary radial weight. The curl cost must dominate its curl absorption allowance. The reference harmonic list must agree exactly with the list used to expand the given field. On eliminated modes, the stretching source is exactly the convolution of the coupling matrix with the complementary resolved polynomials, and its components are bounded and measurable. The proposed orthogonal-error bounds dominate the supplied errors, and all three Young weights are positive.

For each eliminated mode, the pointwise curl, gradient and velocity charges must cover the ordinary and remote-angular errors, the reciprocal orthogonal-error costs, the relevant maximum diagonal elimination weights and the separate row allowances; the gradient charge also covers any forcing-pairing approximation weight. Those row allowances are nonnegative. The further error-mode set is disjoint from the eliminated and resolved sets. Every group of unresolved partners is disjoint from both sets. Every nonzero model coupling from a resolved harmonic to a harmonic outside them must be covered by a group, with the appropriate reference harmonic. Group harmonic sets are pairwise disjoint, and their negatives belong to the reference harmonic list.

The reference field, its weak Hessian, their finite harmonic expansions and all measurable bounds must satisfy the analytic cell regularity conditions; the Hessian is symmetric. The ordinary and remote-angular errors must fit the local pairing allowances. The remote bounds dominate their supplied strain and vorticity-gradient errors; their balance is positive and their cutoff no larger than the cutoff with a proved spectral gap. Every model component and every remote component is zero outside its prescribed harmonic list. The strain model is symmetric. The stretching bound is valid for all harmonics on each cell, and every unresolved harmonic uses a constant at least $\sqrt{7/2}$.

Nonzero entries of the polynomial splitting matrix must stay within one resolved harmonic and avoid pressure coordinates on both sides. Each coupling matrix must represent exactly the symmetrized model stretching expression. Every group wave estimate must be valid on the whole cell, use the same symmetry order, bounds and balancing lengths, and reproduce the strain and vorticity-gradient model harmonics at its fixed second index. If its constant is $\sqrt{7/2}$, the reconstructed vorticity-gradient matrix must have trace zero for every angle; $\sqrt{9/2}$ is allowed without that trace assertion.

Every plane rectangle must satisfy its analytic bounds, have a nonzero harmonic with an admissible reflected label, and have both reflected harmonics unresolved and uneliminated in every cell. Finally, for every remaining unresolved harmonic and every point of the cell, its three charges must dominate the sum of all applicable group costs divided by group balances, all row-error costs, all forcing-pairing approximation weights, all ordinary and remote-angular costs, all reciprocal orthogonal-error costs, and, in the velocity charge, the sum of the plane-rectangle demands. These are quantified inequalities on given functions and matrices, not checks at selected points. The paper describes their role in Proposition B.4 and explicitly lists their kinds after Proposition B.14, but does not print this full collection; the formal hypothesis is correspondingly more explicit than the displayed statement (B.26).
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PotentialCon.summary: On every cell and allowed vector, the retained matrix lies below the explicit stretching form minus model, orthogonal, remote-angular and remainder errors, with positivity, grouping, covering and charge conditions and group constants $\sqrt{7/2}$ or $\sqrt{9/2}$; more explicit than (B.26).

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PotentialDat.text: For a cell, this gives a $12\times12$ complex coupling matrix for every harmonic and meridian point, a matrix splitting the polynomial coordinates into two parts, and a matrix bounding their projection remainders. It specifies finitely many groups of resolved modes, unresolved partners, row partners and reference harmonics, with a fixed second harmonic index for each group. Each group carries strain and vorticity-gradient bounds, a balancing number, wave data, velocity and vorticity bounds and one stretching constant. Two positive-length candidates balance gradient and velocity terms; two numbers bound the ordinary model errors, two bound the polynomial-orthogonal errors, and three numbers are Young-inequality weights. Separate gradient and velocity balances are supplied for each harmonic. A finite reference harmonic set and a further strain and vorticity-gradient bound, positive balance candidate and natural-number angular cutoff describe the remote angular part. These are the finite choices used to construct $\mathsf P_{\mathsf Q}$ in (B.26), with the remaining harmonic grouping and error conditions named after Proposition B.14. No positivity or model identity is required by the data definition alone.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PotentialDat.summary: For a cell, $12\times12$ coupling matrices for every harmonic and point, a splitting matrix, a remainder bound, mode groups with bounds and stretching constants, balancing lengths, error numbers, Young weights and remote-angular data: the choices building $\mathsf P_{\mathsf Q}$ in (B.26).

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowCondition.text: The mesh must be valid, and the row labels and test indices must give a bijection with all prescribed tested harmonics and their finite test lists in each cell. Each tested harmonic has a positive row-error weight, and its full test Gram matrix must be positive definite. The forcing cost assigned to the rows is nonnegative and bounded by the cell forcing allowance. Every resolved harmonic has strictly positive gradient and velocity row costs. The row matrix must dominate the base test matrix, the gradient and velocity tail Gram matrices divided by their respective costs, and the error Gram matrix, in Hermitian order. Every component of the resolved tail tests is measurable and bounded on the cell. These are the matrix and finiteness conditions for the pairings of $F$ with the test triples in (B.26) and (B.34). The paper states the role of these rows but leaves these detailed allocations among the further conditions after Proposition B.14.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowCondition.summary: Row labels biject with the tested harmonics and tests; each tested harmonic has positive error weight and positive definite Gram matrix; forcing cost fits the allowance; resolved row costs are positive; the row matrix dominates the test, tail and error Gram matrices. These support (B.26) and (B.34).

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.text: For each resolved cell coordinate this supplies a finite set of determined global variables, complex coefficients on that set, a natural-number rank and one proposed mathematical justification of the row. It selects one determined variable for every forcing coefficient $\beta_i$ and one free variable for every constraint multiplier $\zeta_i$. Each numbered auxiliary cell coordinate also has a selected free real variable, an optional free imaginary variable and a conjugation choice. These data define the embedding matrices $\mathsf X_{\mathsf Q}$ in Appendix B.3. Ranks allow recursive row identities to use only previously justified coordinates. The data definition itself imposes no rank decrease, equality or distinctness condition.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.summary: For each resolved cell coordinate, determined global variables with complex coefficients, a natural-number rank and a proposed justification, plus designated variables for each $\beta_i$, $\zeta_i$ and auxiliary coordinate. These define the embedding matrices $\mathsf X_{\mathsf Q}$ in Appendix B.3.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Acc.text: For each resolved cell coordinate, this requires exactly the conditions belonging to its selected justification: shared trace, subdivision, stream flux, derived linear relation, normal-gradient identity, direct evaluation or unused coordinate. No different justification is substituted automatically. These conditions ensure that the proposed row has a mathematical interpretation or is irrelevant to all forms. This is the formal check of the global-coordinate relations described in Appendix B.3 and named after Proposition B.14. It states a predicate on supplied rows; it does not itself assert that every row satisfies it.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Acc.summary: Each resolved cell coordinate satisfies exactly the conditions of its selected justification: shared trace, subdivision, stream flux, derived relation, normal-gradient identity, direct evaluation or unused. This checks the global-coordinate relations of Appendix B.3 as a predicate on rows.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Der.text: A finite complex linear combination of the layout relations must have coefficient exactly one at the target coordinate and zero at every pressure coordinate. Every other nonzero coefficient must refer to a row with strictly smaller natural-number rank whose justification is not unused. The target row must equal minus the sum of those other coefficients times their already specified rows. This implements solving an exact homogeneous relation for one cell unknown in Appendix B.3. The normalization avoids division; the strict rank decrease makes the construction noncircular. It is a hypothesis on the given coefficients, not an approximate linear solve.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Der.summary: A finite complex combination of layout relations has coefficient one at the target and zero at pressure coordinates, its other terms are rows of strictly smaller rank and not unused, and the target row is minus their weighted sum. This solves an exact relation in Appendix B.3 noncircularly.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Flu.text: This applies only to the constant-test normal velocity moment of angular index zero, represented using its own harmonic or its conjugate with sign one. The two endpoint stream values must have valid real and imaginary global coordinates or justified omissions. On a radial side the radius is positive and the row is $-t_0[\Psi(b)-\Psi(a)]/r_0$. On an axial side the linear test $t_{10}+t_{11}r$ has $t_{10}\ne0$; its moment must already be justified at strictly smaller rank, and the constant-test row is $(t_0/t_{10})[m_1-t_{11}(\Psi(b)-\Psi(a))]$. These are the explicit divergence-based flux relations used in Appendix B.3. The strict rank inequality prevents a circular definition.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Flu.summary: For the constant-test zero-angular normal velocity moment, with valid endpoint stream coordinates: on a radial side with positive radius the row is $-t_0[\Psi(b)-\Psi(a)]/r_0$; on an axial side with $t_{10}\ne0$ it is $(t_0/t_{10})[m_1-t_{11}(\Psi(b)-\Psi(a))]$, with $m_1$ of smaller rank.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Key.text: The cell coordinate must have a geometric trace label. Its proposed same, conjugate or plane-reflected representation must satisfy the four allowed symmetry cases. The optional real and imaginary variables must either identify the corresponding shared trace components exactly or have a justified omission by reality, symmetry, normalization or an axis stream value. Finally the supplied row must equal the resulting coefficient vector multiplied by the reflection sign. These conditions make one global-coordinate relation precise in Appendix B.3. They are exact identities on labels and coefficients, with the relevant field reality and symmetry hypotheses used later to justify the trace equality.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Key.summary: The coordinate has a geometric trace label, its representation is one of the four allowed symmetry cases, its real and imaginary variables identify the shared trace or are justifiably omitted, and the row equals the coefficient vector times the reflection sign, as in Appendix B.3.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Lea.text: Without conjugation, the source coordinate must be the target itself. With conjugation, it must lie in the negative harmonic and have exactly the corresponding conjugate layout data: basis, indices, segments or corners as appropriate. A real-part global coordinate is compulsory and must evaluate that source cell coordinate; any imaginary-part coordinate must evaluate the same source. An absent imaginary coordinate is permitted only for the zero time-angle harmonic. The row must be exactly the real-plus-or-minus-imaginary extraction vector. This is the direct field-evaluation alternative for the global unknowns in Appendix B.3.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Lea.summary: Without conjugation the source is the target; with it, the conjugate counterpart in the negative harmonic. A real-part variable must evaluate the source, an imaginary part may be absent only for the zero harmonic, and the row is the extraction vector. This is direct evaluation in Appendix B.3.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Nor.text:
This gives the exact row identity for the normal component of the normal gradient on a side, obtained from the solenoidal equation at angular frequency $k$. The terminal endpoint must be an identified corner with all components already justified. The initial endpoint must be similarly identified, except that it may be absent on an axial side starting at radius zero. Every side velocity moment used in the formula must have a valid index, smaller rank and a non-unused justification.

On a radial side at $r_0\ne0$, for test polynomial $t$, the row for $\int t\,\partial_rv_r\,dz$ is $-r_0^{-1}\int t(v_r+ikv_\phi)\,dz-t(b)v_z(b)+t(a)v_z(a)+\int t'v_z\,dz$. A supplied finite expansion of $t'$ in the side tests must hold as an exact polynomial identity. On an axial side, the row for $\int rt\,\partial_zv_z\,dr$ is $-bt(b)v_r(b)+at(a)v_r(a)+\int rt'v_r\,dr-ik\int tv_\phi\,dr$; the supplied polynomial expansion is now for $rt'$. The source uses natural-number exponents, so the exponent $j-1$ is truncated at zero; its coefficient $j$ makes the constant derivative term vanish. These are the divergence relations mentioned in Appendix B.3 and after Proposition B.14, with explicit noncircular row dependencies.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Nor.summary: The exact row for the normal component of the normal gradient on a side, from the solenoidal equation at frequency $k$, with explicit radial and axial formulas and exact expansions of $t'$ or $rt'$. Moments and corners used have smaller rank; the exponent $j-1$ truncates at zero.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Spl.text: The original coordinate must be a side moment, admit the selected symmetry representation and not be an omitted pressure-normalization coordinate. There must be a positive finite number of subsegments, each with increasing endpoints, adjoining consecutively and covering the original interval exactly. On every subsegment the original test polynomial must equal the prescribed finite linear combination of the subsegment tests as a polynomial identity on the whole real line. Every nonzero term must avoid omitted pressure coordinates and must have correctly assigned or legitimately omitted real and imaginary components. A subsegment marked for flux is allowed only for a zero-angular normal velocity coordinate, using the same harmonic or its conjugate with sign one. Its endpoint stream coordinates must be valid; a radial flux has nonzero radius, and an axial flux has a nonzero constant coefficient in its linear test and valid coordinates for that linear moment. Finally the cell row must equal the signed sum of the subsegment rows with the prescribed coefficients. These are exact subdivision and divergence relations for $\mathsf X_{\mathsf Q}$ in Appendix B.3, among the conditions named after Proposition B.14.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Spl.summary: A side moment is split into finitely many consecutive subsegments covering its interval, its test equals a combination of subsegment tests, flux subsegments meet the flux conditions, and the row is the signed sum of subsegment rows: exact subdivision relations for $\mathsf X_{\mathsf Q}$.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Unu.text: An unused coordinate must have the zero row on global variables. Its entire row and column in the cell matrix must also be zero, and it must not be any of the moments selected by a plane rectangle. Thus assigning no physical value to it cannot change the cell form or the plane terms in (B.38). These are exact conditions for the unused alternative in the global-coordinate construction of Appendix B.3. Merely setting its value to zero would not satisfy this statement unless the matrix and rectangle conditions also hold.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Unu.summary: An unused coordinate has the zero row on global variables, a zero row and column in the cell matrix, and is not a moment selected by a plane rectangle. So it cannot change the cell form or the plane terms in (B.38); setting its value to zero alone would not suffice.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.cor.text: For a corner used in a derived row, this requires all three of its velocity-component rows at the selected harmonic to have rank strictly smaller than the target row and to have a justification other than unused. It supplies the already established boundary values needed when integrating the divergence equation along a side. This is a detailed ordering requirement in the global-coordinate construction of Appendix B.3. It does not impose any smoothness or compatibility of the values by itself.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.cor.summary: For a corner used in a derived row, all three velocity-component rows at the selected harmonic have rank strictly smaller than the target and are not unused. This supplies earlier boundary values when integrating the divergence equation along a side in Appendix B.3.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.cor.text: If a corner index is supplied, this returns the global row of the specified velocity component at that corner and harmonic. If no corner is supplied, it returns the zero row. This convention is used at the axis endpoint of an axial side, where the relevant boundary term contains a factor of radius. It supports the normal-gradient identities in Appendix B.3. The definition alone does not justify omitting an arbitrary corner; the row conditions restrict when the absent-corner case is allowed.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.cor.summary: If a corner is supplied, the global row of the specified velocity component at that corner and harmonic; otherwise the zero row. This convention is used at the axis endpoint of an axial side, where the boundary term has a factor of radius, in the normal-gradient identities of Appendix B.3.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.rel.text: Given a finite set of the layout's homogeneous linear relations and a complex multiplier for each, this forms their weighted sum and returns its coefficient at a specified cell coordinate. The coefficients are the exact relation rows supplied by the polynomial and boundary calculus. This is used to solve one coordinate in terms of others when constructing $\mathsf X_{\mathsf Q}$ in Appendix B.3. The definition alone does not normalize the target coefficient, exclude pressure coordinates or ensure that the other coordinates have already been justified.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.rel.summary: Given finitely many homogeneous layout relations with complex multipliers, the coefficient of their weighted sum at a given cell coordinate. It is used to solve one coordinate in terms of others for $\mathsf X_{\mathsf Q}$ in Appendix B.3; normalization and ordering are checked elsewhere.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.row.text: This defines the matrix from determined and free real global variables to all complex cell unknowns. Resolved-mode coordinates use their specified rows on determined variables. Auxiliary cell coordinates use one free real coordinate plus an optional free imaginary coordinate, with sign of $i$ reversed when conjugation is selected. Forcing coefficients select their designated determined variables, and constraint multipliers select their designated free variables. Every other matrix entry is zero. It is the explicit matrix $\mathsf X_{\mathsf Q}$ of Appendix B.3. The construction alone does not show that its rows agree with field evaluations or that every variable is used.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.row.summary: The matrix $\mathsf X_{\mathsf Q}$ of Appendix B.3 from real global variables to complex cell unknowns: resolved coordinates use their rows, auxiliary ones a free real and optional imaginary variable, and $\beta$, $\zeta$ their designated variables; other entries are zero.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.row.text: For one cell coordinate and a real vector $x$ of determined global unknowns, this is the finite complex sum $\sum_{a\in S}c_ax_a$, where $S$ is that row's supplied support and $c_a$ its coefficients. It is the local value obtained from the global unknowns in Appendix B.3. Only real global variables are used here; complex cell values arise from complex row coefficients. The row's mathematical interpretation is justified separately by trace, symmetry, divergence or evaluation identities.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.row.summary: For one cell coordinate and a real vector $x$ of determined global unknowns, the finite complex sum $\sum_{a\in S}c_ax_a$ over the row's support. It is the local value from the global unknowns in Appendix B.3; its interpretation is justified separately.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.row.text: For one resolved cell coordinate this returns its supplied complex coefficient at each determined global variable in the specified finite support, and zero at every other variable. Thus values supplied outside that finite support are deliberately ignored. This is the row representing that coordinate in the embedding $\mathsf X_{\mathsf Q}$ of Appendix B.3. The definition provides a linear coefficient vector without asserting that it computes an actual trace or polynomial coefficient of a perturbation.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.row.summary: For one resolved cell coordinate, its supplied complex coefficient at each determined global variable in the finite support and zero elsewhere, so values outside the support are ignored. This is the row of that coordinate in $\mathsf X_{\mathsf Q}$ of Appendix B.3.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.til.text: For a radial subsegment at radius $r_0$, this forms $-t_0\,[\Psi(b)-\Psi(a)]/r_0$, where $t_0$ is its constant test value and the stream values are represented by real and imaginary global variables. For an axial subsegment, if its linear test is $t_{10}+t_{11}r$, it forms $(t_0/t_{10})[m_1-t_{11}(\Psi(b)-\Psi(a))]$, where $m_1$ is the linear-test normal-velocity moment. Conjugation is included if requested. These are the zero-angular flux identities used for trace subdivision in Appendix B.3. The denominators must be nonzero in a valid row; the definition alone uses zero for a quotient by zero.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.til.summary: On a radial subsegment at radius $r_0$, $-t_0[\Psi(b)-\Psi(a)]/r_0$; on an axial one with linear test $t_{10}+t_{11}r$, $(t_0/t_{10})[m_1-t_{11}(\Psi(b)-\Psi(a))]$, with optional conjugation. These are the zero-angular flux identities of Appendix B.3; a quotient by zero is taken as zero.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.til.text: This constructs one of the subsegments specified for a split trace row, retaining the original side orientation and level and using the selected endpoints and test-polynomial coefficients. Its auxiliary opposite level is chosen to be one greater than its level, as in the shared-trace convention. This supplies the segment on which the row's smaller moments are defined. The requirement that the subsegments form the original interval, with ordered nonempty interiors, belongs to the split-row conditions in the global assembly of Appendix B.3.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.til.summary: One subsegment of a split trace row, keeping the original side orientation and level, with the selected endpoints and test coefficients and auxiliary opposite level one greater than its level. That the subsegments form the original interval is checked by the split-row conditions of Appendix B.3.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.til.text: For a selected subsegment and test index, this uses the stream-function flux formula only if that subsegment is marked for flux and the test index is zero. Otherwise it uses the ordinary real-plus-imaginary coordinate row, with the selected conjugation. This choice combines direct moments with flux-derived constant moments in one subdivision formula. It is part of the global-coordinate construction named after Proposition B.14. Eligibility for a flux formula, allowed missing coordinates and nonzero denominators are verified by the split-row conditions, not by this selection.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.til.summary: For a subsegment and test index, the stream-function flux formula if the subsegment is marked for flux and the index is zero, and otherwise the ordinary real-plus-imaginary coordinate row with the selected conjugation. Eligibility and nonzero denominators are checked by the split-row conditions.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.vel.text: For a side velocity moment used to derive another coordinate, this requires that its test index be within the side degree plus two, that its natural-number rank be strictly smaller than the target's rank, and that its justification not be the unused alternative. These conditions ensure the moment is both defined and already justified when the relation is used. This is the well-founded ordering of the divergence and trace relations for the global unknowns in Appendix B.3. It is a requirement on the proposed row construction, with no estimate on the magnitude of the moment.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.vel.summary: A side velocity moment used to derive another coordinate has test index within the side degree plus two, rank strictly smaller than the target's, and a justification other than unused. This gives the well-founded ordering of the relations for the global unknowns in Appendix B.3.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.vel.text: This retrieves the global coefficient row for a selected harmonic, side, vector component and velocity-moment index when the index is below the side degree plus two. For every larger natural-number index it returns the zero row. The extension makes formulas involving arbitrary polynomial indices defined everywhere. It is used in the divergence identities constructing the cell unknowns in Appendix B.3. A zero returned outside the index range is a convention and makes no assertion that the corresponding physical moment vanishes.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.vel.summary: The global row for a selected harmonic, side, component and velocity-moment index below the side degree plus two, and the zero row for larger indices. The zero is a convention making formulas defined everywhere, not an assertion that the moment vanishes.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowFunctiona.text:
For every cell and every allowed cell vector, each row of the supplied matrix must equal the sum of three explicit terms: its own similarity-equation row with angular frequency $\varkappa\iota_1$ and temporal frequency $2\pi(2\iota_2-\iota_1)$ times the modeled inverse period; the convolution rows with all resolved velocity and vorticity model harmonics; and the forcing coefficients paired with the supplied forcing models. On eliminated harmonics the row-source test must equal the convection test exactly. On resolved harmonics the remainder test must equal the complementary radial weight times that test minus its polynomial projection, using degree $d$ for gradient entries and $d-1$ for velocity entries.

Every listed row partner belongs to the further error-mode set. All nonzero model couplings from tested rows to modes outside the resolved and eliminated sets must be covered by the supplied groups, and the finite difference set of all possible such sources must also lie in the error-mode set. The curl and velocity allowances there dominate twice the discarded-group cost times the sum of squared group velocity or vorticity bounds, together with the ordinary-plus-orthogonal model errors and the remote-angular errors whenever a reference harmonic connects to a tested row.

Every test triple is solenoidal, has bounded angular derivative divided by radius, has the prescribed separate polynomial degrees, and has side degree at least two below the coefficient degree. Its pressure segments satisfy the boundary partition and orthonormality conditions. The forcing approximation has positive cost and nonnegative error; their product is at most the row forcing allowance. Its weighted squared error summed over the designated harmonic list is at most that error bound. Every model forcing harmonic is measurable and square integrable on the cell; outside the designated list the tested pairings with the true and model forcing fields agree exactly.

Every forcing-pairing approximation weight is positive, and on a resolved harmonic it fits the local gradient allowance. The ordinary, discarded-group, low-angular and high-angular costs are positive, as is each tested harmonic's inverse-period cost. For each tested harmonic, the row-error weight multiplied by the sum of reciprocal ordinary cost, reciprocal period cost when its time frequency is nonzero, the number of active groups divided by the group cost, the remote-angular reciprocal term and the reciprocal forcing cost when applicable is at most one.

For every resolved harmonic the curl allowance dominates twice the ordinary cost times the squared sum of the velocity-model and orthogonal errors, plus twice the selected remote source cost times its squared velocity error. The velocity allowance has the analogous vorticity terms and, on tested harmonics, the period cost times the squared inverse-period error multiplied by $[2\pi(2\iota_2-\iota_1)]^2$. The same two inequalities, without the period term, hold for the separate row allowances on eliminated harmonics. Each group's reconstructed velocity and vorticity have the asserted squared bounds at every point, time and angle. Finally the modeled inverse period approximates $1/S(\alpha)$ within the cell error for every $\alpha\in\mathcal K$. These are the full kinds of row identities and absorbed-error conditions used in (B.26) and Proposition B.4, explicitly deferred after Proposition B.14. They are hypotheses on all relevant points and vectors, not conclusions of a finite sampling procedure.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowFunctiona.summary: Each equation row equals its similarity-equation row plus convolution rows and forcing pairings, with exact tests, solenoidal test triples, forcing bounds, row budgets at most one, allowance dominations, and $1/S(\alpha)$ approximated on $\mathcal K$: the row conditions of (B.26).

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowReason.text: A cell coordinate may be represented by a directly shared trace, a subdivision into smaller side moments, a stream-function flux, a linear combination of established cell relations, a normal-gradient identity from divergence, or a direct cell coordinate with optional conjugation. A final alternative marks a coordinate unused. Each alternative carries the concrete indices, coefficients or endpoint data needed to check it. These are the possible global-unknown relations described in Appendix B.3 and named after Proposition B.14. Selecting an alternative is only data; a separate predicate checks its full mathematical conditions.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowReason.summary: The permitted justifications of a cell coordinate: shared trace, subdivision, stream flux, combination of established relations, normal-gradient identity, direct coordinate with optional conjugation, or unused, each with its checking data. Selecting one is only data.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowReason.Is.text: This condition holds exactly when the chosen justification for a cell coordinate is the unused alternative. It is false for every trace, subdivision, flux, relation, divergence or direct-evaluation alternative. It is used to prevent a derived row from depending on a coordinate that has no asserted field interpretation. The accompanying unused-row condition must additionally show that the coordinate contributes to neither the cell matrix nor a plane rectangle. This is an internal classification of the global-coordinate construction described in Appendix B.3.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowReason.Is.summary: Holds exactly when the chosen justification of a cell coordinate is the unused alternative. It prevents a derived row from depending on a coordinate with no field interpretation; the unused-row condition must also show it contributes to neither the cell matrix nor a plane rectangle.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.SplitChoice.text: This gives a choice of symmetry-related harmonic, a finite number of subsegments with endpoints and test-polynomial systems, a common natural-number expansion degree, and the real coefficients expanding the original test on each subsegment. For every subsegment and test index it records optional real and imaginary global variables. Each subsegment also has a choice of whether its constant normal-velocity moment will be represented by a stream-function flux, with optional real and imaginary variables for the two endpoint stream values. These are data for the side-subdivision relations named after Proposition B.14. Coverage, matching endpoints, valid polynomial identities and allowed omissions are checked separately.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.SplitChoice.summary: A symmetry-related harmonic, finitely many subsegments with endpoints and test systems, a common expansion degree, real coefficients expanding the original test, optional real and imaginary variables, and flux choices with endpoint stream variables. Validity is checked separately.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.TailConditio.text: Every cell must satisfy the local calculus conditions. For every resolved harmonic its spectral tail budget must hold at that cell's polynomial degree and angular frequency; its two derivative lower bounds must equal the lower bounds used in the cell matrix. The total gradient cost from stretching, pairings and rows must be at most the sum of the four allocated gradient allowances. The stretching curl cost must be nonnegative and at most its curl allowance. The total velocity cost must fit the three velocity allowances. Finally the highest-degree subtraction matrix must be the sum of the supplied blocks weighted by their velocity charges. These are the exact budget comparisons used with (B.27) to control the orthogonal remainders in Proposition B.4. The conditions assume the bounds on the given numbers and matrices.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.TailConditio.summary: On every cell, each resolved harmonic's tail budget holds at the cell's degree and frequency with the same lower bounds as the cell matrix; gradient, curl and velocity costs fit their allowances; the highest-degree matrix is the charge-weighted sum of blocks. These are the budgets used with (B.27).

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.TreeRowCondi.text: The cell embedding matrices must agree with the prescribed global rows, and every used local datum must be justified by a permitted trace, symmetry, divergence or gauge relation. The formal statement requires $\langle A_0x,x\rangle\le-(c\omega^2/(4\pi)+e)|\beta|^2-|\zeta|^2/(4\pi t)$ for every real global vector. It also identifies the determined coordinates carrying $\beta$, sets the extra linear coupling from free to determined coordinates to zero, requires the cell form and its adjoint to annihilate constant-pressure directions, and requires the base perturbation, all its derivatives, $\beta$ and $F$ to vanish. The rectangle coordinates must ignore those constant-pressure directions. Thus the displayed bound (B.43) is one clause of a condition which also makes the local and global unknowns compatible.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.TreeRowCondi.summary: Cell embeddings agree with the global rows, used local data are justified by trace, symmetry, divergence or gauge relations, and $\langle A_0x,x\rangle\le-(c\omega^2/(4\pi)+e)|\beta|^2-|\zeta|^2/(4\pi t)$ for real $x$. The bound (B.43) is one clause among these compatibility conditions.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.TreeStateInt.text: For any finite cell and tree data and any real vector $x$ of global unknowns, the formal statement proves $\langle Nx,x\rangle=\langle A_0x,x\rangle+\sum_Q\langle A_QX_Qx,X_Qx\rangle+2\sum_\Pi\langle C_\Pi X_\Pi x,X_\Pi x\rangle$. Complex cell and rectangle forms are read by taking the real part of the Hermitian quadratic expression. The total matrix is the sum of all attached forms after their embedding in the global coordinates; the two occurrences of each auxiliary matrix have opposite signs and cancel. No analytic condition on a perturbation, no positivity, and no node inequality is needed for this algebraic identity. The matrices passed between nodes are arbitrary and do not enter the total sum.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.TreeStateInt.summary: For any cell and tree data and real $x$, $\langle Nx,x\rangle=\langle A_0x,x\rangle+\sum_Q\langle A_QX_Qx,X_Qx\rangle+2\sum_\Pi\langle C_\Pi X_\Pi x,X_\Pi x\rangle$, complex forms read through their real Hermitian value. Auxiliary matrices cancel; no positivity or analytic condition is needed.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.absorbValue.text: For a resolved harmonic this evaluates $a_c|\operatorname{curl}G|^2+a_g|G|_{\mathrm F}^2+a_v|u|^2$ on its reconstructed polynomial gradient and velocity, using the three absorption coefficients supplied for that cell and harmonic. This is the lower-order form available to absorb projection and model errors in the proof of Proposition B.4. The formula is pointwise in the meridian variables and makes no assertion about the signs or adequacy of those coefficients; that is part of the local lower-bound and tail-budget hypotheses.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.absorbValue.summary: For a resolved harmonic, $a_c|\operatorname{curl}G|^2+a_g|G|_{\mathrm F}^2+a_v|u|^2$ on its reconstructed polynomial gradient and velocity, with the cell's absorption coefficients. This is the lower-order form absorbing projection and model errors in Proposition B.4; no sign is asserted.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.activeGroups.text: For a row harmonic $\iota$, this selects every reference-harmonic group for which there is a listed row partner $\iota'$ with $\iota-\iota'$ in that group's reference harmonic set. The number of selected groups appears in the error budget for that row, because each may contribute a separate unresolved coupling. This is a finite combinatorial step in the proof of Proposition B.4. It does not assert that the groups are disjoint or their bounds valid; those are independent hypotheses.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.activeGroups.summary: For a row harmonic $\iota$, every reference-harmonic group with a listed row partner $\iota'$ such that $\iota-\iota'$ lies in the group's reference set. Their number enters that row's error budget in Proposition B.4; disjointness and bounds are separate hypotheses.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.actuatorRow.text: For a cell, harmonic $\iota$, polynomial test triple $\varphi$ and real forcing field $b(\theta,y)$, this defines $\int_{\mathsf Q}r\sum_a\widehat b_{\iota,a}(r,z)\overline{\varphi_a(r,z)}\,dr\,dz$. The harmonic uses the symmetry order of the cell data. It is the coefficient multiplying a forcing parameter in the local row of Proposition B.4. The forcing field is arbitrary in this definition; finite harmonic support, measurability, square integrability and any approximation by a polynomial model are supplied by the surrounding conditions.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.actuatorRow.summary: For a cell, harmonic $\iota$, test triple $\varphi$ and real forcing field $b$, the integral $\int_{\mathsf Q}r\sum_a\widehat b_{\iota,a}\overline{\varphi_a}\,dr\,dz$: the coefficient of a forcing parameter in the local row of Proposition B.4. The forcing field is arbitrary here.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.bandEliminat.text: For a complex cell vector $x$, this sums over the finite eliminated harmonic set and integrates on the cell with measure $r\,dr\,dz$ the expression $\sum_{j=1}^9w_j|b_j|^2-2\operatorname{Re}\sum_j\overline{b_j}s_j-\sum_j|s_j-w_jb_j|^2/(w_j\delta)$. Here $b$ is the supplied linear approximation in gradient variables, $s$ the combined converted source, $w_j$ the gradient weights and $\delta$ the cell slack. This is the eliminated-harmonic contribution $\mathsf b_{\mathsf Q}$ to (B.26). Its use requires positive weights and $0\le\delta<1$. At $\delta=0$ division is zero by convention, and a separate condition requires $s_j=w_jb_j$ exactly, so no error is discarded.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.bandEliminat.summary: The eliminated-harmonic contribution $\mathsf b_{\mathsf Q}$ to (B.26): the cell integral with weight $r$ of $\sum_jw_j|b_j|^2-2\operatorname{Re}\sum_j\overline{b_j}s_j-\sum_j|s_j-w_jb_j|^2/(w_j\delta)$. At $\delta=0$ division is zero, and a separate condition then requires $s_j=w_jb_j$.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.bandGram.text: This defines the matrix whose $(i,i')$ entry is $\sum_\iota\int_{\mathsf Q}r\sum_{j=1}^9\overline{s_{ij}}s_{i'j}/w_j\,dr\,dz$, summing over the eliminated harmonics. The vectors $s_i$ are the row sources after converting velocity into angular-gradient variables, and $w_j$ are the corresponding gradient weights. It quantifies the additional equation-row cost produced by elimination in (B.26). Positivity follows under positive weights and integrability, imposed separately. Zero denominators are assigned quotient zero in the raw definition; the intended conditions require $w_j>0$.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.bandGram.summary: The matrix with entries $\sum_\iota\int_{\mathsf Q}r\sum_{j=1}^9\overline{s_{ij}}s_{i'j}/w_j\,dr\,dz$ over eliminated harmonics, quantifying the extra row cost of elimination in (B.26). Zero denominators give quotient zero in the raw definition; the intended conditions require $w_j>0$.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.bandPart.text: For a complex cell vector $x$ this is $Px$, with $P$ the supplied splitting matrix. Together with $x-Px$ it sums exactly to $x$. It is used in the polynomial decomposition of the stretching form in (B.26). No idempotence, self-adjointness or orthogonality is part of the definition. The conditions restrict the nonzero entries of $P$ to nonpressure coordinates within the same resolved harmonic and control the resulting form directly.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.bandPart.summary: For a complex cell vector $x$, the vector $Px$ with $P$ the supplied splitting matrix, so $Px$ and $x-Px$ sum to $x$. It is used in the polynomial decomposition of the stretching form in (B.26); no idempotence or orthogonality is assumed.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.couplingPair.text: For two complex cell vectors $x,y$, this sums over all pairs of resolved harmonics $\iota,\iota'$ the integral $\int_{\mathsf Q}r\operatorname{Re}(U_\iota(x)^*M_{\iota-\iota'}U_{\iota'}(y))\,dr\,dz$, where $U$ concatenates the polynomial gradient and velocity and $M$ is the supplied coupling matrix. The difference of harmonic labels expresses the mode-selection rule for the reference field. It is the polynomial model contribution to $\mathsf P_{\mathsf Q}$ in (B.26). Its identification with the actual stretching expression and its error bounds are separate assumptions.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.couplingPair.summary: For cell vectors $x,y$, the sum over resolved harmonics $\iota,\iota'$ of $\int_{\mathsf Q}r\operatorname{Re}(U_\iota(x)^*M_{\iota-\iota'}U_{\iota'}(y))\,dr\,dz$. It is the polynomial model contribution to $\mathsf P_{\mathsf Q}$ in (B.26); its link to the true stretching is a separate assumption.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.couplingTail.text: For one resolved harmonic, form the sum of its coupling with all complementary resolved polynomials and its local lower matrix applied to its own complementary polynomial. Multiply this twelve-component function by $\widehat r=r/w(r)$, where $w(r)=r$ on an axis cell and $w(r)=1$ otherwise. Choose either the gradient part or the velocity part. For the chosen part, the expression sums the squared weighted norms of the residuals after projection onto the product polynomial space: degree at most $d$ in each variable for the nine gradient components, or degree at most $d-1$ for the three velocity components. It is the projection remainder that the auxiliary matrix must bound in (B.26). Natural-number subtraction truncates at zero; valid layouts provide the intended positive degree. The projection is defined by choosing a polynomial $P$ of the stated degrees such that $\int_{\mathsf Q}w(r)(F-P)\overline T\,dr\,dz=0$ for every polynomial $T$ of those degrees. It is independent of the supplied basis. If no such polynomial exists, the chosen projection is zero; the usual orthogonal-projection interpretation requires the cell and integrability hypotheses.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.couplingTail.summary: For one resolved harmonic, its coupling with the complementary polynomials plus its lower matrix term, multiplied by $\widehat r=r/w(r)$, with squared norms orthogonal to the polynomial space of degree $d$ (gradient) or $d-1$ (velocity) summed. This is the projection remainder bounded in (B.26).

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.creditVelDem.text: For a harmonic $\iota$ and meridian point, this sums the prescribed charge of every plane rectangle containing that point for which the physical harmonic of $\iota$ is the reflection of the rectangle harmonic or its negative. Other rectangles contribute zero. This is the additional velocity-square cost charged to the unresolved reflected modes in the proof of Proposition B.4, giving the terms with $2\mathsf C_\Pi$ in (B.34). The definition permits overlapping rectangles, in which case their charges add. The cell index is an available parameter but does not enter this sum; coverage by the mesh and nonnegativity are separate hypotheses.
Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.creditVelDem.summary: For a harmonic $\iota$ and meridian point, the sum of the charges of every plane rectangle containing the point whose harmonic reflects to that of $\iota$ or its negative. This is the extra velocity-square cost giving the $2\mathsf C_\Pi$ terms in (B.34); overlapping charges add.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.crossTest.text: For complex reference velocity $W$, vorticity $\Omega$ and a complex test vector $\varphi$, this constructs twelve coefficients for pairing a perturbation gradient and velocity with convection.
