Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsCellFo.summary: For every $\alpha\in\mathcal K$ and weak perturbation solving the linearized identity with a periodic pressure gradient, the cell vector satisfies a positive-part inequality among $\langle A_Qx,x\rangle$, pairings, errors and $D_Q^\pm,U_Q^\pm$; when finite this is the estimate of (B.33).

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsCellMo.text: For a fixed cell and each of its resolved lattice harmonics, the formal statement requires $d_0\ge1$ and a compatible local description of the harmonic's polynomial coefficients, face and corner data, and linear relations. It identifies the volume degree with the natural number $d$ and the side degree with the integer $d_0$ stored for that harmonic. It also requires the chosen finite parametrization to satisfy the selected local relations. Together with the mesh conditions this yields $d\ge d_0+2$ and $d_0\ge2$ on tested harmonics, as in the paragraph following (B.25). This condition specifies consistent local data for a given cell; it does not assert that arbitrary complex values are traces of an actual perturbation.
Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsCellMo.summary: For each resolved harmonic of a cell, $d_0\ge1$ and a compatible local description of polynomial coefficients, face and corner data and linear relations, with volume degree $d$ and side degree $d_0$. With the mesh conditions this gives $d\ge d_0+2$ and $d_0\ge2$ on tested harmonics, as after (B.25).

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsCellMo.text: Fix a cell $\mathsf Q$, the symmetry order $\varkappa$, a polynomial degree $d$, a reference field $W^{\mathrm r}$, its supplied Hessian, and polynomial models of velocity, vorticity, strain and vorticity gradient. For each of these four quantities the formal statement requires a decomposition into its polynomial model, a remainder orthogonal to polynomials, a remainder beyond an angular cutoff $N$, and an error bounded by a prescribed constant. The bounds for velocity, vorticity and strain hold at every time and point belonging to this cell alone and away from the axis. For the vorticity gradient the final error bound holds for almost every meridian point and every time and angle. Each of the four remote angular remainders has all harmonics $|\iota_1|\le2N$ equal to zero. Its velocity and vorticity are continuous away from the axis and the plane $z=0$, its two matrix fields are measurable, and its strain is symmetric. Each orthogonal remainder is measurable; its every harmonic and component has zero unweighted integral against $r^iz^j$ on the cell for $i,j\le2d+1$, and its strain is symmetric. All twelve error bounds are nonnegative. The four polynomial models are closed under complex conjugation of harmonics. These are explicit extra hypotheses for the polynomial decomposition described in the proof of Proposition B.4 and named after Proposition B.14; the paper does not write these quantified conditions out.
Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsCellMo.summary: Each of velocity, vorticity, strain and vorticity gradient of $W^{\mathrm r}$ splits into a polynomial model, an orthogonal remainder, a remainder beyond cutoff $N$ and a bounded error, with stated regularity and moment conditions. The paper does not write these quantified conditions out.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsCharge.text: For every resolved harmonic and every point of a cell, this requires three bounds. First, at all normalized times and azimuthal angles, the quadratic form of the symmetric gradient of $W^{\mathrm r}$ is at most $s_1|u|^2$ for every real vector $u$. Second, the complex matrix of the zero time-angle harmonic of the supplied vorticity gradient has Euclidean operator norm at most $|s_2|$. Third, the difference between the full vorticity gradient and the real part of that mean, converted from cylindrical components to a Cartesian linear map, has norm at most $s_3|u|$ for every real $u$, time and angle. These are the three majorants in (B.25). Their sign requirements and the identification of the supplied Hessian with that of $W^{\mathrm r}$ are imposed elsewhere; the squared mean-matrix condition alone permits a negative $s_2$.
Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsCharge.summary: Three majorants of (B.25) on a cell: the strain quadratic form is at most $s_1|u|^2$, the mean vorticity-gradient matrix has operator norm at most $|s_2|$, and its deviation from the mean is at most $s_3|u|$. Signs are imposed elsewhere; $s_2$ may be negative here.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsHarmon.text: This condition requires a layout for a rectangle with nonnegative inner coordinates and positive widths, specified radial and vertical orthonormal polynomial bases, azimuthal order κ and the prescribed finite angular-label set. The layout’s cell, bases, labels and degrees must agree with those data. Its side and pressure segments are valid; its pressure-gauge segment has a nonzero constant test and nonnegative left endpoint. Side segments lie on the designated cell sides and cover each nonaxis side with disjoint interiors. Radial side segments on r=0 are excluded. Recorded opposite positions and endpoints must agree with the rectangle geometry; missing endpoint or corner entries are permitted only at the axis. Corners are nonaxis corners, with the correct opposite corners. Radial-side tests have a nonzero constant coefficient; horizontal-side tests also have a nonzero linear coefficient. Side tests are orthonormal through degree q+1, where q≥1 is the side degree and Q≥q+1 is the volume degree. These are local representation requirements for the unknowns before (B.26); the paper’s full cell assumptions also require d≥d₀+2. The formal condition asks for the existence of auxiliary data with no forcing or constraint indices, solely to specify this layout; it makes no assertion about a fractional equation.
Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsHarmon.summary: A valid cell layout with order κ, given rectangle, prescribed orthonormal bases and angular labels: valid side and pressure segments, side degree q≥1 and volume degree Q≥q+1. The paper's full cell assumptions require d≥d₀+2, stronger than this degree separation.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsLeafBo.text: For every resolved harmonic this requires positive source and orthogonal weights and balancing length, nonnegative strain allowance and row weights, and the following comparisons. The curl allowance is at least twice the source weight times the squared velocity-model error. The strain allowance dominates the chosen strain constant. The velocity allowance dominates twice the source weight times the squared vorticity-model error, plus, for tested harmonics, the row weight multiplied by $[2\pi(2\iota_2-\iota_1)\varepsilon_S]^2$, where $\varepsilon_S$ bounds the inverse-period error. The pairing allowances dominate the strain-model error, $3/(2\sqrt2)$ times the vorticity-gradient error times the balancing length, and $3/(2\sqrt2)$ times that error divided by the pointwise stretching length. These are explicit allocations for the error form in (B.26), among the additional conditions named after Proposition B.14. The pointwise stretching length must be positive through the other cell conditions; division by zero is defined as zero in the raw expression.
Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsLeafBo.summary: For each resolved harmonic, positive weights and explicit allowance inequalities dominating the model errors of velocity, vorticity, strain and vorticity gradient, allocating them to the error form in (B.26). Division by zero is defined as zero in the raw expression.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsLeafVa.text: For each resolved harmonic of a fixed cell, the formal statement requires a constant $\underline I_2>0$ below the Hessian coefficient and a constant $\underline I'_2\ge0$ below the gradient-of-curl coefficient. It gives a measurable, bounded Hermitian $12\times12$ matrix field $A(r,z)$ acting on the nine entries of $\mathbf G$ and three entries of $\mathbf v$. Its quadratic form is bounded above by $I'_1|\operatorname{curl}\mathbf G|^2+I_1|\mathbf G|^2+I_0|\mathbf v|^2$ minus the prescribed polynomial-model errors. A second inequality, for $r\ne0$, bounds the stretching majorant and pairing errors by this form plus constant absorption allowances, with the cell's radial weight. It also requires nonnegative $s_2,s_3$, positive $h$, and equality of the constant allowances for opposite harmonics. All these are hypotheses on the supplied matrix field and constants; no eigenvalue calculation is performed by this condition.
Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsLeafVa.summary: For each resolved harmonic, $\underline I_2>0$, $\underline I'_2\ge0$ and a Hermitian $12\times12$ field $A(r,z)$ whose form is at most $I'_1|\operatorname{curl}\mathbf G|^2+I_1|\mathbf G|^2+I_0|\mathbf v|^2$ minus model errors and absorbs the stretching majorant. No eigenvalues are computed.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsMatOrt.text: For every harmonic label ι, both matrix indices a,b, and natural exponents i,j≤d, require the meridian integral of the corresponding rotating-frame matrix mode times rⁱzʲ to vanish. The raw Fourier frequency is (2ι₂−ι₁,κι₁), and evaluation is at normalized time zero on (r,0,z). This is the matrix version of the finite-degree moment condition used in Appendix B.3. The measure is dr dz, with no additional radial weight. The supplied matrix field need not yet be a velocity gradient, and no integrability assumption is part of this condition; those facts are separate in the analytic application.
Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsMatOrt.summary: For every label ι, indices a,b and natural exponents i,j≤d, the meridian integral of the rotating-frame matrix mode times rⁱzʲ vanishes, with measure dr dz and no radial weight. No integrability is part of the condition.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsPeriod.text: Given a parameter set $\mathcal K$, a real-valued period function $S$, an approximation $s_0$ and an error allowance $\varepsilon$, this is precisely the condition $|1/S(\alpha)-s_0|\le\varepsilon$ for every $\alpha\in\mathcal K$. No sign or continuity assumption is part of this definition. In the certificate application, positivity of $S(\alpha)$ is imposed elsewhere. The reciprocal is defined to be zero when $S(\alpha)=0$; the positive-period hypothesis excludes that convention in the intended application.
Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsPeriod.summary: Exactly $|1/S(\alpha)-s_0|\le\varepsilon$ for every $\alpha\in\mathcal K$, with no sign or continuity assumption. The reciprocal is zero when $S(\alpha)=0$; positivity of $S$ is imposed elsewhere in the certificate.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsPlaneM.text: Given two cell layouts, this requires every nonradial velocity or gradient segment of the first layout at height zero to have a segment of the second with the same endpoints and the same test-polynomial coefficients. It requires the analogous matching for pressure segments. These are the trace identifications used with the reflected harmonic $\iota^\flat$ in (B.24) and in Proposition B.4. The relation as defined is directional: every relevant segment of the first layout must occur in the second, without asserting the reverse inclusion. Equality of test coefficients is stronger than merely equality of their moments on one field.
Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsPlaneM.summary: Every nonradial velocity, gradient or pressure segment at height zero in the first layout has a segment in the second with the same endpoints and test coefficients, as used with $\iota^\flat$ in (B.24). The relation is directional.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsPressu.text: For a rectangular cell, this requires every pressure segment to lie on one of its radial or axial sides. Segments on the same side have disjoint interiors. They cover both axial sides, the outer radial side, and the inner radial side when its level is nonzero. The coverage requirement exempts an inner side at $r=0$; this definition still permits segments on that side. The full local cell conditions separately forbid radial pressure segments at level zero. Each segment lies within its side, and its stored opposite level is the other radial or axial endpoint of the rectangle. For every segment, the real test polynomials with indices below the prescribed side degree are orthonormal in the unweighted one-dimensional integral. These are detailed hypotheses for the pressure moments of Appendix B.3 and the pressure normalization mentioned after Proposition B.14. The paper does not state this segmentation convention explicitly. Endpoints may be shared, since disjointness is only required for interiors.
Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsPressu.summary: Pressure segments lie on cell sides, have disjoint interiors on each side, and cover both axial sides and the required radial sides; coverage of the inner side r=0 is exempted. Their test polynomials are orthonormal; exclusion of axis segments is a separate condition.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsSplitP.text: On a specified spatial set, at every real time, require ‖H‖≤a, ‖L‖≤b, and ‖F−P−H−L‖≤c. Here F is the full field, P its local polynomial model, H and L two supplied further parts, and a,b,c real constants; all fields take values in the same normed space. These are the three pointwise model-error bounds of the kind described in Appendix B.3 and after Proposition B.14. The declaration imposes no frequency support, orthogonality, measurability, or decay on H or L despite their intended use for particular omitted parts.
Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsSplitP.summary: On a spatial set at every time, $\|H\|\le a$, $\|L\|\le b$ and $\|F-P-H-L\|\le c$, for a field $F$, polynomial model $P$ and two further parts. No frequency support, orthogonality or measurability is imposed on $H$ or $L$.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsSplitP.text: On the specified spatial set, the two supplied parts H,L obey ‖H‖≤a and ‖L‖≤b at every time and point. The remaining error F−P−H−L is bounded by c for almost every meridian pair (r,z), for every real time and every angle, whenever (r cos φ,r sin φ,z) is in the set. This is the representative-tolerant version of the polynomial-model error condition in Appendix B.3. The exceptional meridian set is chosen before time and angle, so it is independent of both; this is stronger than a separate almost-everywhere assertion at each time. No frequency or orthogonality claim is included.
Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsSplitP.summary: The parts obey ‖H‖≤a and ‖L‖≤b everywhere on the set, and the error F−P−H−L is at most c for almost every meridian pair (r,z), every time and angle. The exceptional set is chosen independently of time and angle.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsStrong.text:

The a.e. identity $F=g-\operatorname{tr}H+c(G)	imes W+c(D_yW)	imes v+\sum_i eta_ib_i+P_g$, $c$ the curl vector. With $G=
