Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.realNodeE.summary: Given the weighted matrix error inequality, a real node whose supplied matrices satisfy the two quadratic-form comparisons, the weighted row bounds on the residual and $\underline p_{\xi,j}\le p_j-m_j$ on pivots satisfies (B.42) for every real global vector $x$.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.realRestr.text: For a complex n×m coordinate matrix E and complex n×n matrix H, this is the real m×m matrix Re(E*HE), taking the real part entry by entry. For real x its quadratic form is Re((Ex)*H(Ex)). It is the complex-to-real form conversion used after (B.40). Neither Hermitian symmetry of H nor injectivity of E is assumed by the definition; those properties matter separately when drawing conclusions about the form.
Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.realRestr.summary: For complex E and H, the real matrix Re(E*HE), whose form at real x is Re((Ex)*H(Ex)): the complex-to-real conversion after (B.40). Neither Hermitian H nor injective E is assumed.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.signedSla.text: Let $H,K$ be real symmetric matrices on a finite coordinate set, $\mathcal U$ a pivot set, $Y',Y$ rectangular matrices, and $w_i>0$. If $w_i\sum_j|B_{ij}|/w_j\le m_i$ for $B=H-\operatorname{diag}_{\mathcal U}(p)-Y'Y'^T+YY^T-K$, then for every real $x$ one has $\langle(K-\operatorname{diag}_{\mathcal U^c}(m))x,x\rangle+\sum_{j\in\mathcal U}(p_j-m_j)x_j^2-|Y^Tx|^2\le\langle Hx,x\rangle$. This is the weighted quadratic-form estimate used in the proof of Lemma B.7. The error matrices $H',K'$ of (B.39) are included when this result is applied at a node; they are not separate arguments of this scalar-row theorem. The weights are strictly positive, so its row divisions have their ordinary meaning.
Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.signedSla.summary: For symmetric $H,K$, pivots $\mathcal U$ and $w_i>0$, if $w_i\sum_j|B_{ij}|/w_j\le m_i$ for $B=H-\operatorname{diag}_{\mathcal U}(p)-Y'Y'^T+YY^T-K$, then $\langle(K-\operatorname{diag}_{\mathcal U^c}(m))x,x\rangle+\sum_{j\in\mathcal U}(p_j-m_j)x_j^2-|Y^Tx|^2\le\langle Hx,x\rangle$ for real $x$.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.signedTre.text: For finite sets of determined and free real coordinates and a finite collection of nodes, suppose the root has no parent and every other node has exactly one assigned parent. At each node assume, for every real $x$, $\langle V_\xi x,x\rangle+\sum_{j\in\mathcal U_\xi}\underline p_{\xi,j}x_j^2-|Y_\xi^Tx|^2\le\langle N_\xi x,x\rangle+\sum_{\xi'}\langle V_{\xi'}x,x\rangle$, where $\xi'$ ranges over children. Then $\langle Nx,x\rangle\ge\langle V_{\rm root}x,x\rangle+\sum_\xi\sum_{j\in\mathcal U_\xi}\underline p_{\xi,j}x_j^2-\sum_\xi|Y_\xi^Tx|^2$ for every real $x$, with $N=\sum_\xi N_\xi$. Each non-root passed matrix occurs once on each side in the sum. No separate connectedness or acyclicity hypothesis is required for this cancellation identity. The theorem retains the root term; the paper's (B.41) follows when that term is nonnegative. It assumes neither positive pivot lower bounds nor coverage of all coordinates, and thus does not alone imply strict positivity on the common column kernel.
Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.signedTre.summary: If each non-root node has one parent and every node satisfies the real node inequality, then $\langle Nx,x\rangle\ge\langle V_{\rm root}x,x\rangle+\sum_\xi\sum_{j\in\mathcal U_\xi}\underline p_{\xi,j}x_j^2-\sum_\xi|Y_\xi^Tx|^2$, $N=\sum_\xi N_\xi$; (B.41) follows when the root term is nonnegative.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.slackRema.text: For real square matrices H,K, a pivot set U with real values p, and rectangular matrices Y₊,Y₋, this is H−diag_U(p)−Y₊Y₊ᵀ+Y₋Y₋ᵀ−K. It is precisely the matrix inside the absolute values in (B.40), where Y₊ is the positive-column correction and Y₋ contains the columns whose squares remain as a loss. The formula has no symmetry, sign or row-sum hypotheses. Its entrywise enclosure is a separate requirement.
Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.slackRema.summary: The real matrix H−diag_U(p)−Y₊Y₊ᵀ+Y₋Y₋ᵀ−K, precisely the matrix inside the absolute values in (B.40). No symmetry, sign or row-sum hypothesis is attached.

Breakdown.CertCell.CoefficientConditions.text: For every parameter in $\mathcal K$, each supplied region and harmonic set must give valid lower bounds for the five coefficients of (B.16). The regions must cover every point of the open quarter plane for a harmonic that is neither resolved nor eliminated in any cell containing that point. On each region the first four lower coefficients are bounded below by one common real constant $-M$, with no sign condition on $M$, and the velocity coefficient multiplied by $r^2+z^2$ has the same lower bound. On each cell, every resolved or eliminated harmonic has five prescribed constant lower coefficients below the actual coefficients for all parameters; the first four and the radially weighted fifth again have one common lower bound. These are the bounds used to prove $\mathcal I^-<\infty$ in Proposition B.4. They need not be nonnegative and do not assert the positivity tests (B.29) or (B.30).
Breakdown.CertCell.CoefficientConditions.summary: For every parameter in $\mathcal K$, regions and harmonic sets give valid lower bounds for the five coefficients of (B.16), covering unresolved harmonics, with uniform common lower constants on regions and cells. These prove $\mathcal I^-<\infty$ in Proposition B.4.

Breakdown.CertCell.CoefficientEntry.text: This supplies finitely many pairs of harmonic sets and meridian regions, each with data bounding the five coefficients of the mode density, together with a uniform real lower-bound constant. It also supplies a five-component lower bound for each numbered cell and harmonic and a second uniform constant for those bounds. The data serve two purposes: covering the harmonics and regions outside the resolved or eliminated modes, and controlling possible negative parts of all densities. They correspond to the coefficient bounds used before Proposition B.4 and in its proof of finiteness of $\mathcal I^-$. Coverage and validity of the supplied bounds are separate conditions.
Breakdown.CertCell.CoefficientEntry.summary: Finitely many pairs of harmonic sets and meridian regions with coefficient bound data and a uniform lower constant, plus five-component lower bounds per cell and harmonic with a second constant, as used for finiteness of $\mathcal I^-$ in Proposition B.4.

Breakdown.CertCell.ContinuumConditionsGi.text:
Let $W^{\mathrm r}$ be the supplied reference field on $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3$, let $H$ be a supplied second-derivative field, and let the weights, periods and harmonic majorants depend on a parameter $\alpha\in\mathcal K$. The formal statement requires the following three sets of bounds and symmetries.

First, there must be real numbers $\mathsf n_\lambda,\mathsf n_{\nabla\lambda},\mathsf n_\mu$, common to all $\alpha\in\mathcal K$, for which the admissibility inequalities hold. At every time and spatial point, each harmonic in the supplied finite reference list has the prescribed majorants for the Euclidean norm of its velocity and curl and the Frobenius norms of its gradient and vorticity gradient. The vorticity gradient is formed from $H$. The two full-field majorants bound the curl norm and the operator norm of the vorticity gradient, uniformly on every circle about the axis; each transport bound similarly dominates $|W^{\mathrm r}(\theta,R_\phi y)+R_\phi y/2-\nu_p\mathbf e_z\times R_\phi y|$ for all $\theta,\phi,y$. For each multiplier piece the rotating-frame frequency has a strictly positive lower bound on its selected harmonic set. The coefficient $\mathsf I'_{2,\iota}$ is nonnegative, $\mathsf n_\mu\ge0$, and all three inequalities (B.19) hold pointwise. These are the numerical admissibility clauses of Appendix B.2; regularity of the weights, positivity of the periods and identification of $H$ with the Hessian of $W^{\mathrm r}$ are separate hypotheses.

Second, the four harmonic majorants are invariant under simultaneous reflection of the harmonic and the point, and the two full-field majorants are invariant under $R_*y=(y_1,-y_2,-y_3)$. These six functions and every transport bound are axisymmetric. The reflection requirement for a harmonic majorant applies to every integer time-angle pair $(n,k)$, with $(n,k)\mapsto(n,-k)$, including pairs outside the supplied finite list. On the paper's lattice $(n,k)=(2\iota_2-\iota_1,\varkappa\iota_1)$ this is $\iota\mapsto\iota^\flat=(-\iota_1,\iota_2-\iota_1)$. This clause imposes no reflection permutation of the transport bounds or rotation rates. Those belong to the separate weight symmetries, which are also needed for the coefficient identity (B.17).

Third, a finite family of regions, each with an assigned set of harmonics, must supply lower bounds for all five coefficients of (B.16), uniformly over $\mathcal K$. The regions cover each point with $r,z>0$ for any harmonic that is unresolved and uneliminated in every cell containing the point. The first four lower coefficients are bounded below by a common real $-M$, and the fifth multiplied by $r^2+z^2$ has the same lower bound. For every resolved or eliminated cell harmonic there are constant lower coefficients on the whole cell with analogous bounds using a second common real $-M'$. Neither $M$ nor $M'$ has a sign requirement. These are hypotheses used to control $\mathcal I^-$ in Proposition B.4. They assert bounds on the entire regions; the statement contains no deduction of these bounds from a finite sample.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.FieldKey.summary: An integer pair ι=(ι₁,ι₂) and an integer l, labelling E_{ι,l}(θ,y)=exp(i[2π(2ι₂−ι₁)θ+κι₁φ+l f(|y|²)]) in (B.5) and (B.6). All three integers may have either sign.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.FieldKey.f.text: For ι=(ι₁,ι₂), this operation replaces ι by ιᶠ=(−ι₁,ι₂−ι₁) and leaves the radial-phase integer l unchanged. Thus the temporal frequency 2ι₂−ι₁ is unchanged while the azimuthal frequency κι₁ changes sign. This is the index transformation defined after (B.2), used for reflection by R*(y₁,y₂,y₃)=(y₁,−y₂,−y₃). The operation alone does not transform the amplitudes or assert invariance of the represented vector field.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.FieldKey.f.summary: Replaces ι by ιᶠ=(−ι₁,ι₂−ι₁) keeping l, so the temporal frequency 2ι₂−ι₁ is unchanged and the azimuthal frequency κι₁ changes sign: the index map after (B.2) for the reflection R*.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.FieldKey.n.text: For an index (ι,l), this operation returns (−ι,−l). With real θ, φ, and radial phase f, its exponential factor in (B.5) is the complex conjugate of the original one. This is the pairing of indices required for the real field (B.6). The operation acts only on the index. Conjugating the spline amplitudes and requiring the paired term to belong to the finite index set are separate conditions.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.FieldKey.n.summary: Returns (−ι,−l), whose exponential factor in (B.5) is the conjugate of the original for real θ, φ and f: the index pairing required for the real field (B.6). It acts on the index only.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.FieldWeakH.text: Let L>0 and κ∈ℕ with κ>0. Let f:ℝ→ℝ be C³ on (−δ,∞) for some δ>0, with |sf′(s)|, |s²f″(s)| and |s³f‴(s)| bounded for s≥0. Let g(σ) be a real polynomial up to 0<σ_g≤1 and a constant afterward, with g(0)=1; when σ_g<1 the values and the first two derivatives join at σ_g. No join beyond σ=1 is required. Take finitely many modes (ι,l)∈ℤ²×ℤ, closed under (ι,l)↦(−ι,−l) and (ι,l)↦(ι^♭,l), where ι^♭=(−ι₁,ι₂−ι₁). Each active complex amplitude is polynomial on a finite rectangular partition of [0,1]×[−1,1]. The joins in (σ,η) have orders (2,1) for A, (1,2) for B, (2,2) for S and (1,1) for T. Here A,B are used when ι₁≠0 and S,T,γ when ι₁=0. In the latter branch S(0,η)=T(0,η)=0. Negated modes have conjugate active data and equal exponents. Reflected nonzero modes have A(σ,−η), −B(σ,−η) and equal exponents; S,T of a zero azimuthal mode are odd in η. All h are natural numbers ≥1, and h₀≥2 in the nonzero branch. For y≠0 put σ=|y|/(|y|+L), η=y₃/|y|, φ=arg(y₁+iy₂), p=ηy/|y|−e₃ and a=e₃×y/|y|. Put V_l=σ(1−σ)∂_σ+2ilρ²f′(ρ²), with ρ=Lσ/(1−σ). If ι₁≠0, set u₀=σ^{h₀}(1−σ)^h(1−η²)²A, u₁=σ^{h₀}(1−σ)^h(1−η²)²B and u₂=i[(V_l+2)u₀−∂_η((1−η²)u₁)]/(κι₁). If ι₁=0, set Ψ=γg(σ)η+S and p₀=σ(1−σ)^h, and put (u₀,u₁,u₂)=(−p₀∂_η((1−η²)Ψ),−(V_l+2)(p₀Ψ),p₀T). Write U_{ι,l}=exp(i[2π(2ι₂−ι₁)θ+κι₁φ+lf(|y|²)])[u₀y/|y|+u₁p+u₂a] and W=Re∑U_{ι,l}. Time θ ranges over ℝ. At the origin all quotients by |y| and the axis angle are assigned zero, so p(0)=−e₃ and the full amplitude factors give U_{ι,l}(θ,0)=0. For every θ and every coordinate direction e_j, the formal statement asserts that y↦H_W(θ,y)(·,e_j) is the weak spatial gradient of y↦∂_jW(θ,y), so a further derivative in a direction h is represented by H_W(θ,y)(h,e_j). Equivalently, for every smooth compactly supported scalar φ and each coordinate direction e_k, ∫∂_jW(θ,y)∂_kφ(y)dy=−∫H_W(θ,y)(e_k,e_j)φ(y)dy, componentwise. The array H_W is the real sum of the second derivatives of the individual harmonics; nonexistent classical derivatives have assigned value zero. The distributional identity is insensitive to such values on sets of measure zero and does not assert global C² regularity. The collected field results prove this assertion.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.FieldWeakH.summary: For a field of the finite vector representation, at each $\theta$ and direction $e_j$, $y\mapsto H_W(\theta,y)(\cdot,e_j)$ is the weak gradient of $\partial_jW(\theta,\cdot)$, where $H_W$ sums the harmonics' second derivatives, missing values set to zero. No global $C^2$ regularity is claimed.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.GivenJetDa.text: These data choose a finite set of representative harmonic indices (ι,l) and give Hermite amplitude data at every index. The complete reference field is obtained by expanding the chosen representatives and adjoining their conjugates and reflections. This is a finite representation implementing the symmetry requirements after (B.8). The declaration itself does not ensure one representative per symmetry orbit or compatibility at an index fixed by an orbit operation; these are explicit later hypotheses.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.GivenJetDa.summary: A finite set of representative indices (ι,l) with Hermite amplitude data; the reference field is obtained by expanding them and adjoining conjugates and reflections, implementing the symmetry requirements after (B.8). One representative per orbit is a later hypothesis.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.GivenJetDa.text: Expand the four Hermite amplitude representations for each chosen index into polynomial splines, close the index set under negation and reflection, and extend amplitudes by those operations. The output is the complete finite harmonic data for the reference field (B.6). This construction records exactly how the representative coefficients determine the field. It does not verify their conjugation or parity consistency, their joining orders, or their radial vanishing; those are conditions on the original Hermite endpoint data.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.GivenJetDa.summary: Expands the Hermite endpoint data of each representative into polynomial splines, closes the index set under negation and reflection, and extends amplitudes accordingly, giving the complete finite harmonic data for (B.6). Consistency conditions are not verified here.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.GivenShape.text: For k forcing fields, these data give common shape parameters and a finite harmonic expansion for the reference profile Wʳ, and, separately for each forcing field bᵢ, its own shape parameters, harmonic expansion, and radial support threshold. This matches the separate reference and forcing representations in Appendix B.1. Lengths, radial phases, and origin corrections may differ between the fields. The data declaration imposes no validity, support, symmetry, or equality with the certificate's actual fields; those are conditions on the data.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.GivenShape.summary: Common shape parameters and a finite harmonic expansion for the reference profile Wʳ, and for each forcing field bᵢ its own parameters, expansion and radial support threshold, matching Appendix B.1. No validity or equality with the certificate's fields is imposed.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.HasEdgeBre.text: For a compactified radial endpoint $\sigma_b$ and a finite harmonic representation of a field, this requires $\sigma_b$ to be a break of both amplitude partitions used by every nonzero-angular harmonic and of both stream and swirl partitions used by every zero-angular harmonic. This makes the proposed support boundary align with every relevant piecewise-polynomial radial mesh. It is a precise requirement for the forcing fields that vanish beyond $\sigma_i$ in Appendix B.1. Membership in a mesh alone asserts no vanishing and no physical radius bound; those are required separately.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.HasEdgeBre.summary: Requires $\sigma_b$ to be a break of every radial partition used by the field's nonzero-angular and zero-angular harmonics, aligning the support boundary of the forcing fields in Appendix B.1 with every radial mesh. It asserts no vanishing.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.HasSymmetr.text: The list of knot scales must have exactly the same length as the knot list and must equal its own reversal. This ensures that reflected endpoint derivatives receive matching scale factors in the parity relations for the Hermite-type representation of Appendix B.1. The condition does not require positive or nonzero scales, and it does not itself require a symmetric or ordered knot list. Those aspects of the geometry and data are separate.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.HasSymmetr.summary: The knot-scale list has the same length as the knot list and equals its own reversal, so reflected endpoint derivatives get matching scales in the parity relations of Appendix B.1. Positive or nonzero scales are not required.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsBoundVal.text: For every α∈𝒦, the certificate's harmonic and full-vorticity bounding functions must equal the evaluation of its supplied bound data. The transport bound of every λ- and μ-piece must likewise equal its fixed represented function in the designated chart. This identifies the functions used in Appendix B.2 with their piecewise polynomial and power representations. It gives exact functional equalities, including the assigned values at the origin and on the equatorial plane. It does not establish that any of these functions actually bounds the reference field or its derivatives.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsBoundVal.summary: For every α∈𝒦, the certificate's harmonic and vorticity bounding functions equal their represented data, and each λ- and μ-piece transport bound equals its represented function: exact identifications for Appendix B.2. Actual dominance is not established.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsCompactT.text:
For a cutoff σ_i<1, this condition requires the B.1 amplitude conditions and that every polynomial piece whose radial interval starts at or beyond σ_i is zero. It also requires a partition edge between σ_i and 1 in each active amplitude, and γ=0 for zero azimuthal modes. This gives compact support, but the cutoff need not itself be an edge in every partition. The theorem giving the precise radius Lσ_i/(1−σ_i) requires that extra edge condition. The paper explicitly takes σ_i to be a partition point. Each forcing field may have its own positive L and admissible phase. The C¹ regularity, divergence and symmetry facts follow from the field theorems once the shape parameters are valid.

The underlying finite-amplitude conditions are these. Take finitely many modes (ι,l)∈ℤ²×ℤ, closed under (ι,l)↦(−ι,−l) and (ι,l)↦(ι^♭,l), where ι^♭=(−ι₁,ι₂−ι₁). Each active complex amplitude is polynomial on a finite rectangular partition of [0,1]×[−1,1]. The joins in (σ,η) have orders (2,1) for A, (1,2) for B, (2,2) for S and (1,1) for T. Here A,B are used when ι₁≠0 and S,T,γ when ι₁=0. In the latter branch S(0,η)=T(0,η)=0. Negated modes have conjugate active data and equal exponents. Reflected nonzero modes have A(σ,−η), −B(σ,−η) and equal exponents; S,T of a zero azimuthal mode are odd in η. All h are natural numbers ≥1, and h₀≥2 in the nonzero branch.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsCompactT.summary: The B.1 amplitude conditions, with every polynomial piece starting at or beyond $\sigma_i<1$ equal to zero, a partition edge between $\sigma_i$ and 1, and $\gamma=0$ in zero modes. This gives compact support; the precise radius needs $\sigma_i$ itself to be an edge, as the paper takes it.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsFullMesh.text: The radial knot list must be strictly increasing from 0 to 1, and the angular knot list strictly increasing from −1 to 1. They partition the variables σ and η of (B.3), as required for the piecewise polynomials in Appendix B.1. The condition includes both endpoints and excludes repeated knots; it thereby gives intervals of positive length. It does not impose a degree bound, matching of neighboring polynomial pieces, or any parity condition. The two lists are finite because they are supplied as finite lists.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsFullMesh.summary: The radial knots strictly increase from 0 to 1 and the angular knots from −1 to 1, partitioning σ and η of (B.3) into intervals of positive length, as required in Appendix B.1. No degree, matching or parity condition is imposed.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsGivenJet.text: The chosen indices must contain at most one distinct member of each orbit under conjugation and reflection. Nonaxisymmetric radial and polar splines require joining classes (2,1) and (1,2), with h₀≥2. Axisymmetric stream and swirl splines require classes (2,2) and (1,1), symmetric angular partitions, odd reflected coefficients, and zero value coefficients at σ=0. Every term has h≥1. At an index fixed by conjugation, the stream and swirl coefficients and γ must be real. At a nonaxisymmetric index fixed by conjugation followed by reflection, the radial and polar data obey the respective even and odd conjugate-reflection coefficient identities on symmetric angular partitions. These are finite-coefficient conditions implementing the reference representation and symmetry requirements of Appendix B.1. Common shape-parameter validity is additional.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsGivenJet.summary: At most one index per orbit under conjugation and reflection, the required joining classes and depths, h₀≥2 and h≥1, odd reflected and zero-origin stream and swirl data, and reality and conjugate-reflection identities at fixed indices, implementing Appendix B.1.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsJetAxis.text: The knot list must be strictly increasing, begin at a prescribed real number a, end at a prescribed real number b, and have derivative depth D≥1. These are the one-variable partition requirements used in the Hermite-type representation of Appendix B.1. No bound is imposed on the number of interior polynomials. The declaration has no explicit condition a<b; when distinct endpoints are used, as for [0,1] and [−1,1], its knot conditions imply positive interval lengths. A one-knot list can occur when a=b.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsJetAxis.summary: The knot list strictly increases from a prescribed a to a prescribed b, with derivative depth D≥1, as in the Hermite representation of Appendix B.1. There is no explicit condition a<b; a one-knot list can occur when a=b.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsJetClass.text: For desired radial and angular joining orders a,b≥0, require a valid radial Hermite partition of [0,1], a valid angular partition of [−1,1], radial depth at least a+1, and angular depth at least b+1. These are exactly the depth conditions described for the reference-profile representation in Appendix B.1. Each depth is a natural number. Because the endpoint derivatives are shared by neighboring intervals, these depths suffice for joins through the requested orders; the declaration does not impose parity, coefficient bounds, or vanishing at σ=0.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsJetClass.summary: For joining orders a,b≥0, requires valid radial and angular Hermite partitions of [0,1] and [−1,1], radial depth at least a+1 and angular depth at least b+1: exactly the depth conditions of Appendix B.1.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsJoinedSp.text: For nonnegative integers a,b, require a full partition of [0,1]×[−1,1], equality of radial derivative traces through order a across each radial knot, and equality of angular derivative traces through order b across each angular knot. Each trace equality holds as a polynomial in the other variable. This is the exact joining convention of Appendix B.1: the choices (2,1), (1,2), (2,2), and (1,1) are used for 𝔄, 𝔅, 𝔖, and 𝔗 respectively. The condition has no assertion about decay or boundary values at σ=0.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsJoinedSp.summary: A full partition of [0,1]×[−1,1] with radial derivative traces equal through order a across radial knots and angular traces through order b across angular knots: the joining convention of Appendix B.1, with (2,1), (1,2), (2,2), (1,1) for 𝔄, 𝔅, 𝔖, 𝔗.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsOriginPr.text: This condition gives g as a real polynomial on σ≤σ_g and as a constant beyond σ_g, with 0<σ_g≤1 and g(0)=1. If σ_g<1, the polynomial and constant agree through the second derivative at σ_g, so g is C² there. If σ_g=1, no derivative matching beyond 1 is required: the physical compactified coordinate is always less than 1. The paper only uses g on [0,1]. This is a description of the data for g, with no assertion about a vector field until g is inserted in Ψ=γg(σ)η+S.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsOriginPr.summary: $g$ is a real polynomial on $\sigma\le\sigma_g$ and constant beyond, with $0<\sigma_g\le1$ and $g(0)=1$; if $\sigma_g<1$ the pieces agree through the second derivative, so $g$ is $C^2$ there. No matching beyond $\sigma=1$ is required.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsRadialPh.text: The radial phase is a function f:ℝ→ℝ. This condition requires a δ>0 such that f is C³ on (−δ,∞), and one real bound B such that |s f′(s)|, |s²f″(s)| and |s³f‴(s)| are all at most B for every s≥0. In the field representation the argument s is |y|², so these are precisely the scaled derivative bounds used for radial differentiation of exp(ilf(|y|²)). The condition makes no claim about f below −δ and requires no boundedness of f itself.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsRadialPh.summary: $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is $C^3$ on $(-\delta,\infty)$ for some $\delta>0$, with one bound $B$ on $|sf'(s)|$, $|s^2f''(s)|$, $|s^3f'''(s)|$ for all $s\ge0$. With $s=|y|^2$ these are the scaled bounds for radially differentiating $\exp(ilf(|y|^2))$; $f$ itself need not be bounded.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsScaledJe.text: The unconverted coefficient arrays must satisfy all representative-data requirements: at most one chosen index in each symmetry orbit, valid Hermite axes of the required depths, h₀≥2 for nonaxisymmetric terms, h≥1 for every term, and the prescribed reality, reflection, and origin-value conditions. In addition, the angular scale lists for axisymmetric stream and swirl data must match the knot-list length and be invariant under reversal. The same scale symmetry is required for radial and polar data at nonaxisymmetric indices fixed by conjugation-reflection. These conditions ensure that conversion preserves the amplitude symmetries of Appendix B.1. They do not require the scales to be positive or nonzero, so invertibility of the representation change is not asserted.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsScaledJe.summary: The unconverted coefficients satisfy all representative-data requirements, and the angular scale lists for stream, swirl and fixed-index radial and polar data match the knot lists and are reversal-invariant, preserving the symmetries of Appendix B.1. Scales may be zero.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsScaledJe.text: Require valid scaled representative data and require their converted, symmetry-completed expansion to equal the reference model. The reference and all forcing fields must have valid shape parameters with the common cell-system azimuthal order; every forcing expansion must satisfy the compact-support amplitude conditions. The supplied reference field must equal its harmonic evaluation, and its Hessian must equal the representative that is zero on the reflected interface set. The supplied reference frequency list must contain all frequencies of the model and be closed under negation. Each certificate forcing field must equal its represented expansion, and its listed labels must equal those of that expansion. These are the exact representation identifications of Appendix B.1, including an explicit choice at Hessian interfaces. No numerical model-error or residual bound is asserted.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsScaledJe.summary: Identifies the reference field and its chosen Hessian with a valid converted harmonic expansion, and the forcing fields with valid compactly supported expansions. The supplied frequency set contains the reference frequencies and is closed under negation, as used in Appendix B.1.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsShapePar.text: Require L>0 and a positive natural-number azimuthal order κ. Require f to be C³ on (−δ,∞) for some δ>0, with sf′, s²f″, and s³f‴ uniformly bounded for s≥0. Require the origin correction g to have 0<σg≤1, g(0)=1, and polynomial-to-constant joins through order two whenever σg<1. These are the chart and phase hypotheses for (B.3)–(B.8). The order restriction is weaker than Appendix B.1's κ≥3: this formal condition permits κ=1 and κ=2. It imposes no conditions on the harmonic amplitudes.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsShapePar.summary: Requires L>0, a positive natural azimuthal order κ, the C³ phase bounds on f, and the origin-correction conditions on g: the hypotheses for (B.3) to (B.8). This permits κ=1 and κ=2, weaker than Appendix B.1's κ≥3.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsSymmetri.text: Reflect every knot x to −x and reverse the resulting list. This condition requires the resulting list to equal the original list exactly. It is the symmetry of the angular partition needed to express the reflection conditions of Appendix B.1 by permuting coefficients. The condition alone neither orders the knots nor fixes the endpoints at ±1; those assertions belong to the validity condition on the one-variable partition. On a valid symmetric partition, reflection exchanges its opposite intervals and endpoints.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsSymmetri.summary: Reflecting every knot x to −x and reversing the list gives the original list exactly: the symmetry of the angular partition needed for the reflection conditions of Appendix B.1. Ordering and endpoints ±1 are separate conditions.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsTimeFiel.text: This condition concerns a finite set of integer modes and their amplitude data; it does not assume a vector field is already given. Take finitely many modes (ι,l)∈ℤ²×ℤ, closed under (ι,l)↦(−ι,−l) and (ι,l)↦(ι^♭,l), where ι^♭=(−ι₁,ι₂−ι₁). Each active complex amplitude is polynomial on a finite rectangular partition of [0,1]×[−1,1]. The joins in (σ,η) have orders (2,1) for A, (1,2) for B, (2,2) for S and (1,1) for T. Here A,B are used when ι₁≠0 and S,T,γ when ι₁=0. In the latter branch S(0,η)=T(0,η)=0. Negated modes have conjugate active data and equal exponents. Reflected nonzero modes have A(σ,−η), −B(σ,−η) and equal exponents; S,T of a zero azimuthal mode are odd in η. All h are natural numbers ≥1, and h₀≥2 in the nonzero branch. The equalities of reflected or conjugate splines mean agreement of the represented functions throughout [0,1]×[−1,1], even when their partitions differ. Unused A,B data in zero modes and unused S,T,γ data in nonzero modes have no restrictions from these active-branch conditions. The positive length, positive κ, radial-phase regularity and the origin function g are separate assumptions. The conclusion of this condition is exactly that this list of data requirements holds; regularity, divergence freedom and decay of the assembled field are separate theorems.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsTimeFiel.summary: Requirements on a finite mode set closed under negation and $\iota\mapsto\iota^\flat$: piecewise polynomial amplitudes with joins of orders $(2,1),(1,2),(2,2),(1,1)$ for $A,B,S,T$, $S(0,\eta)=T(0,\eta)=0$, conjugation and reflection rules, and exponents $h\ge1$, with $h_0\ge2$ in nonzero modes.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetAxis.text: The data are a finite list of real knots, a natural-number derivative depth D, and a natural-number number of interior polynomials per interval. They determine the endpoint derivatives of orders 0,…,D−1 and the additional coefficients in the Hermite-type representation of the reference profile in Appendix B.1. The declaration permits D=0, unordered knots, and empty lists. Positive depth and an ordered partition with specified endpoints are separate hypotheses.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetAxis.summary: A finite list of real knots, a derivative depth D and a number of interior polynomials per interval, determining the endpoint derivatives of orders 0,…,D−1 and interior coefficients of the Hermite representation in Appendix B.1. D=0 and unordered knots are permitted.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetAxis.do.text: Fix an interval number i in a one-variable partition, derivative depth D, and interior count b. An endpoint label (k,p) gives the left endpoint polynomial if k=i, the right endpoint polynomial if k=i+1, and zero otherwise; it is also zero when p≥D. An interior label (i′,s) gives ((x−a)(b′−x))ᴰ(x−(a+b′)/2)ˢ on its own interval i′=i when s<b, and zero otherwise, where a,b′ are that interval's endpoints. This is the local basis construction behind Appendix B.1. Missing endpoints are assigned zero, so valid interval indices and a strictly ordered partition are needed for the interpolation interpretation.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetAxis.do.summary: On interval i, an endpoint label (k,p) gives the left or right endpoint polynomial for k=i or i+1 and p<D, else zero; an interior label (i,s) with s<b gives ((x−a)(b′−x))ᴰ(x−(a+b′)/2)ˢ, the local basis of Appendix B.1.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetAxis.do.text: The sign of an endpoint label of derivative order p is (−1)ᵖ; the sign of an interior label with midpoint-power index s is (−1)ˢ. These are the signs acquired by the corresponding one-variable Hermite polynomials under reflection of the coordinate. They supply the coefficient form of the parity conditions in Appendix B.1. The sign is a real number ±1 regarded as complex, and it does not depend on the knot or interval number. Reflection of the label itself is a separate operation.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetAxis.do.summary: The sign (−1)ᵖ for an endpoint label of derivative order p and (−1)ˢ for an interior label with midpoint power s: the signs of the Hermite polynomials under reflection, giving the coefficient parity conditions of Appendix B.1.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetAxis.do.text: For a partition with N intervals, derivative depth D, and b interior polynomials per interval, the set consists of all endpoint labels (k,p) with 0≤k≤N and 0≤p<D, together with all interior labels (i,s) with 0≤i<N and 0≤s<b. This makes explicit the finite degrees of freedom in the Hermite-type representation of Appendix B.1. N is the knot-list length minus one, truncated at zero. The definition does not require a valid partition; if D or b is zero, the corresponding part of the set is empty.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetAxis.do.summary: For N intervals, depth D and b interior polynomials, all endpoint labels (k,p) with 0≤k≤N, 0≤p<D and interior labels (i,s) with 0≤i<N, 0≤s<b: the finite degrees of freedom in Appendix B.1.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetAxis.re.text: For a partition with N intervals, the reflected endpoint label is (N−k,p), and the reflected interior label is (N−1−i,s). This reverses interval order while preserving derivative order or interior-polynomial index, as used for reflection in Appendix B.1. It has the expected geometric meaning for valid labels on a symmetric partition. The formula is defined for every natural-number label by truncating negative differences at zero; therefore it is not an involution on arbitrary out-of-range labels. The derivative or parity sign is assigned separately.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetAxis.re.summary: For N intervals, sends endpoint (k,p) to (N−k,p) and interior (i,s) to (N−1−i,s), reversing interval order as used for reflection in Appendix B.1. Negative differences are truncated at zero, so it is not an involution on out-of-range labels.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetDof.text: A one-variable coefficient is labelled either by a knot number k and derivative order p, or by an interval number i and an interior-polynomial index s. These are the endpoint derivative data and additional interior coefficients of the Hermite-type representation described for the reference profile in Appendix B.1. All indices are natural numbers. The bare labels have no range restrictions; a specified partition, derivative depth, and number of interior polynomials determine which labels are actually used.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetDof.summary: A one-variable coefficient label: either a knot number k with derivative order p, or an interval number i with interior index s, all natural numbers, for the Hermite representation of the reference profile in Appendix B.1.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetKeyData.text: The data for one (ι,l) are four tensor-product Hermite representations for 𝔄, 𝔅, 𝔖, and 𝔗, a complex coefficient γ, and natural radial exponents h₀,h. Expanding the coefficients gives the splines in (B.7) and (B.8). This is the form used for the reference profile in Appendix B.1. It stores both nonaxisymmetric and axisymmetric possibilities; only the appropriate pair of splines is used for a given ι₁. The declaration imposes no depth, origin, decay, or symmetry conditions.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetKeyData.summary: For one (ι,l), four tensor Hermite representations for 𝔄, 𝔅, 𝔖, 𝔗, a complex coefficient γ and natural exponents h₀,h; expanding them gives the splines in (B.7) and (B.8). No depth, origin, decay or symmetry condition is imposed.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.compactFie.text:

Assume additionally that σ_i itself occurs in every active radial partition. The theorem proves that the represented field vanishes for every real θ at all points with |y|>Lσ_i/(1−σ_i). The displayed conclusion uses a strict inequality. The paper states vanishing also at the boundary; the field's continuity supplies that endpoint once the radius is nonnegative. Without the additional partition-edge hypothesis the precise radius does not follow from the compact-data condition alone.

The finite vector representation and its hypotheses in this statement are as follows. Let L>0 and κ∈ℕ with κ>0. Let f:ℝ→ℝ be C³ on (−δ,∞) for some δ>0, with |sf′(s)|, |s²f″(s)| and |s³f‴(s)| bounded for s≥0. Let g(σ) be a real polynomial up to 0<σ_g≤1 and a constant afterward, with g(0)=1; when σ_g<1 the values and the first two derivatives join at σ_g. No join beyond σ=1 is required. Take finitely many modes (ι,l)∈ℤ²×ℤ, closed under (ι,l)↦(−ι,−l) and (ι,l)↦(ι^♭,l), where ι^♭=(−ι₁,ι₂−ι₁). Each active complex amplitude is polynomial on a finite rectangular partition of [0,1]×[−1,1]. The joins in (σ,η) have orders (2,1) for A, (1,2) for B, (2,2) for S and (1,1) for T. Here A,B are used when ι₁≠0 and S,T,γ when ι₁=0. In the latter branch S(0,η)=T(0,η)=0. Negated modes have conjugate active data and equal exponents. Reflected nonzero modes have A(σ,−η), −B(σ,−η) and equal exponents; S,T of a zero azimuthal mode are odd in η. All h are natural numbers ≥1, and h₀≥2 in the nonzero branch. For y≠0 put σ=|y|/(|y|+L), η=y₃/|y|, φ=arg(y₁+iy₂), p=ηy/|y|−e₃ and a=e₃×y/|y|. Put V_l=σ(1−σ)∂_σ+2ilρ²f′(ρ²), with ρ=Lσ/(1−σ). If ι₁≠0, set u₀=σ^{h₀}(1−σ)^h(1−η²)²A, u₁=σ^{h₀}(1−σ)^h(1−η²)²B and u₂=i[(V_l+2)u₀−∂_η((1−η²)u₁)]/(κι₁). If ι₁=0, set Ψ=γg(σ)η+S and p₀=σ(1−σ)^h, and put (u₀,u₁,u₂)=(−p₀∂_η((1−η²)Ψ),−(V_l+2)(p₀Ψ),p₀T). Write U_{ι,l}=exp(i[2π(2ι₂−ι₁)θ+κι₁φ+lf(|y|²)])[u₀y/|y|+u₁p+u₂a] and W=Re∑U_{ι,l}. Time θ ranges over ℝ. At the origin all quotients by |y| and the axis angle are assigned zero, so p(0)=−e₃ and the full amplitude factors give U_{ι,l}(θ,0)=0.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.compactFie.summary: For valid $L,\kappa>0$ and compact data with cutoff $\sigma_i<1$ in every active radial partition, the field vanishes for all $\theta$ when $|y|>L\sigma_i/(1-\sigma_i)$. The paper's boundary case follows by continuity; without the edge hypothesis the radius does not follow.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.complexFie.text: At a real time θ and spatial point y, sum the complex vector terms E_{ι,l}[u₀ y/|y|+u₁p+u₂a] over the supplied finite index set 𝒜. Finiteness makes the sum algebraically defined without a convergence hypothesis. Conjugate-pair conditions are needed to identify it as real before taking real parts, and regularity is established separately.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.complexFie.summary: At (θ,y), the sum over 𝒜 of E_{ι,l}[u₀ y/|y|+u₁p+u₂a] with each term's amplitudes and shared length, order, phase and origin correction: the complex sum whose real part is (B.6). Finiteness avoids convergence hypotheses.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.fieldClass.text: Let L>0 and κ∈ℕ with κ>0. Let f:ℝ→ℝ be C³ on (−δ,∞) for some δ>0, with |sf′(s)|, |s²f″(s)| and |s³f‴(s)| bounded for s≥0. Let g(σ) be a real polynomial up to 0<σ_g≤1 and a constant afterward, with g(0)=1; when σ_g<1 the values and the first two derivatives join at σ_g. No join beyond σ=1 is required. Take finitely many modes (ι,l)∈ℤ²×ℤ, closed under (ι,l)↦(−ι,−l) and (ι,l)↦(ι^♭,l), where ι^♭=(−ι₁,ι₂−ι₁). Each active complex amplitude is polynomial on a finite rectangular partition of [0,1]×[−1,1]. The joins in (σ,η) have orders (2,1) for A, (1,2) for B, (2,2) for S and (1,1) for T. Here A,B are used when ι₁≠0 and S,T,γ when ι₁=0. In the latter branch S(0,η)=T(0,η)=0. Negated modes have conjugate active data and equal exponents. Reflected nonzero modes have A(σ,−η), −B(σ,−η) and equal exponents; S,T of a zero azimuthal mode are odd in η. All h are natural numbers ≥1, and h₀≥2 in the nonzero branch. For y≠0 put σ=|y|/(|y|+L), η=y₃/|y|, φ=arg(y₁+iy₂), p=ηy/|y|−e₃ and a=e₃×y/|y|. Put V_l=σ(1−σ)∂_σ+2ilρ²f′(ρ²), with ρ=Lσ/(1−σ). If ι₁≠0, set u₀=σ^{h₀}(1−σ)^h(1−η²)²A, u₁=σ^{h₀}(1−σ)^h(1−η²)²B and u₂=i[(V_l+2)u₀−∂_η((1−η²)u₁)]/(κι₁). If ι₁=0, set Ψ=γg(σ)η+S and p₀=σ(1−σ)^h, and put (u₀,u₁,u₂)=(−p₀∂_η((1−η²)Ψ),−(V_l+2)(p₀Ψ),p₀T). Write U_{ι,l}=exp(i[2π(2ι₂−ι₁)θ+κι₁φ+lf(|y|²)])[u₀y/|y|+u₁p+u₂a] and W=Re∑U_{ι,l}. Time θ ranges over ℝ. At the origin all quotients by |y| and the axis angle are assigned zero, so p(0)=−e₃ and the full amplitude factors give U_{ι,l}(θ,0)=0. For every real θ,y, the theorem proves W(θ,R_*y)=R_*W(θ,y), W(θ+1/2,R_{π/κ}y)=R_{π/κ}W(θ,y), and W(θ,R_{2π/κ}y)=R_{2π/κ}W(θ,y). Here R_*y=(y₁,−y₂,−y₃) and R_φ rotates about the y₃ axis. These are exactly the two generator symmetries and their full-turn consequence. Invariance under an arbitrary prescribed Γ additionally requires that each of its elements is composed of these symmetries and an integer time translation.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.fieldClass.summary: For a field of the finite vector representation, $W(\theta,R_*y)=R_*W(\theta,y)$, $W(\theta+1/2,R_{\pi/\kappa}y)=R_{\pi/\kappa}W(\theta,y)$ and $W(\theta,R_{2\pi/\kappa}y)=R_{2\pi/\kappa}W(\theta,y)$ for real $\theta,y$. A general $\Gamma$ needs elements built from these and integer time shifts.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.harmonicsO.text: For the finite index set 𝒜 and natural symmetry order κ, collect the integer pairs (2ι₂−ι₁, κι₁) for all (ι,l)∈𝒜. These are the temporal and azimuthal frequencies of (B.2); the radial-phase index l does not change either frequency. Repeated pairs are included only once. This gives a containing frequency set for the field representation. It may contain frequencies whose amplitudes vanish or cancel, so it does not assert that every listed frequency actually occurs.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.harmonicsO.summary: For the index set 𝒜 and order κ, the set of pairs (2ι₂−ι₁, κι₁) over (ι,l)∈𝒜: the temporal and azimuthal frequencies of (B.2). It may include frequencies whose amplitudes vanish or cancel.

For p<D, its derivatives of orders below D at x=0 equal one at order p and zero at every other order, and they all vanish at x=1. This gives the endpoint-derivative basis used in the Hermite-type representation of Appendix B.1. The formula itself accepts p≥D; then the sum is empty and the polynomial is zero. Natural-number differences are truncated at zero, and p! is always nonzero.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.jetUnit.summary: H_{D,p}(x)=xᵖ(1−x)ᴰ/p! times ∑_{s=0}^{D−p−1} binom(D−1+s,s)xˢ. For p<D its derivatives below order D are one at order p and zero otherwise at 0, and vanish at 1: the endpoint basis of Appendix B.1. For p≥D it is zero.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.keyHess.text: For the complex vector field given by one term of (B.6), this is its second spatial derivative at fixed θ, represented as a real bilinear map ℝ³×ℝ³→ℂ³. The formal expression differentiates the first derivative as an everywhere-defined function. Where either derivative does not exist, the derivative operation uses its default zero value. This is a set containing every spline interface potentially relevant to that term of (B.6). It includes even the two spline types not used by the term's axisymmetric or nonaxisymmetric branch, so it can be larger than the true set of derivative discontinuities. This enlargement is used to choose second-derivative representatives in Appendix B.1; it is not a claim that the field is singular throughout the set.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.keyKnots.summary: The union of radial-knot spheres and angular-knot cones from all four splines 𝔄,𝔅,𝔖,𝔗 of one harmonic, containing every potentially relevant interface of that term of (B.6). It can be larger than the true discontinuity set.

Since κι₁ is integral, changing the angular representative by 2π does not change it. The assigned angle on the axis alone supplies no continuity there; the corresponding vector amplitude has the axis factors required in (B.7) or (B.8).
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.keyPhase.summary: $\exp(i[2\pi(2\iota_2-\iota_1)\theta+\kappa\iota_1\phi(y)+lf(|y|^2)])$, with $\phi$ the principal argument of $y_1+iy_2$, set to zero on the axis. Off the axis it is $E_\iota(\theta,\phi)e^{ilf(|y|^2)}$; the axis value gives no continuity, which comes from the amplitude's axis factors.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.keyVector.summary: A term E_{ι,l}(θ,y)[u₀ y/|y|+u₁p+u₂a] of (B.6), with p and a the polar and azimuthal frames and amplitudes from (B.7) or (B.8) at σ=|y|/(|y|+L), η=y₃/|y|. It is the same expression as the paper; regularity needs further hypotheses.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.knotZeroHe.text: For the field represented by (B.6), use the sum of harmonic second derivatives away from the reflected union of the axis, equatorial plane, origin, origin-correction sphere, and all spline-knot spheres and cones. Assign the zero bilinear map on that union. This is an explicit choice of the second-derivative representative described in Appendix B.1. It changes only the Hessian data at the exceptional set, not the velocity. Agreement with the weak Hessian requires the valid data and null-set argument; the definition itself is not a differentiability or weak-derivative theorem.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.knotZeroHe.summary: The sum of harmonic second derivatives away from the reflected union of axis, equatorial plane, origin, origin-correction sphere and spline-knot spheres and cones, and zero on that union: an explicit Hessian representative for (B.6), as described in Appendix B.1.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.labelsOf.text: Project the finite set of harmonic indices (ι,l) onto its integer pair ι=(ι₁,ι₂), discarding the radial-phase index l and duplicates. These are the labels used in (B.2) and in the mode restrictions of Appendix B.2. The operation records all labels supplied by the representation, including those with zero amplitudes. It imposes no conjugation, reflection, or range condition on that finite set.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.labelsOf.summary: Projects the finite set of indices (ι,l) onto the pairs ι=(ι₁,ι₂), discarding l and duplicates: the labels used in (B.2) and Appendix B.2, including those with zero amplitude.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.logPhaseIs.text: Let $a\in\mathbb R$ and $r_c>0$, and set $f(\rho)=\tfrac a2\log(1+\rho/r_c^2)$. In the represented field the scalar argument is $\rho=|y|^2$; the derivatives below are with respect to $\rho$. The formal statement proves that $f$ is $C^3$ on $(-\delta,\infty)$ for some $\delta>0$ and that there is a finite $B$ with $|\rho f'(\rho)|\leq B$, $|\rho^2 f''(\rho)|\leq B$, and $|\rho^3 f^{(3)}(\rho)|\leq B$ for every $\rho\geq0$. The proof takes $\delta=r_c^2$ and $B=|a|$. Thus the logarithmic phase in Appendix C meets these analytic conditions when $a=4\pi/\bar S$ and $\bar S>0$. The formal coefficient is $a/2$, so setting $a=2\pi/\bar S$ would give half the printed phase. The formal function is defined for all real arguments; the assertion uses only the interval where the logarithm has positive argument. It does not identify a numerical value of $r_c$, a computed period, or a particular certificate.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.logPhaseIs.summary: For $a\in\mathbb R$, $r_c>0$, $f(\rho)=\tfrac a2\log(1+\rho/r_c^2)$ is $C^3$ on $(-\delta,\infty)$ with $|\rho f'|,|\rho^2f''|,|\rho^3f'''|\le B$ for $\rho\ge0$ ($\delta=r_c^2$, $B=|a|$). The Appendix C phase needs $a=4\pi/\bar S$; $a=2\pi/\bar S$ gives half the printed phase.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.mirrorKnot.text: Take the exceptional meridian set containing the axis, equatorial plane, origin, origin-correction sphere, and all harmonic spline interfaces, and adjoin its image under (r,z)↦(r,−z). This is the set used to assign a reflection-compatible representative of the Hessian for the field (B.6). It may contain interfaces of unused amplitude splines and points where the field is smooth. The declaration defines a set only; its measure-zero property and the weak-derivative interpretation require the valid finite representation.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.mirrorKnot.summary: The exceptional meridian set (axis, equatorial plane, origin, origin-correction sphere, all spline interfaces) together with its image under (r,z)↦(r,−z), used to choose a reflection-compatible Hessian representative for (B.6).

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.nodalLeft.text: For real endpoints a,b and natural numbers D,p, the polynomial is (b−a)ᵖH_{D,p}((x−a)/(b−a)), where H_{D,p}(u)=uᵖ(1−u)ᴰ/p! times ∑_{s<D−p}binom(D−1+s,s)uˢ. If a<b and p<D, the derivatives through order D−1 at a select derivative p with value one, and those at b vanish. This is the left endpoint factor of the Hermite-type representation in Appendix B.1. The formula imposes no a<b hypothesis; at a=b the inverse length is defined as zero and the interpolation interpretation does not follow.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.nodalLeft.summary: The polynomial (b−a)ᵖH_{D,p}((x−a)/(b−a)). If a<b and p<D, its derivatives through order D−1 at a select order p with value one and those at b vanish: the left endpoint factor in Appendix B.1. At a=b the inverse length is taken as zero.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.nodalRight.text: For real a,b and natural D,p, use (a−b)ᵖH_{D,p}((b−x)/(b−a)), with H_{D,p}(u)=uᵖ(1−u)ᴰ/p! times ∑_{s<D−p}binom(D−1+s,s)uˢ. When a<b and p<D, the derivatives through order D−1 vanish at a and select derivative p with value one at b. The sign (a−b)ᵖ cancels the orientation change in differentiation. This is the right endpoint factor in Appendix B.1's Hermite representation. The definition allows degenerate intervals; division by zero then has value zero, so the stated interpolation properties require a<b.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.nodalRight.summary: The polynomial (a−b)ᵖH_{D,p}((b−x)/(b−a)). If a<b and p<D, its derivatives through order D−1 vanish at a and select order p with value one at b: the right endpoint factor in Appendix B.1. Division by zero is zero for degenerate intervals.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.orbitClosu.text: From a finite set of indices (ι,l), form its union with the images under simultaneous negation, reflection ι↦ιᶠ=(−ι₁,ι₂−ι₁), and their composition. Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.orbitClosu.summary: The union of a finite index set with its images under negation, reflection ι↦ιᶠ=(−ι₁,ι₂−ι₁) and their composition: the index set closed under the two operations after (B.8). Compatible amplitudes are not supplied.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.phaseSlope.text: For ρ=Lσ/(1−σ), define a(σ)=2ρ²f′(ρ²). This is the real factor multiplying il in the radial phase contribution to 𝒱l in (B.5). The formula is defined on the entire plane, including the origin, and includes no assumption r≥0.

This is the factor appearing in (B.4), (B.7), and (B.8), and it vanishes at the two axis directions η=±1. The formula is defined for every real η and is nonnegative only on [−1,1].
