These are definitions; h₀≥2 for nonzero azimuthal modes, h≥1, the spline joins and the admissibility of L,f,g are separate hypotheses. The nonzero branch divides by κι₁, which is nonzero under κ>0 and ι₁≠0. The exponents are natural numbers, matching the paper's nonnegative integer exponents.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.reducedCom.summary: For $\iota_1\ne0$, $u_0,u_1$ are $\sigma^{h_0}(1-\sigma)^h(1-\eta^2)^2$ times $A,B$ and $u_2=i[(V_l+2)u_0-\partial_\eta((1-\eta^2)u_1)]/(\kappa\iota_1)$; for $\iota_1=0$, $u_0,u_1$ come from $\Psi=\gamma g(\sigma)\eta+S$ and $u_2=\sigma(1-\sigma)^hT$. Joins and exponent bounds are separate.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.reflectPol.text: For a complex polynomial P(σ,η), this operation gives P(σ,−η), leaving σ unchanged. It implements the angular reflection used in the amplitude relations of Appendix B.1. The coefficients are unchanged and are not complex-conjugated. There are no regularity hypotheses because the object is a polynomial; any parity statement such as evenness or oddness requires a subsequent equality with this reflected polynomial.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.reflectPol.summary: For a complex polynomial $P(\sigma,\eta)$, the polynomial $P(\sigma,-\eta)$, the angular reflection used in the amplitude relations of Appendix B.1. Coefficients are not complex-conjugated; evenness or oddness needs a further equality with the reflected polynomial.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.reflectSpl.text: Reflect every angular knot by η↦−η, reverse their order, and replace the polynomial in a cell by P(σ,−η) from the reflected cell. An additional chosen sign is +1 for an even reflection and −1 for an odd reflection. This is the spline representation of the amplitude symmetries in Appendix B.1. The radial partition is unchanged. The formula is defined even for invalid partitions and out-of-range natural indices, where subtraction is truncated at zero; the geometric interpretation uses valid cells of a full ordered mesh.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.reflectSpl.summary: Reflects a spline by $\eta\mapsto-\eta$ on its angular knots, reversing their order and using $P(\sigma,-\eta)$ from the reflected cell, times a sign $+1$ (even) or $-1$ (odd); the radial partition is unchanged. This represents the amplitude symmetries of Appendix B.1.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shapeHess.text: At fixed θ and y, sum the real parts of the second spatial derivatives of the individual complex harmonic terms in (B.6). The result is a real bilinear map on two spatial directions. At points where all relevant derivatives exist, finite-sum differentiation identifies this with the Hessian of the represented real field. At a spline interface the formula retains the everywhere-defined derivative convention, which uses zero when a derivative fails to exist. Appendix B.1 uses bounded second derivatives agreeing with the classical ones away from the partition spheres and cones; the identification with that weak derivative requires the additional construction and hypotheses.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shapeHess.summary: At fixed $\theta,y$, the sum of real parts of the second spatial derivatives of the complex harmonic terms in (B.6), a real bilinear map. Where a derivative fails to exist it is taken as zero; identifying it with the weak Hessian of Appendix B.1 needs further hypotheses.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shapeInfoF.text: For real θ and y∈ℝ³ this defines the real part of a finite sum E_ι(θ,φ(y))e^{ilf(|y|²)}[u₀y/|y|+u₁p+u₂a], indexed by (ι,l) in a finite subset of ℤ²×ℤ. The three amplitudes are those of (B.7) and (B.8), evaluated at σ=|y|/(|y|+L), η=y₃/|y|. The vectors p and a are the weighted spherical-coordinate vectors in (B.4). The real part is taken componentwise. All expressions have assigned values everywhere: quotients by zero are zero and the angle is zero on the axis. With the prescribed positive exponents the complete vector equals zero at the origin. This definition alone imposes no spline joins, symmetry, divergence condition or decay bound; the data conditions and theorems provide those assertions.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shapeInfoF.summary: The real part of a finite sum $E_\iota(\theta,\phi(y))e^{ilf(|y|^2)}[u_0y/|y|+u_1p+u_2a]$ over $(\iota,l)$, with amplitudes from (B.7) and (B.8) at $\sigma=|y|/(|y|+L)$, $\eta=y_3/|y|$. Quotients by zero and the axis angle are zero; no joins, symmetry, divergence or decay are imposed.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shapeKnots.text: In the signed meridian plane, include z=0, r=0, the origin, the circle of radius Lσ_g/(1−σ_g) associated with the origin correction, and all radial-knot circles and angular-knot cones from all four amplitude splines at every index of the finite expansion. This explicitly enlarges the interfaces described in Appendix B.1. For valid chart parameters, a C³ radial phase and valid amplitudes, classical second derivatives of (B.6) can be computed from the polynomial pieces away from this set. The set definition itself requires none of these regularity hypotheses. Membership records a possible interface and does not assert a loss of differentiability.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shapeKnots.summary: The signed meridian set containing z=0, r=0, the origin, the origin-correction sphere and all amplitude spline interfaces. For valid parameters and amplitudes, the second derivatives of (B.6) can be computed off this set; the definition itself assumes no regularity.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shiftedSca.text: For an integer l, a complex amplitude u(σ,η), a radial phase f, and length L, the defined expression is σ(1−σ)∂_σu+il·2ρ²f′(ρ²)u, where ρ=Lσ/(1−σ). For L>0 and 0≤σ<1, ρ is the physical radius and this is the operator V_l in (B.5). The formula accepts all real σ and uses zero for division by zero; in particular its value at σ=1 uses a default ρ=0 and is not an evaluation at spatial infinity. Derivatives are ordinary derivatives where they exist; the spline and phase conditions ensure the needed differentiability on the physical coordinate range.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shiftedSca.summary: $\sigma(1-\sigma)\partial_\sigma u+il\cdot2\rho^2f'(\rho^2)u$ with $\rho=L\sigma/(1-\sigma)$, the operator $V_l$ of (B.5) when $L>0$ and $0\le\sigma<1$. Division by zero is zero, so the value at $\sigma=1$ uses $\rho=0$ and is not an evaluation at spatial infinity.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.sphereKnot.text: For every supplied radial knot b, include the meridian points satisfying √(r²+z²)=Lb/(1−b). These are the circles whose rotations give the partition spheres described in Appendix B.1. Under L>0 and 0≤b<1 the radius is the inverse chart coordinate in (B.3). The full knot list includes b=1, where the formal quotient is zero and therefore contributes only the origin, not a sphere at infinity. No valid-mesh or positive-length hypothesis is part of this set definition.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.sphereKnot.summary: The union, over supplied radial knots b, of the circles √(r²+z²)=Lb/(1−b), whose rotations give the partition spheres of Appendix B.1. At b=1 the quotient is zero, so only the origin is added; no mesh-validity hypothesis is included.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.splineKnot.text: Take the union of the sets √(r²+z²)=Lb/(1−b) for radial knots b and z=b√(r²+z²) for angular knots b. This is the meridian description of all possible spatial interfaces of one spline in Appendix B.1. It uses the entire knot lists, including endpoints, so it may contain points where the polynomial pieces are actually smooth across the interface. At radial knot one the radius is assigned zero; no physical infinity is included.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.splineKnot.summary: The union of the sets $\sqrt{r^2+z^2}=Lb/(1-b)$ over radial knots and $z=b\sqrt{r^2+z^2}$ over angular knots, the possible interfaces of one spline in Appendix B.1, using the full knot lists. At radial knot one the radius is assigned zero; no infinity is included.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.streamValu.text: For a harmonic's complex coefficient γ, stream spline 𝔖, and origin correction g, define Ψ(σ,η)=γg(σ)η+𝔖(σ,η). This is exactly the stream function in (B.8). The formula has no joining, parity, or normalization hypothesis. The field construction subsequently requires g(0)=1, the prescribed C² behavior of g, oddness of 𝔖 in η, the radial and angular joins of 𝔖, and 𝔖(0,η)=0. The complex-valued Ψ becomes part of a real field after harmonic summation and taking real parts.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.streamValu.summary: The stream function $\Psi(\sigma,\eta)=\gamma g(\sigma)\eta+\mathfrak S(\sigma,\eta)$, exactly as in (B.8), with no joining, parity or normalization hypothesis. The field construction later needs $g(0)=1$, the $C^2$ behaviour of $g$, oddness and joins of $\mathfrak S$, and $\mathfrak S(0,\eta)=0$.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.symmetricJ.text: For natural numbers α,j, the polynomial is 2⁻ʲ∑_{i=0}^j binom(j+α,i)binom(j+α,j−i)(x−1)^{j−i}(x+1)ⁱ. This is the usual symmetric Jacobi polynomial P_j^(α,α), used here to express the additional interior coefficients in the Hermite-type reference representation of Appendix B.1. The normalization gives P_j^(α,α)(1)=binom(j+α,j). Both parameters are natural numbers in this formal definition. It defines a polynomial and does not assert a norm or orthogonality estimate.
Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.symmetricJ.summary: For natural $\alpha,j$, the polynomial $2^{-j}\sum_{i=0}^j\binom{j+\alpha}{i}\binom{j+\alpha}{j-i}(x-1)^{j-i}(x+1)^i$, the symmetric Jacobi polynomial $P_j^{(\alpha,\alpha)}$ with $P_j^{(\alpha,\alpha)}(1)=\binom{j+\alpha}{j}$, used for interior coefficients in Appendix B.1.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.ActuatorShap.text: The field b(θ,y) must be measurable, one-periodic, uniformly bounded, and supported in a fixed spatial ball. Both b and its spatial derivative have finite squared integrals on [0,1]×ℝ³; the derivative is measurable, one-periodic, and is the weak spatial gradient at every θ. Away from the axis, every nonzero Fourier mode lies among a prescribed finite set or its negatives. The two symmetries in (B.1) hold almost everywhere. These are selected analytic consequences of the forcing representation in Appendix B.1. This condition alone is weaker than the paper's full assertion that b is C¹ and divergence-free: neither of those assertions is included here.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.ActuatorShap.summary: The forcing $b(\theta,y)$ is measurable, one-periodic, bounded and supported in a fixed ball, with $b$ and its weak spatial gradient square-integrable, finitely many Fourier modes off the axis, and the (B.1) symmetries a.e. This is weaker than the paper: $C^1$ and divergence-free are not included.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.ChartScalar.text: These data consist of an upper-half and a lower-half piecewise complex polynomial, together with a natural decay exponent h. The intended scalar field uses their real parts at (σ,|η|), multiplied by (1−σ)^h, where σ=|y|/(|y|+L) and η=y₃/|y|. This is the scalar-weight representation in Appendix B.2. The two polynomials may have separate meshes; no joining, positivity, smoothness or decay lower bound is required by the declaration, and h=0 is allowed.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.ChartScalar.summary: Data for the scalar weights of Appendix B.2: upper and lower piecewise complex polynomials and a natural decay exponent $h$, giving the real parts at $(\sigma,|\eta|)$ times $(1-\sigma)^h$. Separate meshes are allowed, and no joining, positivity or smoothness is required; $h=0$ is allowed.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.ChartScalar..text: Given a chart length L, natural decay exponent h and two half-chart polynomials P₊,P₋, this is (1−σ)^h Re P₊(σ,η) for y₃≥0 and (1−σ)^h Re P₋(σ,−η) for y₃<0, with σ=|y|/(|y|+L) and η=y₃/|y|. It is the spatial scalar representation used for weights in Appendix B.2. At y₃=0 the upper branch is chosen; at y=0 both ratios are zero for every real L. Whenever |y|+L=0, division by zero assigns σ=0. The half-chart pieces are evaluated with the right-hand piece at an internal knot and with polynomial extrapolation outside their partition. The exponent is natural, with h=0 permitted. The definition imposes neither L>0 nor matching across z=0 or spline interfaces, so smoothness and positivity are separate conditions.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.ChartScalar..summary: $(1-\sigma)^h\mathrm{Re}\,P_+(\sigma,\eta)$ for $y_3\ge0$ and $(1-\sigma)^h\mathrm{Re}\,P_-(\sigma,-\eta)$ for $y_3<0$, $\sigma=|y|/(|y|+L)$, $\eta=y_3/|y|$; zero denominators give zero, so both ratios vanish at $y=0$ for every real $L$. $L>0$ and matching are not imposed.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.ChartScalar..text: This swaps the upper and lower piecewise-polynomial data of a scalar chart field and keeps its natural decay exponent. Away from y₃=0, evaluation corresponds to reflecting height, as in the scalar-weight symmetry of Appendix B.2. On y₃=0 both evaluations choose the upper branch, so equality with the reflected original field there additionally requires the two polynomial traces to match. The operation alone asserts no such matching or regularity.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.ChartScalar..summary: Swaps the upper and lower polynomial data of a scalar chart field, keeping the decay exponent; away from $y_3=0$ this reflects height, as in Appendix B.2. On $y_3=0$ both choose the upper branch, so equality with the reflected field there also needs matching traces.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.EpsGiven.text: One curl multiplier piece consists of a set of integer time-angle frequencies, a scalar spline representing λ, and eight piecewise constant auxiliary factors: two shares of derivative energy, a length factor, four balancing factors, and a scale factor. The spatial factors include their own integer decay powers. These are the finitely represented inputs for one p∈𝒫λ in Appendix B.2. This declaration supplies the data only. Disjointness from the negative frequency set, positivity, joining conditions, a rotation rate, and a transport bound are imposed or supplied elsewhere.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.EpsGiven.summary: The data of one $p\in\mathcal P_\lambda$ in Appendix B.2: a set of integer time-angle frequencies, a scalar spline for $\lambda$, and eight piecewise constant auxiliary factors with integer decay powers. Disjointness, positivity, joins, the rate and the transport bound are imposed elsewhere.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.EpsGiven.mir.text: For a curl multiplier piece, replace each raw Fourier pair (n,k) by (n,−k), interchange the upper and lower spline factors, and interchange the two halves of each of the eight auxiliary functions. This corresponds to the paper's label reflection ι↦(−ι₁,ι₂−ι₁) after converting labels to raw Fourier pairs, and implements the λ-data symmetry in (B.17). It preserves all radial decay exponents. The rotation rate is not among these data and is not changed here; the requirement that the reflected rate be its negative is imposed separately. On the equatorial plane, equality of evaluations also uses the appropriate joining conditions.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.EpsGiven.mir.summary: Sends raw Fourier pairs $(n,k)\mapsto(n,-k)$ and swaps upper and lower halves of the spline and eight auxiliary factors, matching the label reflection $\iota\mapsto(-\iota_1,\iota_2-\iota_1)$ and the $\lambda$-symmetry in (B.17). Decay exponents are kept; the rate condition is imposed separately.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.GeneratedByC.text: Fix a natural number κ, the azimuthal order of the cell data. The condition says that every (R,τ)∈Γ has R=R_{aπ/κ}R_*^b and τ=a/2+j for some natural number a, b∈{0,1}, and integer j. Thus the angle is a nonnegative integer multiple of π/κ and τ−κ(aπ/κ)/(2π) is integral when κ>0. This restricts the elements already in Γ; it does not assert that every such pair belongs to Γ or that the two generators belong to Γ. Positivity of κ and inclusion of the generators are separate assumptions. Under these assumptions, invariance under the generators and time period 1 imply invariance under Γ.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.GeneratedByC.summary: Every $(R,\tau)\in\Gamma$ has $R=R_{a\pi/\kappa}R_*^b$ and $\tau=a/2+j$ for natural $a$, $b\in\{0,1\}$ and integer $j$. It restricts the elements of $\Gamma$ without placing the generators in it; with them and period 1, generator invariance implies $\Gamma$-invariance.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.HasNonnegVal.text: At every (σ,x)∈[0,1]², the real parts of both the upper and lower spline values must be nonnegative. The two splines are the factors evaluated at x=|η| in the scalar weights of Appendix B.2. The formal condition agrees with the stated sign requirement for those factors; it leaves their imaginary parts unrestricted. The additional factor (1−σ)ᵈ is nonnegative on this square when d is the natural-number decay exponent used for these weights. Continuity, valid partitions, and the identification with a weight on ℝ³ are separate conditions.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.HasNonnegVal.summary: At every $(\sigma,x)\in[0,1]^2$ the real parts of the upper and lower spline values are nonnegative, the sign requirement for the factors evaluated at $x=|\eta|$ in the scalar weights of Appendix B.2. Imaginary parts are unrestricted.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.InstanceData.text: The inputs are finite representations of the multiplier weights; parameter-dependent rotation rates; fixed spatial transport bounds; permutations implementing reflection for the λ- and μ-pieces; a proposed upper bound for the row weights; finite lists of forcing labels; and a natural-number forcing cutoff. These are the data needed to connect the analytic fields to the explicit representations of Appendix B.1 and B.2. Their types allow arbitrary real bounds and arbitrary functions of the parameter. This declaration supplies no positivity, mode separation, reflection identity, or estimate; all such assertions belong to the associated validity condition.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.InstanceData.summary: The certificate inputs: finite multiplier-weight data, parameter-dependent rotation rates, transport bounds, reflection permutations for the $\lambda$- and $\mu$-pieces, a row-weight bound, forcing label lists and a natural forcing cutoff. No positivity, separation or estimate is asserted.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsActuatorIn.text: For positive κ and a natural integer j_*, suppose each forcing field is assigned a finite set of labels. This condition requires |ι₂|≤j_* and |ι₂−ι₁|≤j_* for every assigned label. For every parameter α in K and every label in that entire rectangle, neither its Fourier index (2ι₂−ι₁,κι₁) in normalized time and azimuth nor its negative may belong to any λ or μ mode set. Thus the multiplier's skew terms avoid a rectangle containing all declared forcing harmonics. The condition alone does not prove that the actual fields have only those harmonics; the finite field representation and its harmonic-expansion theorem supply that identification.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsActuatorIn.summary: For $\kappa>0$ and natural $j_*$, every forcing label has $|\iota_2|\le j_*$ and $|\iota_2-\iota_1|\le j_*$, and for every $\alpha\in\mathcal K$ no label in that rectangle has Fourier index $\pm(2\iota_2-\iota_1,\kappa\iota_1)$ in any $\lambda$ or $\mu$ mode set.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsConstantCo.text: For upper and lower scalar splines, require σ*>0 to be a knot of the upper radial partition. There must be one complex number c such that, for every radial index i of that upper partition whose right endpoint is at most σ*, every upper angular piece at index i and every lower angular piece at the same index i is the constant polynomial c. The lower radial endpoints are not inspected. This is the formal condition used for the constant class weights of Appendix B.2. To conclude that the represented spatial weight is constant near the origin, one also needs valid, identical radial partitions, positive compactification length L, and decay exponent zero.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsConstantCo.summary: There is one complex c such that every upper radial index ending at or before σ*>0 has constant upper and lower pieces c. The test uses the upper partition; the physical constant-core interpretation of Appendix B.2 also needs matching partitions and decay exponent zero.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsFlatAtOrig.text: For the upper and lower scalar splines, there must be one complex number c such that every polynomial in the first radial strip restricts to c at σ=0, independently of η. This is precisely the constant value at σ=0 required for the polynomial factors of λ and μ in Appendix B.2. It is an endpoint-value condition. It does not require the spline to be constant on a neighborhood of the origin, nor does it impose derivative matching or positivity. Taking real parts gives the corresponding common real endpoint value.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsFlatAtOrig.summary: There is one complex $c$ such that every polynomial in the first radial strip of both splines restricts to $c$ at $\sigma=0$, independently of $\eta$, the origin-value condition for $\lambda$ and $\mu$ in Appendix B.2. It is an endpoint condition only, with no constancy near the origin.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsFlipClosed.text: Choose a permutation of the λ-pieces and a permutation of the μ-pieces. This condition requires the class weights at raw Fourier pair (n,−k) to equal the upper/lower reflections of those at (n,k), and the two permutations to carry every piece to its reflected finite representation. These equalities implement the data symmetry used in (B.17). No condition here says that either permutation is an involution. Rotation rates and transport bounds are absent from these data, so their transformation rules must be checked separately before (B.17) follows.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsFlipClosed.summary: For chosen permutations of the $\lambda$- and $\mu$-pieces, class weights at $(n,-k)$ are the upper/lower reflections of those at $(n,k)$ and each piece goes to its reflection, the data symmetry of (B.17). The permutations need not be involutions; rates and transport bounds are separate.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsInstanceEn.text: This condition joins five requirements for the same cell data. The test rows and their weights agree with the cell-polynomial construction and its Gram-matrix normalization; their weights satisfy 0<τ≤τmax, the coercivity c is positive, and τmax/c≤c₀² with c₀≥0. The multiplier weights agree with the stated spline data and obey their regularity and reflection conditions. The forcing labels lie in a range avoided by the skew weights. The matrix-valued constraint fields Ξᵢ agree with their cell-polynomial representations. Every prescribed symmetry has the generated form following (B.1). These are the representation conditions of Appendix B.1–B.2, including the row-weight inequalities. The cell estimates, tail bounds, adjoint errors and remaining certificate inequalities are imposed separately.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsInstanceEn.summary: Collects the represented rows, multiplier weights, forcing labels, constraint fields and symmetries of Appendix B.1–B.2. It includes row-weight bounds, including τmax/c≤c₀², while the cell estimates and remaining certificate inequalities are imposed separately.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsJoinedScal.text: Let a be a nonnegative integer and let the scalar be represented separately above and below y₃=0 by complex polynomial splines in σ=|y|/(|y|+L) and |η|=|y₃|/|y|. This condition requires joins through order a within each half, identical radial partitions, and equality of the equatorial traces of their η-derivatives with the factor (−1)ᵒ for order o≤a. That sign changes differentiation in |η| below the plane into differentiation in η. These are the matching conditions behind the scalar weights of Appendix B.2; taking real parts produces the real weight. The condition itself imposes neither a positive length L nor the radial prefactor and its decay.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsJoinedScal.summary: For integer $a\ge0$, the upper and lower splines in $\sigma$ and $|\eta|$ join through order $a$, share radial partitions, and their equatorial $\eta$-derivative traces of order $o\le a$ agree with factor $(-1)^o$: the matching conditions for the scalar weights of Appendix B.2. $L>0$ is not imposed.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsPinInstanc.text: The meridian mesh must be valid, the certificate's constraint fields Ξᵢ must equal the fields obtained by evaluating the cell-polynomial tensor data, and every such representation must be closed under conjugation of its harmonics. This identifies the tensors entering ℓᵢ(v)=⟨Ξᵢ,∇v⟩ with the representation in (B.10). It does not require Ξᵢ to be an exact gradient and does not give the approximation by ∇Φᵢ or its error bound. Those additional conditions are used separately in the adjoint estimate.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsPinInstanc.summary: The meridian mesh is valid, each matrix-valued constraint field $\Xi_i$ equals its evaluated cell-polynomial representation, and each representation is closed under conjugating harmonics, matching (B.10). $\Xi_i$ need not be an exact gradient, and no approximation by $\nabla\Phi_i$ is given.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsPositiveSt.text: This condition requires a valid tensor partition of [0,1]² and strictly positive upper and lower constants in every actual cell. It supplies the positivity requirement for the auxiliary functions of Appendix B.2. It places no restriction on the integer exponent d in the factor (1−σ)ᵈ. For L>0 that factor is positive at every finite point of ℝ³, and hence the evaluated function is positive. The length condition is not part of this declaration, and the arrays outside the finite cell range are unrestricted.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsPositiveSt.summary: A valid tensor partition of $[0,1]^2$ with strictly positive upper and lower constants in every actual cell, the positivity requirement for the auxiliary functions of Appendix B.2. The integer exponent $d$ is unrestricted, and $L>0$ is not part of the condition.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsRowInstanc.text:
This condition requires the polynomial generator and mesh assumptions of B.1, identifies the certificate rows with the inverse-square-root-normalized real generators, and identifies their separate weights as t_{Q,ι}/c. It requires c>0, c₀≥0 and t_max/c≤c₀², where 0<t_{Q,ι}≤t_max is imposed for every tested cell and label. Hence the weighted fields e_a=√(t_{Q,ι}/c)u_a have norm at most c₀ once the normalization theorem gives ‖u_a‖_H=1. In the cell construction c=3/50 and t_max=400(1+2^{−18}), yielding the third bound in (B.22). The condition also includes the local complex Gram positivity and row identifications, so it asserts more than that scalar inequality alone.

Its polynomial row assumptions are these. On a finite valid mesh of rectangles Q, choose finitely many polynomial triples φ for each tested label ι, and one real field for each real part and, for ι≠0, each imaginary part. This condition requires complete, distinct choices from one representative of ±ι, with the zero label real; conjugate labels have conjugate polynomials. It requires r∂_rφ_r+φ_r+iκι₁φ_φ+r∂_zφ_z=0 and φ_r=φ_φ=0 on any cell axis. Each complex matrix ∫_Q φ·overline{φ′} r dr dz is positive definite. It also requires positive cell-and-label weights, unchanged by sign reversal and bounded by a supplied maximum. These are assumptions ensuring the normalized real rows can be formed. Extending an individual generator by zero across a cell boundary need not preserve divergence distributionally. The mesh rectangles are Q=[r₁,r₂]×[z₁,z₂] with 0≤r₁<r₂ and 0≤z₁<z₂ and pairwise disjoint interiors. Here r=√(y₁²+y₂²), z=y₃, and E_ι=exp(i[2π(2ι₂−ι₁)θ+κι₁φ]), with φ=arg(y₁+iy₂). The full real generator on z<0 uses the reflected label (−ι₁,ι₂−ι₁), the polynomials at (r,−z), and vector-component signs (+,−,−) in the cylindrical frame. Endpoints shared by closed cells can contribute more than one indicator term; they form a set of measure zero for the Gram integrals.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsRowInstanc.summary: Identifies certificate rows with normalized real generators and weights $t_{Q,\iota}/c$, with $c>0$, $c_0\ge0$, $0<t_{Q,\iota}\le t_{\max}$ and $t_{\max}/c\le c_0^2$, so weighted rows have norm at most $c_0$. With $c=3/50$, $t_{\max}=400(1+2^{-18})$ this gives the third bound in (B.22).

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsRowValues.text: On a finite valid mesh of rectangles Q, choose finitely many polynomial triples φ for each tested label ι, and one real field for each real part and, for ι≠0, each imaginary part. This condition requires complete, distinct choices from one representative of ±ι, with the zero label real; conjugate labels have conjugate polynomials. It requires r∂_rφ_r+φ_r+iκι₁φ_φ+r∂_zφ_z=0 and φ_r=φ_φ=0 on any cell axis. Each complex matrix ∫_Q φ·overline{φ′} r dr dz is positive definite. It also requires positive cell-and-label weights, unchanged by sign reversal and bounded by a supplied maximum. These are assumptions ensuring the normalized real rows can be formed. Extending an individual generator by zero across a cell boundary need not preserve divergence distributionally. The mesh rectangles are Q=[r₁,r₂]×[z₁,z₂] with 0≤r₁<r₂ and 0≤z₁<z₂ and pairwise disjoint interiors. Here r=√(y₁²+y₂²), z=y₃, and E_ι=exp(i[2π(2ι₂−ι₁)θ+κι₁φ]), with φ=arg(y₁+iy₂). The full real generator on z<0 uses the reflected label (−ι₁,ι₂−ι₁), the polynomials at (r,−z), and vector-component signs (+,−,−) in the cylindrical frame. Endpoints shared by closed cells can contribute more than one indicator term; they form a set of measure zero for the Gram integrals. The azimuthal order κ is a positive natural number.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsRowValues.summary: On a valid mesh, polynomial triples $\varphi$ per tested label with complete conjugate choices, a cylindrical divergence-free condition, vanishing radial and azimuthal parts on axis cells, positive definite cell Gram matrices and positive bounded weights, so normalized real rows exist.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsWeightInst.text: Fix finite weight data of the prescribed compactified-polynomial form and reflection permutations of the λ and μ indices. This condition identifies the multiplier weights at every α in K with those fixed data, using supplied rates ν_p(α) and fixed transport bounds. All spatial weights, classes, mode sets and auxiliary functions are independent of α. The reflected index has the reflected mode set, the mirrored weight and auxiliary functions, the opposite rate −ν_p(α), and the reflected transport bound. The coefficient c equals the chosen cell coercivity constant. These are identifications and symmetry requirements; admissibility estimates such as positive rotating-frame frequencies and (B.19) must still be established for each α.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsWeightInst.summary: Identifies the multiplier weights at each $\alpha\in\mathcal K$ with fixed data, with supplied rates $\nu_p(\alpha)$ and fixed transport bounds, so spatial weights and mode sets are independent of $\alpha$; reflected indices carry mirrored data and rate $-\nu_p(\alpha)$; $c$ is the cell coercivity.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsWeightValu.text: The condition describes finitely many classes of integer harmonics, with real weights D_ι,Z_ι in the compactified coordinates σ=|y|/(|y|+L), |η|=|y₃|/|y| for a positive length L. The polynomial pieces for D and Z match through order 2, including the plane y₃=0, are constant on a common neighborhood of the origin, and have no extra decay factor; D is nonnegative. The λ weights are (1−σ) times continuous nonnegative polynomial data, the μ weights are (1−σ)² times such data, each constant in the angular coordinate at σ=0. Auxiliary functions are positive constants on rectangular cells multiplied by integer powers of 1−σ, whose exponents may be negative; the μ auxiliary scalar is positive. D and Z agree at opposite labels. The two constants c,c_μ lie strictly between 0 and 1. This condition prescribes regularity and shape; the transport, frequency and numerical bounds are additional conditions.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsWeightValu.summary: Harmonic classes with weights $D_\iota,Z_\iota$ in $\sigma$ and $|\eta|$, matching through order 2 and constant near the origin, $D\ge0$; $\lambda$ weights are $(1-\sigma)$ and $\mu$ weights $(1-\sigma)^2$ times nonnegative polynomial data; auxiliary functions positive; $0<c,c_\mu<1$.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.MuGiven.text: One velocity multiplier piece consists of a set of integer time-angle frequencies, a scalar spline representing μ, two piecewise constant auxiliary functions, and a real number η. The functions are the energy-share and balancing factors; η is the additional scalar balancing parameter. This represents one p∈𝒫μ in Appendix B.2. The data impose no sign restriction on η or on the functions, and no separation of the mode set from its negative. Positivity, symmetry, the rotating-frame rate, and the transport estimate are separate requirements.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.MuGiven.summary: The data of one $p\in\mathcal P_\mu$ in Appendix B.2: integer time-angle frequencies, a scalar spline for $\mu$, piecewise constant energy-share and balancing functions, and a real $\eta$. No sign or mode separation is imposed; positivity, symmetry, rate and transport are separate.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.MuGiven.mirr.text: For a velocity multiplier piece, send its raw Fourier pairs (n,k) to (n,−k), interchange the upper and lower halves of the μ-weight and its two auxiliary functions, and keep the scalar η unchanged. This is the reflection prescribed for these data in Appendix B.2 and (B.17). The operation leaves the radial decay powers unchanged. It does not supply a reflected rotation rate or prove a symmetry of the evaluated functions; the rate and the necessary joining conditions belong to the surrounding hypotheses.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.MuGiven.mirr.summary: Sends raw Fourier pairs $(n,k)\mapsto(n,-k)$, swaps upper and lower halves of the $\mu$-weight and its two auxiliary functions, and keeps $\eta$, as prescribed in Appendix B.2 and (B.17). Decay powers are unchanged; the reflected rate and joining conditions are separate hypotheses.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.SplineJoins.text: For a nonnegative integer a, this condition requires a strictly ordered tensor partition of [0,1]² and equality of the two polynomial traces at every interior partition line, for every derivative order 0,…,a in the direction normal to that line. The equality is an equality of polynomials in the remaining variable, so it holds along the whole interface. This supplies the joining condition for the scalar multiplier weights in Appendix B.2. The formal condition states these equalities directly; it does not assert positivity, decay, or a bound on any derivative. Natural-number subtraction in the adjacent index is harmless because the interface index is at least one.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.SplineJoins.summary: For integer $a\ge0$, a strictly ordered tensor partition of $[0,1]^2$ with the two polynomial traces equal at every interior partition line for normal derivative orders $0,\dots,a$, as polynomials along the whole interface: the joining condition for the scalar weights of Appendix B.2.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.text: The data consist of a tensor partition in (σ,|η|), two arrays of real constants for the upper and lower halves, and an integer d. Their associated spatial function is (1−σ)ᵈ times the constant selected by the cell containing (σ,|η|). This is the representation of the positive auxiliary functions described in Appendix B.2. The exponent is an arbitrary integer, so negative exponents are permitted. The data alone require neither an ordered partition nor positive constants. Arrays are defined for every pair of natural-number indices, although only indices of actual cells enter a valid representation.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.summary: A tensor partition in $(\sigma,|\eta|)$, upper and lower arrays of real constants, and an integer $d$, representing $(1-\sigma)^d$ times the cell constant, the auxiliary functions of Appendix B.2. Negative $d$ is allowed, and neither an ordered partition nor positive constants is required.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.ev.text: Write σ=|y|/(|y|+L) and η=y₃/|y|. The function equals (1−σ)ᵈ times the upper cell value at (σ,η) when y₃≥0, and the lower cell value at (σ,−η) otherwise. This is the integer-power, piecewise constant representation specified in Appendix B.2. The exponent d ranges over all integers. If L>0 then σ<1 at every finite point, so a negative exponent has a nonzero denominator. Without that hypothesis the formula remains defined by zero-valued division; it need not represent the intended spatial weight. The equatorial plane belongs to the upper branch.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.ev.summary: With $\sigma=|y|/(|y|+L)$, $\eta=y_3/|y|$, the value $(1-\sigma)^d$ times the upper cell value at $(\sigma,\eta)$ for $y_3\ge0$, or the lower value at $(\sigma,-\eta)$ otherwise, with integer $d$. Division by zero is taken as zero, so without $L>0$ it need not represent the weight.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.lo.text: For a point y, this expression selects the radial cell at σ=|y|/(|y|+L) and the angular cell at −η=−y₃/|y|, and returns the corresponding lower-array value. It supplies the piecewise constant factor below the equatorial plane for the auxiliary functions of Appendix B.2. Its geometric interpretation uses y₃<0, L>0, and valid partitions. At an interior knot the right-hand cell is selected. The expression itself is defined for all y, including y=0 by the convention 0/0=0. The decay factor and positivity conditions are supplied separately.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.lo.summary: The lower-array value in the radial cell at $\sigma=|y|/(|y|+L)$ and the angular cell at $-\eta=-y_3/|y|$, the factor below the equatorial plane in Appendix B.2. At an interior knot the right-hand cell is chosen; it is defined for all $y$, with $0/0=0$ at $y=0$.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.mi.text: The operation interchanges the upper and lower arrays of a piecewise constant auxiliary function, leaving its tensor partition and integer decay exponent unchanged. It represents reflection of the multiplier data across y₃=0 in the symmetry condition of Appendix B.2. Away from the plane, evaluation gives the reflected function. On y₃=0 both evaluations select an upper branch, so equality with spatial reflection there also needs matching upper and lower values. This operation imposes no such matching and no positivity condition.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.mi.summary: Interchanges the upper and lower arrays of an auxiliary function, keeping its partition and exponent, representing reflection across $y_3=0$ in Appendix B.2. On $y_3=0$ both evaluations take the upper branch, so equality with spatial reflection there needs matching values.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.up.text: For a point y, choose the radial cell containing σ=|y|/(|y|+L) and the angular cell containing η=y₃/|y|, and return the corresponding real number from the upper array. This is the piecewise constant factor of an auxiliary function in Appendix B.2, before multiplication by (1−σ)ᵈ. Its intended use is y₃≥0 with L>0 and a valid partition of [0,1]². At an interior knot the right-hand cell is selected. The formula is defined for all y; at y=0 the quotient defining η is taken to be zero. No positivity or regularity assertion is included.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.up.summary: The upper-array value in the radial cell containing $\sigma=|y|/(|y|+L)$ and angular cell containing $\eta=y_3/|y|$, the piecewise constant factor before $(1-\sigma)^d$ in Appendix B.2. At an interior knot the right-hand cell is chosen; at $y=0$, $\eta$ is taken as zero.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.WeightValues.text: These data specify a spatial chart, a radial coordinate σ* for a common central region, a class assigned to each integer mode, one strain-conversion and one vorticity-conversion scalar spline per class, finitely many λ- and μ-pieces, and real constants c and cμ. They represent the weights of Appendix B.2, where the main coercivity constant is 3/50. Here c is a free input, and the class set need not yet be finite. Admissibility, positive length, joins, signs, decay, and 0<c,cμ<1 are requirements of subsequent conditions, not consequences of providing these data.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.WeightValues.summary: Data for the weights of Appendix B.2: a chart, a central radius $\sigma^*$, a class per integer mode, conversion splines per class, finitely many $\lambda$- and $\mu$-pieces, and constants $c,c_\mu$. In the paper $c=3/50$; here $c$ is a free input, and the class set need not be finite.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.WeightValues.text: Given the spline and step-function data of a λ-piece, a chart with length L, a real rotation rate ν, and a real spatial transport bound, this expression forms the corresponding piece of the multiplier. It evaluates λ and all eight auxiliary factors on ℝ³, and retains the prescribed frequency set, rate, and transport bound. This is the passage from the finite representation in Appendix B.2 to its spatial functions. The definition proves no transport estimate or admissibility condition. Quotients and integer powers in the chart and the auxiliary functions retain their everywhere-defined conventions unless L>0 is supplied.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.WeightValues.summary: From the data of a $\lambda$-piece, a chart of length $L$, a rotation rate $\nu$ and a transport bound, the multiplier piece with $\lambda$ and its eight auxiliary factors evaluated on $\mathbb R^3$, as in Appendix B.2. No transport estimate is proved; division conventions apply unless $L>0$.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.WeightValues.text: Given the spline and step-function data of a μ-piece, a chart, a rotation rate ν, and a spatial transport bound, this expression supplies μ, its energy-share and balancing functions, the scalar η, and the mode set to the multiplier. It is the evaluation of one p∈𝒫μ described in Appendix B.2. The definition does not require any of these values to be positive and does not verify the transport bound. Those analytic requirements belong to the admissibility conditions; the chart needs L>0 for its intended geometric interpretation.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.WeightValues.summary: From the data of a $\mu$-piece, a chart, a rate $\nu$ and a transport bound, the multiplier piece with $\mu$, its energy-share and balancing functions, $\eta$ and the mode set: one $p\in\mathcal P_\mu$ of Appendix B.2. Positivity and the transport bound are not required.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.WeightValues.text: For the prescribed mode classes and finite λ- and μ-families, evaluate their scalar splines and auxiliary factors on ℝ³, using the common chart, and attach the supplied rates and transport bounds. The resulting functions are the conversion weights 𝔇ι and ℨι and the pieces appearing in (B.14)–(B.16), with constants c and cμ unchanged. This definition is a representation map. It asserts neither the inequalities of (B.19) nor the lower bound for the mode density. Parameter dependence enters through the rates passed to it; the spline data themselves are fixed.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.WeightValues.summary: Evaluates all class splines and $\lambda$- and $\mu$-pieces on $\mathbb R^3$ with the common chart, attaching rates and transport bounds, giving $\mathfrak D_\iota$, $\mathfrak Z_\iota$ and the pieces of (B.14)-(B.16) with $c,c_\mu$ unchanged. It asserts neither (B.19) nor the mode-density bound.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.rowFieldsOrt.text: Assume the regularity assertion that real polynomial harmonic fields on a finite valid cell mesh are measurable, periodic, bounded and square integrable over (0,1)×ℝ³. For a row system satisfying the mesh, polynomial, completeness, conjugation and positive-weight conditions of B.1, assume additionally that its assembled real Gram matrix G_{ab}=⟨tilde e_a,tilde e_b⟩_H is positive definite. The theorem proves ⟨u_a,u_b⟩_H=δ_{ab} for u_a=∑_b(G^{−1/2})_{ab}tilde e_b. Positivity of the assembled Gram matrix and regularity of the cell fields are explicit premises of this theorem; separate results derive them from the finite representation. The paper's rows are e_a=√τ_a u_a, so their squared norms are τ_a after this rescaling.
Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.rowFieldsOrt.summary: Assuming regularity of the polynomial cell fields and a positive definite assembled Gram matrix $G$, the rows $u_a=\sum_b(G^{-1/2})_{ab}\tilde e_b$ satisfy $\langle u_a,u_b\rangle_H=\delta_{ab}$. The paper's rows are $e_a=\sqrt{\tau_a}u_a$, with squared norms $\tau_a$.

Breakdown.CertCell.InstancePair.IsPairSu.text:
Fix the cell data, the forcing harmonics, proposed matrix profiles for forcing and constraint pairings, and numbers $e_{\mathsf Q}$. Every forcing harmonic and its negative, and every constraint harmonic and its negative, must belong to one common finite set. The constraint profiles agree exactly with the harmonics of $\Xi_i$ throughout each cell. For every harmonic in the common finite set outside a specified exceptional subset, a forcing profile agrees with the corresponding harmonic of $
abla b_i$. This clause imposes no agreement at harmonics outside that common set. All profile components are measurable and bounded. The exceptional subset is contained in the common set and has positive weights $w_\iota$; the sum of $\int_{\mathsf Q}r\sum_i|\widetilde{

abla b_i|^2/(4w_\iota)$ over it is at most $e_{\mathsf Q}$. These are the forcing-approximation errors entering $\mathsf n_b$ after (B.43). The paper states this kind of weighted error bound without prescribing this exact indexing arrangement.
Breakdown.CertCell.InstancePair.IsPairSu.summary: Forcing and constraint harmonics and negatives lie in one finite set; constraint profiles equal the harmonics of $\Xi_i$, and on that set outside an exceptional subset forcing profiles equal those of $\nabla b_i$, with weighted error sum over the subset at most $e_{\mathsf Q}$.

Assume rotation by $\pi/\varkappa$ with time shift $1/2$ and reflection $R_*(y_1,y_2,y_3)=(y_1,-y_2,-y_3)$ with time shift zero are in the symmetry set. Assume finite harmonic representations and regularity of the forcing fields $b_i$, support of those fields in the cells, polynomial representations of the constraint fields $\Xi_i$, and bounds on the errors of their cell approximations. If the sum of the allocated approximation errors is at most $e$, then for every $\alpha\in\mathcal K$, weak perturbation with finite positive density, real $ eta,\zeta$, and measurable period-one square-integrable forcing satisfying the linearized equation modulo gradients, the sum of cell pairings is at most $(\sum_i eta_i\langle b_i,\mathsf Mvangle+2\zeta\cdot\ell(v))/(4\pi)+e| eta|^2$ plus the allocated gradient allowances. The velocity and the separately supplied fields $G,H,g$ are measurable on $\mathbb R	imes\mathbb R^3$ and exactly period one in $	heta$. The velocity has divergence zero, $v(	heta)\in L^6(\mathbb R^3)$ for almost every $	heta$, and weak spatial derivatives $G=

abla v$ are in $L^2$; the last identity is distributional. For every supplied symmetry $(R,	au)\in\Gamma$, $v(	heta+	au,Ry)=Rv(	heta,y)$ almost everywhere. Here $\ell_i(v)=\int_0^1\int\Xi_i:
abla v$; equality modulo gradients means equality against every smooth solenoidal test compactly supported in $\mathbb R	imes\mathbb R^3$. The multiplier pairing is identified by integration by parts. The forcing-row identity and rectangle bounds are separate contributions to (B.34). This auxiliary statement imposes no sign condition on the real parameter S. Normalized time still has period one; when S=0 the coefficient 1/S in the transport identity is assigned zero. The paper’s physical period is positive.
Breakdown.CertCell.InstancePair.pairShar.summary: Under both symmetries and the forcing and constraint representations with allocated errors at most $e$ in total, each $\alpha\in\mathcal K$ and admissible perturbation give cell pairings at most $(\sum_i\beta_i\langle b_i,\mathsf Mv\rangle+2\zeta\cdot\ell(v))/(4\pi)+e|\beta|^2$ plus allowances.

Breakdown.CertCell.InstanceSplit.Enclosu.text: For a fixed period S, reference W and its supplied second derivative, and a family of λ and μ weights, this condition requires pointwise upper bounds for the modes of W, ∇W, curl W and ∇curl W whose frequencies lie in the supplied finite set, plus bounds for |curl W| and the operator norm of ∇curl W along every axial rotation. It bounds |W+y/2−ν_pe₃×y| by the transport function of each p. Every selected mode set has Ω_p bounded below by a positive number. For every y it requires ∑λ_p≤n_λ and ∑|∇λ_p|≤n_{∇λ}; for every frequency it requires (∑|sgn_p|μ_p)²≤n_μ∑|sgn_p||Ω_p|μ_p, with n_μ≥0. Finally I′₂≥0 is required. The condition supplies these numerical inequalities; positivity, regularity, measurability and decay of the weights are additional data requirements. All bounds are uniform in real time. This condition does not require that finite set to contain zero, be closed under negation or contain the complete harmonic expansion of W; those are separate assumptions in the full admissibility condition.
Breakdown.CertCell.InstanceSplit.Enclosu.summary:
Bounds on the reference modes of $W$, $
abla W$, $\operatorname{curl}W$, $
abla\operatorname{curl}W$, transport bounds, positive lower bounds on $\Omega_p$, $\sum_p\lambda_p\le n_\lambda$, $\sum_p|
abla\lambda_p|\le n_{
abla\lambda}$, the $\mu$ inequality with $n_\mu\ge0$, and $I'_2\ge0$.

Breakdown.CertCell.InstanceSplit.ValuesF.text: For every raw Fourier pair ξ=(n,k) and point y, the four harmonic majorants must be unchanged by (ξ,y)↦((n,−k),R*y), and the two full-field vorticity majorants must be unchanged by R*. All six kinds of majorant must also be invariant under every rotation about the y₃-axis. Every λ- and μ-transport bound must be axisymmetric. These are the symmetries of the bounding functions used in (B.17). The condition does not assert that they actually bound the field, nor does it impose the reflected permutation rule on transport bounds or rotation rates; those are separate conditions.
Breakdown.CertCell.InstanceSplit.ValuesF.summary: The four harmonic majorants are invariant under $(\xi,y)\mapsto((n,-k),R^*y)$, the two vorticity majorants under $R^*$, all six under rotations about the $y_3$-axis, and transport bounds are axisymmetric: the symmetries of the bounds in (B.17). That they bound the field is not asserted.

Breakdown.CertCell.Internal.slice_invers.text: For measurable $u:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ with a measurable weak gradient $G=\nabla u$ and $u\in L^6(\mathbb R^3)$, the formal statement proves $\int|u(y)|^2/|y|^2\,dy\le4\int|G(y)|^2\,dy$. It is stated for nonnegative extended integrals, so no finiteness assumption on the gradient integral is needed; the finite-energy case is the one used in Lemma B.11. No solenoidality, symmetry or second derivative is required. Division by zero is assigned the value zero at the origin; changing the integrand at that single point leaves the integral unchanged. A complex scalar field can be represented by its real and imaginary parts as the first two components of a real vector field.
Breakdown.CertCell.Internal.slice_invers.summary: For measurable $u:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ in $L^6$ with measurable weak gradient $G$, $\int|u|^2/|y|^2\,dy\le4\int|G|^2\,dy$ as extended nonnegative integrals, with no finiteness assumption. No solenoidality or symmetry is required; the finite-energy case is used in Lemma B.11.

Breakdown.CertCell.IsBoxUniform.text: For every $\alpha\in\mathcal K$, the reference field must equal one fixed field $W^{\mathrm r}$. The classification of harmonics, the two convection-group assignments, the harmonic majorants, the multiplier's velocity coefficient and the coefficient of the energy term are fixed throughout $\mathcal K$; the last equals the designated coercivity number. Each curl and velocity multiplier piece is identical to its value at parameter zero after setting its rotating-frame rate to zero, so only that rate may vary. These conditions express the parameter independence used in Appendix B.2 and B.3. They compare the supplied functions even at parameter zero, whether or not zero belongs to $\mathcal K$. They are stronger and more explicit than merely saying that all estimates hold uniformly.
Breakdown.CertCell.IsBoxUniform.summary: For every $\alpha\in\mathcal K$ the reference field is one fixed $W^{\mathrm r}$, classes, majorants and coefficients are fixed, and each multiplier piece equals its value at parameter zero apart from its rate. This is stronger and more explicit than the parameter independence in Appendix B.2-B.3.

Breakdown.CertCell.IsCellMesh.text: The input is a finite family of nondegenerate rectangles in the closed meridian quarter plane, with resolved, tested and eliminated finite sets of lattice harmonics on each rectangle. The formal statement requires distinct rectangles to overlap only on a set of area zero, the tested set to lie in the resolved set, the eliminated and resolved sets to be disjoint, and each set to be closed under $\iota\mapsto-\iota$. On an axis cell only $\iota_1=0$ may be resolved. It requires equal degrees for opposite harmonics, an integer side degree $d_0\ge-1$, $d_0\ge2$ on tested modes, and a natural-number volume degree $d\ge\max(d_0,0)+2$. The stronger $d_0\ge1$ for every resolved harmonic is imposed by the separate condition on cell layouts. The condition here alone permits $d_0=-1$ or $0$ and does not impose a nonzero azimuthal frequency on eliminated modes.
Breakdown.CertCell.IsCellMesh.summary: Finitely many nondegenerate rectangles overlapping only in area zero, with resolved, tested and eliminated harmonic sets closed under $\iota\mapsto-\iota$, only $\iota_1=0$ resolved on axis cells, $d_0\ge-1$, $d_0\ge2$ on tested modes and $d\ge\max(d_0,0)+2$. By itself it permits $d_0=-1$ or $0$.

Breakdown.CertCell.IsLatticeHarmonic.text: For m∈ℕ and an ordinary integer frequency pair (j,j′), this requires integers ι₁,ι₂ with j=2ι₂−ι₁ and j′=mι₁. For m>0 it says that m divides j′ and j−j′/m is even, the harmonic condition after (B.2). The existential formula also has a meaning at m=0, where it requires j′=0 and allows any j; it therefore does not by itself include the paper's κ≥3 hypothesis.
Breakdown.CertCell.IsLatticeHarmonic.summary: For $m\in\mathbb N$ and integers $(j,j')$, there are integers $\iota_1,\iota_2$ with $j=2\iota_2-\iota_1$, $j'=m\iota_1$; for $m>0$ this is the harmonic condition after (B.2). At $m=0$ it requires $j'=0$ and allows any $j$, so it does not include the paper's $\kappa\ge3$.

Breakdown.CertCell.KnotZero.planeOf.text: Map y=(y₁,y₂,y₃)∈ℝ³ to (r,z)=(√(y₁²+y₂²),y₃). This is the signed meridian-plane coordinate used for the partition spheres and cones in Appendix B.1. In particular z is not replaced by |z|. The map is defined on the axis with r=0 and retains the sign of the vertical coordinate. Reflection symmetry is imposed separately when the exceptional set is completed.
Breakdown.CertCell.KnotZero.planeOf.summary: The map $y\in\mathbb R^3\mapsto(r,z)=(\sqrt{y_1^2+y_2^2},y_3)$, the signed meridian coordinate used for the partition spheres and cones of Appendix B.1. The sign of $z$ is kept and $r=0$ on the axis.

Breakdown.CertCell.KnotZero.zeroOn.text: Given a set N in the signed meridian plane and a time-dependent bilinear field H, set H to zero at every y whose meridian coordinates (√(y₁²+y₂²),y₃) belong to N, and leave it unchanged elsewhere. This makes explicit a representative convention for the bounded second derivatives discussed in Appendix B.1. It does not change the velocity field. The operation alone does not assert that N lifts to a null set or that H is a weak Hessian; only with those facts does the modification preserve the weak-derivative class.
Breakdown.CertCell.KnotZero.zeroOn.summary: Sets a bilinear field $H$ to zero at every $y$ whose meridian coordinates lie in a set $N$, and leaves it unchanged elsewhere: a representative convention for the bounded second derivatives of Appendix B.1. That $N$ lifts to a null set, or that $H$ is a weak Hessian, is not asserted.

Breakdown.CertCell.ModeCharges.text: For each lattice label ι and meridian point (r,z), these data supply four real functions: the coefficient s₁ of |curl G|², the coefficient s₂ of |G||v|, the coefficient s₃ of the Young-inequality terms, and the splitting length h. They enter the expression s₁|curl G|²+√(7/2)s₂|G||v|+(√(7/2)/2)s₃(h|G|²+|v|²/h) in (B.25). This data format allows dependence on the harmonic as well as location. Nonnegative majorants, h>0, measurability and the claimed bounds for the reference field are separate conditions.
Breakdown.CertCell.ModeCharges.summary: For each label $\iota$ and meridian point, four real functions $s_1,s_2,s_3,h$ entering $s_1|\mathrm{curl}\,G|^2+\sqrt{7/2}\,s_2|G||v|+(\sqrt{7/2}/2)s_3(h|G|^2+|v|^2/h)$ in (B.25), allowed to depend on the harmonic. Nonnegativity, $h>0$ and the bounds are separate conditions.

Breakdown.CertCell.ModeCoefficients.text: The data are five arbitrary real numbers multiplying, respectively, |∇²v̂_ι|², |∇curl v̂_ι|², |curl v̂_ι|², |∇v̂_ι|² and |v̂_ι|². They are I₂, I′₂, I′₁, I₁ and I₀ in (B.16). The fourth coefficient multiplies the Frobenius norm squared of the full gradient, with no symmetrization. The formal statement requires no nonnegativity, relation to multiplier weights or lower-bound property.
Breakdown.CertCell.ModeCoefficients.summary: Five arbitrary reals multiply |∇²v̂_ι|², |∇curl v̂_ι|², |curl v̂_ι|², |∇v̂_ι|² and |v̂_ι|², respectively: I₂,I′₂,I′₁,I₁,I₀ in (B.16). The fourth term uses the full gradient with its Frobenius norm, without symmetrization.

Breakdown.CertCell.ModeCoefficients.ofPi.text: Given multiplier-piece weights, reference harmonic bounds, a spatial energy weight, a real period P, natural angular order m and label ι, this collects the five coefficient functions of (B.16) at y=(r,0,z) and Fourier index (2ι₂−ι₁,mι₁). The Hessian coefficient is D−c, where D is the supplied conversion weight and c the coercivity coefficient. The curl-gradient coefficient is 1−D minus the share already charged to multiplier couplings. The curl coefficient is the computed curl coefficient before conversion minus Z; the full-gradient and velocity coefficients are the corresponding computed coefficients after the conversion and coupling losses. The paper describes these functions and their roles after (B.16) without printing all loss formulas. This declaration only evaluates and collects them; it supplies no positivity, period bound or admissibility proof. In particular c is a supplied number here, rather than automatically the paper's fixed 3/50.
Breakdown.CertCell.ModeCoefficients.ofPi.summary: Collects the five coefficient functions of (B.16) at $y=(r,0,z)$ and index $(2\iota_2-\iota_1,m\iota_1)$, with Hessian coefficient $D-c$. The paper describes these without printing all loss formulas; here $c$ is a supplied number, not automatically the paper's $3/50$, and no positivity is proved.

Breakdown.CertCell.ModelErrors.text: The data are nine real numbers. Breakdown.CertCell.flipLabel.text: For an ordinary time/angular Fourier pair (j,j′), this returns (j,−j′). It represents reversal of the azimuthal angle while leaving normalized time unchanged. Under the label map (ι₁,ι₂)↦(2ι₂−ι₁,mι₁), it corresponds to the lattice reflection ι↦ι♭ of (B.2). The distinction between a lattice label and an ordinary frequency pair matters: their reflection formulas are different.
Breakdown.CertCell.flipLabel.summary: For a Fourier pair $(j,j')$, the pair $(j,-j')$, reversing the azimuthal angle with time unchanged; under $(\iota_1,\iota_2)\mapsto(2\iota_2-\iota_1,m\iota_1)$ it corresponds to the lattice reflection $\iota\mapsto\iota^\flat$ of (B.2), whose formula is different.

Breakdown.CertCell.flipPoint.text: For y=(y₁,y₂,y₃)∈ℝ³ this defines R_*y=(y₁,−y₂,−y₃), the spatial rotation by π about the y₁ axis. It preserves the Euclidean norm and sends cylindrical coordinates (r,φ,z) to (r,−φ,−z), modulo the choice of angular representative. In the cylindrical frame the corresponding vector component signs are (+,−,−). This is a spatial map only; the required symmetry pair uses zero time shift.
Breakdown.CertCell.flipPoint.summary: $R_*y=(y_1,-y_2,-y_3)$, the rotation by $\pi$ about the $y_1$ axis. It preserves the norm, sends $(r,\phi,z)$ to $(r,-\phi,-z)$, and has cylindrical component signs $(+,-,-)$. The symmetry pair uses zero time shift.

Breakdown.CertCell.formNegFinite.summary: With $\varkappa\ge1$, uniform lower bounds $-B$ on the coefficients and on $(r^2+z^2)I_{0,\iota}$, and a periodic divergence-free $C^1$ reference decaying at orders 1, 2, 3, the integral $\sum_\iota\int(\mathcal I_\iota)^-r\,dr\,dz+\int\overline{J^-}r\,dr\,dz$ is finite for each weak perturbation.

Breakdown.CertCell.frameSign.text: For the ordered cylindrical components (r,φ,z), the signs are (1,−1,−1). Thus R_* preserves the radial component and reverses the angular and axial components when the angle is reflected. These are the vector signs in the lower-half-space extension of the cell fields in Appendix B.1, particularly (B.10); a matrix entry receives the product of the signs of its two indices.
Breakdown.CertCell.frameSign.summary: The signs $(1,-1,-1)$ for the cylindrical components $(r,\varphi,z)$: $R_*$ keeps the radial component and reverses the angular and axial ones. These are the vector signs in the lower-half-space extension of Appendix B.1, especially (B.10); a matrix entry gets the product of two signs.

Breakdown.CertCell.frameUnit.text: For a real angle φ, this defines the three vectors e_r=(cosφ,sinφ,0), e_φ=(−sinφ,cosφ,0) and e_z=(0,0,1), in that order. They are the cylindrical frame used for vector and tensor coefficients. When the angle is evaluated at a point on the axis, its assigned value is 0, giving (e₁,e₂,e₃). This is a coordinate convention at the axis; regularity of a physical field is obtained from its polynomial amplitude and vanishing conditions.
Breakdown.CertCell.frameUnit.summary: $e_r=(\cos\phi,\sin\phi,0)$, $e_\phi=(-\sin\phi,\cos\phi,0)$, $e_z=(0,0,1)$, the cylindrical frame for vector and tensor coefficients. On the axis the angle is assigned 0, giving $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$; regularity of physical fields comes from their amplitudes.

Breakdown.CertCell.globalForm.text: For real coefficient vectors $\beta,\zeta\in\mathbb R^n$, real coercivity $c$, multiplier weight $\omega$, pinning weight $t$ and error allowance $e$, this defines $-(c\omega^2/(4\pi)+e)|\beta|^2-|\zeta|^2/(4\pi t)$. At $c=3/50$, $t=1000$, $e=n_b$, it is the right-hand side of (B.43). The definition imposes no inequality on $A_0$ and no positivity assumptions. Division by zero is assigned zero; in the cell hypotheses $t=1000$, so that convention does not enter the intended expression.
Breakdown.CertCell.globalForm.summary: $-(c\omega^2/(4\pi)+e)|\beta|^2-|\zeta|^2/(4\pi t)$ for $\beta,\zeta\in\mathbb R^n$; at $c=3/50$, $t=1000$, $e=n_b$ it is the right-hand side of (B.43). It imposes no inequality on $A_0$. Division by zero is zero, which does not arise since $t=1000$.

Breakdown.CertCell.halfPlane.text: This is {(r,z)∈ℝ²:r>0 and z>0}, the domain of the reduced integral in (B.23). Both the cylindrical axis and the plane of reflection are excluded. Boundary sets have planar measure zero, but pointwise statements on this domain still require the strict inequalities.
Breakdown.CertCell.halfPlane.summary: The set $\{(r,z)\in\mathbb R^2: r>0,\ z>0\}$, the domain of the reduced integral in (B.23), excluding both the axis and the reflection plane. Pointwise statements on it need the strict inequalities.

Breakdown.CertCell.initialState_closed.text:

Require nonnegative local coefficient costs and a pairing error whose total is at most $e$. For every $\alpha\in\mathcal K$, real $ eta$, forcing $F$, weak perturbation, real $\zeta$ and complex auxiliary coordinates, the formal statement then bounds the sum of cell forms, twice the rectangle forms and the global negative penalty by $Q_+-Q_--[c\omega^2| eta|^2-\sum_i eta_i\langle b_i,\mathsf Mvangle-c[F]^2-t|\ell(v)|^2]/(4\pi)$. Here $Q_\pm=\int_{r,z>0}(\sum_\iota(\mathcal I_\iota)^\pm+\overline{J^\pm})r\,dr\,dz$, $\ell_i(v)=\int_0^1\int\Xi_i:
abla v$, and $[F]$ is the prescribed finite weighted row seminorm. Both $Q_+$ and $Q_-$ must be finite: the input perturbation includes positive-part finiteness, while negative-part finiteness is a separate premise. The velocity and the separately supplied fields $G,H,g$ are measurable on $\mathbb R	imes\mathbb R^3$ and exactly period one in $	heta$. The velocity has divergence zero, $v(	heta)\in L^6(\mathbb R^3)$ for almost every $	heta$, and weak spatial derivatives $G=
abla v$, $H=
abla^2v$. Over $[0,1]	imes\mathbb R^3$, $G$, $\operatorname{tr}H=\Delta v$ and $g=S^{-1}\partial_	heta v+ rac12v+ rac12y\cdot
abla v$ are in $L^2$; the last identity is distributional. For every supplied symmetry $(R,	au)\in\Gamma$, $v(	heta+	au,Ry)=Rv(	heta,y)$ almost everywhere. The measurable, period-one forcing lies in $L^2$ and satisfies $F=g-\Delta v+(W^{\mathrm r}\cdot
abla)v+(v\cdot

The cell equation uses its half-turn average and a periodic pressure gradient satisfying the same reflection. Breakdown.CertCell.initialState_closed.summary: From the cell inequalities, nonnegative unresolved and exterior terms, the forcing, rectangle and pairing bounds and finite $Q_\pm$, the cell, rectangle and penalty forms total at most $Q_+-Q_--[c\omega^2|\beta|^2-\sum_i\beta_i\langle b_i,\mathsf Mv\rangle-c[F]^2-t|\ell(v)|^2]/(4\pi)$.

Breakdown.CertCell.keySeg.text: For a radial-or-axial choice, fixed level $c$, endpoints $a,b$ and real test-polynomial coefficients, this constructs a directed segment with opposite level $c+1$. Its side moment is evaluated by the strip formula using those two levels. It is a convenient way to interpret a shared geometric trace label independently of the cell from which it arose, in the global-unknown relations of Appendix B.3. The definition imposes no endpoint ordering or positive radius. The choice $c+1$ ensures distinct levels, but its identification with a classical boundary trace still uses the regularity hypotheses of that trace.
Breakdown.CertCell.keySeg.summary: From a radial-or-axial choice, a level $c$, endpoints $a,b$ and real coefficients, a directed segment with opposite level $c+1$, whose side moment uses the strip formula, interpreting a shared trace label in Appendix B.3. No endpoint ordering or positive radius is imposed.

Breakdown.CertCell.labelAzimuth.text: For natural symmetry order m and ι∈ℤ², the angular frequency is the integer mι₁. This is κ ι₁ in the harmonic (B.2). The definition includes m=0, whereas the classical paper assumes κ≥3; the lower bound on the symmetry order must be supplied separately.
Breakdown.CertCell.labelAzimuth.summary: For natural symmetry order $m$ and $\iota\in\mathbb Z^2$, the integer angular frequency $m\iota_1$, which is $\kappa\iota_1$ in (B.2). The definition includes $m=0$, while the paper assumes $\kappa\ge3$.

Breakdown.CertCell.labelFlip.text: For an integer pair ι=(ι₁,ι₂), the defined reflected label is ι^♭=(−ι₁,ι₂−ι₁). Its time frequency 2ι₂−ι₁ is unchanged and its azimuthal frequency κι₁ changes sign. Consequently E_{ι^♭}(θ,φ)=E_ι(θ,−φ). This definition concerns the two integer labels. In a field with radial phase index l, the reflection keeps l unchanged; conjugation instead replaces (ι,l) by (−ι,−l).
Breakdown.CertCell.labelFlip.summary: $\iota^\flat=(-\iota_1,\iota_2-\iota_1)$, which keeps the time frequency $2\iota_2-\iota_1$ and reverses the azimuthal frequency $\kappa\iota_1$, so $E_{\iota^\flat}(\theta,\phi)=E_\iota(\theta,-\phi)$. In a field the radial index $l$ is kept; conjugation instead sends $(\iota,l)$ to $(-\iota,-l)$.

Breakdown.CertCell.labelGrad.text: For a real matrix field G(θ,y), order m and label ι, this averages R_−φG(τ,R_φ(r,0,z))R_φ against exp(−i[2π(2ι₂−ι₁)τ+mι₁φ]) over τ∈[0,1] and φ∈[0,2π], with factor 1/(2π). The entry (a,b) is output component a applied to derivative direction b. If G=∇v with the required regularity, it is the gradient mode used in (B.16) on the quarter plane. The supplied G is otherwise an arbitrary matrix field; this definition neither identifies it with a derivative nor asserts integrability.
Breakdown.CertCell.labelGrad.summary: For a real matrix field $G$, order $m$ and label $\iota$, the average of $R_{-\varphi}G(\tau,R_\varphi(r,0,z))R_\varphi$ against $e^{-i[2\pi(2\iota_2-\iota_1)\tau+m\iota_1\varphi]}$ with factor $1/(2\pi)$; for $G=\nabla v$ it is the gradient mode in (B.16). $G$ is otherwise arbitrary.

Breakdown.CertCell.labelHarmonic.text: For m∈ℕ and ι=(ι₁,ι₂)∈ℤ², this is the pair (2ι₂−ι₁,mι₁) of ordinary integer time and angular frequencies. It converts the lattice notation of (B.2) to the indices of the double Fourier projection (B.12). The map is defined even for m=0, where it need not identify a unique lattice label; a positive symmetry order is an additional hypothesis.
Breakdown.CertCell.labelHarmonic.summary: For $m\in\mathbb N$ and $\iota\in\mathbb Z^2$, the pair $(2\iota_2-\iota_1,m\iota_1)$ of integer time and angular frequencies, converting the labels of (B.2) to the indices of (B.12). At $m=0$ it need not identify a unique label.

Breakdown.CertCell.labelPhase.text: For κ a natural number, ι=(ι₁,ι₂)∈ℤ² and real θ,φ, the defined complex number is E_ι(θ,φ)=exp(i[2π(2ι₂−ι₁)θ+κι₁φ]). The first integer frequency is 2ι₂−ι₁ and the second is κι₁. No division or coordinate singularity enters this definition. Time is a real variable; its period 1 follows from the integer frequency. For positive κ, the labels give exactly the pairs (j,j′) with κ dividing j′ and j−j′/κ even.
Breakdown.CertCell.labelPhase.summary: $E_\iota(\theta,\phi)=\exp(i[2\pi(2\iota_2-\iota_1)\theta+\kappa\iota_1\phi])$, with frequencies $2\iota_2-\iota_1$ and $\kappa\iota_1$ and period 1 in time. For $\kappa>0$ the labels give exactly the pairs $(j,j')$ with $\kappa\mid j'$ and $j-j'/\kappa$ even.

Breakdown.CertCell.labelTime.text: For a lattice label ι=(ι₁,ι₂)∈ℤ², define j=2ι₂−ι₁. The time factor in (B.2) is exp(2πijθ), with period 1 in normalized time θ. For a self-similar period S>0, §7.1 sets θ=s/S, so this factor is exp(2πij s/S) and has angular frequency 2πj/S in self-similar time s. The physical time of the original solution is a different variable. This definition is only the integer linear map ι↦j; it supplies no period or field.
Breakdown.CertCell.labelTime.summary: For ι∈ℤ², defines the integer j=2ι₂−ι₁ in exp(2πijθ), as in (B.2). Since θ=s/S, the angular frequency in self-similar time s is 2πj/S; this is distinct from physical time.

Breakdown.CertCell.labelValueAt.text: For a cell, lattice label ι, an arbitrary real multiplier s and a point (r,z), this evaluates the polynomial with label ι at (r,z) when z≥0. When z<0 it evaluates the polynomial with label ι♭=(−ι₁,ι₂−ι₁) at (r,−z) and multiplies by s. This is the lower-half-space extension in (B.10), with s chosen as the appropriate frame sign ±1 in that application. The upper formula is used on z=0. No matching across that plane or restriction to the cell is asserted here.
Breakdown.CertCell.labelValueAt.summary: For a cell, label $\iota$, real $s$ and $(r,z)$, the label-$\iota$ polynomial at $(r,z)$ when $z\ge0$, and $s$ times the label-$\iota^\flat$ polynomial at $(r,-z)$ when $z<0$: the lower-half-space extension in (B.10). No matching across the plane is asserted.

Breakdown.CertCell.labelVel.text: For v:ℝ×ℝ³→ℝ³, natural order m and label ι, this is the complex vector (2π)⁻¹∫₀¹∫₀²π exp(−i[2π(2ι₂−ι₁)τ+mι₁φ])R_−φ v(τ,R_φ(r,0,z))dφdτ. It is the mode (B.12) evaluated at normalized time 0 and angle 0, as prescribed in Appendix B.3. For r>0 its three components are the cylindrical components at angle zero. The formula is also defined for r≤0; at the axis a radial direction is not determined, and at negative r the physical point has azimuth π. The definition does not assume periodicity, symmetry or integrability of v; ordinary nonintegrable Fourier integrals have the default value zero.
Breakdown.CertCell.labelVel.summary: For $v:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$, $(2\pi)^{-1}\int_0^1\int_0^{2\pi}e^{-i[2\pi(2\iota_2-\iota_1)\tau+m\iota_1\varphi]}R_{-\varphi}v(\tau,R_\varphi(r,0,z))\,d\varphi\,d\tau$, the mode (B.12) at time and angle 0 for $r>0$, also defined for $r\le0$. Nonintegrable integrals give zero.

Assign $b_a=c_w n_a+s_a/(2\sqrt{w_*})$ to an $L^2$ term and $b_a=n_a/\sqrt{3w_*}+s_a/(2\sqrt{w_*})$ to an $L^3$ term. If these nonnegative bounds sum to at most $c''_3$, the formal statement proves $Q_{W_\alpha^{\mathrm a}(	heta)}(u)-Q_{W_\alpha^{\mathrm r}(	heta)}(u)\ge-c''_3|u|_w^2$, for every $\alpha\in\mathcal K$, every $	heta$ and every spatial test field. Here $c_w=(4\pi\sqrt{w_*})^{-1/2}$. The spatial test field is $u\in L^6(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$, divergence-free, with weak gradient in $L^2$, weak second derivatives and $\Delta u\in L^2$. Its squared energy is $|u|_w^2=\int_{\mathbb R^3}(|\Delta u|^2+w_*|
abla u|^2)$. The gradient energy uses the sum of squares of the matrix entries; norms of coefficient matrices below are operator norms. For a fixed symmetry set $\Gamma$, this spatial class also requires $u(Ry)=Ru(y)$ almost everywhere whenever $(R,0)\in\Gamma$. Taking $\Gamma=\varnothing$ removes this restriction. abla u|^2/4)-\int[(W\cdot
