Breakdown.Periodic.ComparisonSmall.text:
The whole-space norm is $\|v\|_X=\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3)}$ on solenoidal velocities in $L^6(\mathbb R^3)$. 

The periodic space is the real solenoidal Fourier realization of $H^1(\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3)$, with squared norm $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+4\pi^2|k|^2)|\widehat v(k)|^2$. Its zero Fourier coefficient is allowed to be nonzero. 

Local data are a tuple $(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$ with $A_j\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ and $v\in L^6(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$, measured by $\max\{\max_j\|A_j\|_2,\|v\|_6\}$. No compatibility condition $A_j=\partial_jv$ or divergence condition is part of this data space. 

An approximation on $[0,\ell]$ is specified, for every integer $n\ge0$, by a finite sum $A_n(s)=\sum_{j=1}^m\alpha_{n,j}(s)\varphi_{n,j}$, where each $\alpha_{n,j}$ is continuous, each $\varphi_{n,j}$ is smooth, compactly supported and solenoidal with support in $\bar B_b$, and both the weights and $\|\varphi_{n,j}\|_X$ have one uniform bound. The number $m$ is fixed. 

Use the whole-space heat flow, Navier–Stokes bilinear kernel and spatial dilation $D_\lambda f(x)=\lambda^{1/2}f(\lambda^{1/2}x)$, and assume the periodic kernel estimate $\|K_{\mathbb T}(\tau)\|\le C_{\mathbb T}\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$. Let $P>0$, let $k>0$ be an integer, put $\lambda=e^{-P/k}$ and $\ell=1-\lambda\le1/2$, and choose $\lambda^{1/4}<\theta<1$ and $b>0$. The preceding finite-sum approximation is taken on $[0,\ell]$. Let $E$ be finite dimensional, let $J:E\to X$ be bounded linear, and let $e\mapsto\psi_e$ be linear, with each $\psi_e$ smooth, compactly supported, solenoidal, supported in $\bar B_b$, and representing $Je$.

The three spaces used below are the bounded sequences of continuous $X$-valued, periodic-$H^1$-valued and local-data-valued curves on $[0,\ell]$. Each has norm $\sup_n\sup_{0\le s\le\ell}\|v_n(s)\|$. Write $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$, let $w$ reduce coordinates to the unit cell centered at $a$, and put $\mu_n=T\lambda^n$. The periodic datum map is $J_{\mathbb T}e=T^{1/4}(\psi_e)_T$, where $(\psi_e)_T(x)=T^{-1/2}\psi_e((w(x)-a)/\sqrt T)$.

Here are the operators whose differences the formal statement controls. Whole-space restriction $R$ records $1_{\bar B_b}\partial_jv_n$ and $1_{\bar B_b}v_n$. Periodic restriction $R_{\mathbb T}$ records $1_{\bar B_b}\mu_n^{3/4}\partial_jz_n(a+\sqrt{\mu_n}y)$ and $1_{\bar B_b}\mu_n^{1/4}z_n(a+\sqrt{\mu_n}y)$. The periodic restriction is zero if $0<\mu_n\le1$, $b>0$, $\sqrt{\mu_n}b\le1/8$ fail; sufficiently small $T$ ensures these conditions. For a local tuple $\zeta=(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$ put $F_{\varphi,\zeta}=1_{\bar B_b}\sum_j(\varphi_jA_j+v_j\partial_j\varphi)$. The whole-space interaction is
$\displaystyle (B\zeta)_n(s)=-\sum_l\int_0^s\alpha_{n,l}(\sigma)e^{(s-\sigma)\Delta}\mathbb PF_{\varphi_{n,l},\zeta_n(\sigma)}\,d\sigma.$
For $B_{\mathbb T}$ replace the projected heat field under the integral by
$\displaystyle \mu_n^{-1/4}e^{\mu_n(s-\sigma)\Delta}\mathbb P\bigl[F_{\varphi_{n,l},\zeta_n(\sigma)}((w(x)-a)/\sqrt{\mu_n})\bigr].$
The minus sign and weights are unchanged. These definitions use the bounded integral operators supplied by the heat estimates; their general definitions assign zero if the required bounded realization does not exist.

The preceding-interval maps satisfy $(Sy)_0=(S_{\mathbb T}z)_0=0$ and, for $n\ge1$,
$\displaystyle (Sy)_n(s)=\theta^{-1}e^{s\Delta}D_\lambda y_{n-1}(\ell),\qquad (S_{\mathbb T}z)_n(s)=\frac{\lambda^{1/4}}\theta e^{\mu_ns\Delta}z_{n-1}(\ell).$
The datum maps have $(Ge)_0(s)=e^{s\Delta}Je$ and $(G_{\mathbb T}e)_0(s)=e^{Ts\Delta}J_{\mathbb T}e$, with all later entries zero. The propagation bounds are $\|S\|,\|S_{\mathbb T}\|\le\lambda^{1/4}/\theta<1$, so $I-S$ and $I-S_{\mathbb T}$ have ordinary bounded inverses. The general inverse convention assigns zero to a noninvertible operator, which is excluded here.

For every $\delta>0$, the formal statement asserts a $T_0>0$ such that, for every $0<T\le1$ with $T<T_0$, and the datum map just specified,
$\displaystyle \|R_{\mathbb T}(I-S_{\mathbb T})^{-1}B_{\mathbb T}-R(I-S)^{-1}B\|\le\delta,\qquad \|R_{\mathbb T}(I-S_{\mathbb T})^{-1}G_{\mathbb T}-R(I-S)^{-1}G\|\le\delta.$
The threshold is uniform in the sequence index. No explicit rate in $T$ or the paper’s large torus period is asserted.

This declaration records the assertion; its proof is a separate declaration.
Breakdown.Periodic.ComparisonSmall.summary: States that for every $\delta>0$ some $T_0>0$ makes, for $0<T<T_0$, $T\le1$, the periodic and whole-space localized solution operators for the interaction and the datum differ by at most $\delta$, uniformly in the sequence index. No rate in $T$ or torus period is asserted.

Breakdown.Periodic.Cutoff.Internal.contD.text: For a smooth vector field $g:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ and a fixed centre $x_0$, the formal statement proves that $(\sigma,x)\mapsto\sigma\,g(x_0+\sigma(x-x_0))\times(x-x_0)$ is smooth on all of $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3$. No divergence, decay or support condition is imposed on $g$. The real variable $\sigma$ is the integration parameter of the radial vector potential. At $x_0=0$ and for a fixed time slice $g=u^*(t)$ this proves the spatial and integration-parameter smoothness used in Lemma 5.1. It contains no variable $t$ and therefore does not by itself assert joint smoothness in $(\sigma,t,x)$.
Breakdown.Periodic.Cutoff.Internal.contD.summary: For smooth $g$ and a fixed centre $x_0$, $(\sigma,x)\mapsto\sigma g(x_0+\sigma(x-x_0))\times(x-x_0)$ is smooth on $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3$, with no divergence, decay or support condition. It has no time variable, so it gives no joint smoothness in $(\sigma,t,x)$.

Breakdown.Periodic.Cutoff.Internal.parti.text: Let $g:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ be smooth, fix a centre $x_0$, and define $A(x)=\int_0^1\sigma\,g(x_0+\sigma(x-x_0))\times(x-x_0)\,d\sigma$. For every point $x$ and each pair of Cartesian coordinates $i,j$, the formal statement proves $\partial_i A_j(x)=\int_0^1\partial_{x_i}[\sigma\,g(x_0+\sigma(x-x_0))\times(x-x_0)]_j\,d\sigma$. The derivative on the right acts only on $x$, with $\sigma$ fixed. Smoothness on a compact integration interval supplies integrability and justifies passing the derivative through the integral. Neither solenoidality nor decay is required. The statement concerns a fixed spatial field; the time in Lemma 5.1 is an external parameter.
Breakdown.Periodic.Cutoff.Internal.parti.summary: For smooth $g$, fixed $x_0$ and $A(x)=\int_0^1\sigma g(x_0+\sigma(x-x_0))\times(x-x_0)\,d\sigma$, $\partial_iA_j(x)=\int_0^1\partial_{x_i}[\cdots]_j\,d\sigma$ at every $x$, differentiating under the integral. Neither solenoidality nor decay is required.

Breakdown.Periodic.Cutoff.Internal.poten.text: Let $g:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ be smooth and satisfy $\nabla\cdot g=0$. Fix $x_0\in\mathbb R^3$. For every real $\sigma$, every $x$, and each cyclic triple of Cartesian coordinate indices, the formal statement equates the corresponding component of $\operatorname{curl}_x[\sigma g(x_0+\sigma(x-x_0))\times(x-x_0)]$ to the same component of $\sigma^2Dg(x_0+\sigma(x-x_0))(x-x_0)+2\sigma g(x_0+\sigma(x-x_0))$. The latter is $\partial_\sigma[\sigma^2g(x_0+\sigma(x-x_0))]$. Its three scalar equalities constitute the vector identity in the proof of Lemma 5.1 after taking $x_0=0$ and $g=u^*(t)$. The coordinate indices in the source are $0,1,2$; these correspond to the paper's three Cartesian coordinates, without changing the orientation.
Breakdown.Periodic.Cutoff.Internal.poten.summary: For smooth $g$ with $\nabla\cdot g=0$, $\operatorname{curl}_x[\sigma g(x_0+\sigma(x-x_0))\times(x-x_0)]=\sigma^2Dg(x_0+\sigma(x-x_0))(x-x_0)+2\sigma g(x_0+\sigma(x-x_0))$, which is $\partial_\sigma[\sigma^2g(\cdots)]$. This is the vector identity in the proof of Lemma 5.1 with $x_0=0$.

Breakdown.Periodic.Forced.Internal.force.text: Let $f:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ and $0<\sigma\le\tau$. For $n\ne0$ set $P_nz=z-n(n\cdot z)/|n|^2$, and set $P_0=I$. Let $\hat f(n)=\int_{[0,1]^3}e^{-2\pi i n\cdot x}f(x)\,dx$. Write $F(r)$ for the unit-periodic projected heat field with Fourier coefficients $e^{-4\pi^2r|n|^2}P_n\hat f(n)$, and measure it in the inhomogeneous periodic norm $\sum_n(1+4\pi^2|n|^2)|\hat F(n)|^2$ under a square root. The formal statement proves $F(\tau)=e^{(\tau-\sigma)\Delta}F(\sigma)$. Thus taking $\sigma=r$, $\tau=r+t$ gives the heat-shift law for $r>0,t\ge0$. It is stated for every $f$ using the total Fourier integrals, which are zero if integrability fails; for $f\in L^1([0,1]^3)$ the formula has its usual analytic meaning. The identity holds on the fixed unit torus and does not assert a spatial scaling law. The mean is retained by $P_0=I$; the paper’s Lemma 3.7 assumes mean-zero forcing and quantifies over all periods.
Breakdown.Periodic.Forced.Internal.force.summary: For $0<\sigma\le\tau$, the unit-periodic projected heat field $F(r)$ with coefficients $e^{-4\pi^2r|n|^2}P_n\hat f(n)$ satisfies $F(\tau)=e^{(\tau-\sigma)\Delta}F(\sigma)$, the heat-shift law on the unit torus. No spatial scaling law is asserted.

Breakdown.Periodic.FreeHeatComparison.text: For a field $f$ with the indicated local integrability, write $\mathcal R_bf=(1_{\overline B_b}\partial_1f,1_{\overline B_b}\partial_2f,1_{\overline B_b}\partial_3f,1_{\overline B_b}f)$ and use the norm $\max\{\max_i\|\partial_if\|_{L^2(B_b)},\|f\|_{L^6(B_b)}\}$. The restrictions are extended by zero outside the ball. For a unit-periodic field $z$, its scaled restriction consists of $\mu^{3/4}\partial_i z(a+\sqrt\mu\,y)$ and $\mu^{1/4}z(a+\sqrt\mu\,y)$ on the same ball, where $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$. It is assigned zero unless $0<\mu\le1$, $b>0$ and $\sqrt\mu b\le1/8$. For sufficiently small positive $\mu$ these inequalities hold. Let $\varphi$ be a smooth compactly supported divergence-free field on $\mathbb R^3$. Form its unit-periodic transplant by copying $\mu^{-1/2}\varphi((x-a)/\sqrt\mu)$ into the unit cell and periodically extending it. The formal assertion is: for every $b,\varepsilon,\delta>0$, there exists $\mu_0>0$ such that for $0<\mu<\mu_0$ and every $\tau\in[0,\varepsilon^{-1}]$, the scaled restriction of $\mu^{1/4}e^{\mu\tau\Delta_{\mathbb T^3}}$ applied to this transplant differs from $\mathcal R_b(e^{\tau\Delta_{\mathbb R^3}}\varphi)$ by at most $\delta$ in that product norm. All function-space identifications are up to almost-everywhere equality. The assertion is uniform over the displayed compact time interval for each fixed datum. It gives an arbitrarily small local error as $\mu\to0^+$; it gives no explicit power of $L$. Equation (6.3) bounds the gradient $L^2$ plus velocity $L^6$ error on $Q_L$ by $CL^{-5/2}\|f\|_1$. Applied to the cutoff datum, whose $L^1$ norm is $O(L^2)$, this yields the $O(L^{-1/2})$ error quoted in the introduction. The relation with the large-period picture is $L=\mu^{-1/2}$. The target is the full product $(L^2)^3\times L^6$, with the maximum norm. For a general tuple $(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$ it requires neither $A_i=\partial_i v$ nor $\operatorname{div}v=0$. The paper’s local space consists of actual solenoidal fields on a ball and uses the sum of the gradient and velocity norms; identifying these local descriptions is an additional restriction and norm comparison.
Breakdown.Periodic.FreeHeatComparison.summary: Defines local convergence of the rescaled periodic free heat flow for each compact smooth solenoidal datum, uniformly on a compact forward time interval. It gives no explicit power of the period, unlike the bound $CL^{-5/2}\|f\|_1$ in (6.3).

Breakdown.Periodic.GlueMild.text:
The periodic space is the real solenoidal Fourier realization of $H^1(\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3)$, with squared norm $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+4\pi^2|k|^2)|\widehat v(k)|^2$. Its zero Fourier coefficient is allowed to be nonzero.

Assume $\|K_{\mathbb T}(\tau)\|\le C_{\mathbb T}\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$ with $C_{\mathbb T}>0$, $0<T\le1$, $0<\lambda<1$, and continuous curves $v_n:[0,1-\lambda]\to H^1_{\mathrm{div}}(\mathbb T^3)$. Put $\mu_n=T\lambda^n$ and $t_n=T-\mu_n$. Suppose each $v_n$ satisfies the mild equation with heat flow $e^{\mu_ns\Delta}$ and kernel $\mu_n^{3/4}K_{\mathbb T}(\mu_n\tau)$, and $v_{n+1}(0)=\lambda^{1/4}v_n(1-\lambda)$.

The formal statement asserts that $u(t_n+\mu_ns)=\mu_n^{-1/4}v_n(s)$ defines a mild solution on $[0,T)$, and gives this equality also at both endpoints of every interval. A mild solution here is continuous in the periodic norm and satisfies the Duhamel equation with an integrable nonlinear term at each time. Each curve has domain $[0,1-\lambda]$. Its extension to real times takes the left or right endpoint value outside that interval. The assembled map is defined at every real time; its mild-solution assertion is restricted to $[0,T)$.

The formal statement records the assertion; its proof is separate.
Breakdown.Periodic.GlueMild.summary: States that if rescaled mild curves $v_n$ on $[0,1-\lambda]$ match by $v_{n+1}(0)=\lambda^{1/4}v_n(1-\lambda)$, then $u(t_n+\mu_ns)=\mu_n^{-1/4}v_n(s)$, with $\mu_n=T\lambda^n$, defines a periodic mild solution on $[0,T)$. This records the assertion only.

Breakdown.Periodic.GlueUnbounded.text: Let $V$ be the real Hilbert space of unit-periodic solenoidal Fourier states, with norm squared $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+4\pi^2|k|^2)|\widehat u(k)|^2$; zero mean is not required. Fix $T>0$, $0<\lambda<1$, $0<\theta<1$, $c_0>0$, and $Z\in\mathbb R$. For every integer $n\ge0$, let $u_n$, $\bar u_n$ and $z_n$ be continuous $V$-valued maps on $[0,1-\lambda]$. Assume $\|\bar u_n(s)\|\ge c_0$ for all $n,s$, $\sup_s\|z_n(s)\|\le Z$ for all $n$, and $u_n=\bar u_n+\theta^n z_n$. Put $a_n=T-T\lambda^n$ and $\mu_n=T\lambda^n$. On $[a_n,a_{n+1})$, define the joined curve by $U(t)=\mu_n^{-1/4}u_n((t-a_n)/\mu_n)$. The formal statement concludes that $\{\|U(t)\|:0\le t<T\}$ is unbounded above. The powers $\lambda^n$ and $\theta^n$ have nonnegative integer exponents. The positive parameters ensure that all divisions and logarithms used to select the interval are legitimate on $[0,T)$. Continuous pieces are extended by their endpoint values when evaluated outside their interval; these values are irrelevant on the stated pieces. No matching of endpoints or mild equation is assumed here, so neither continuity of $U$ nor its being a solution is part of this conclusion. This is a geometric unboundedness criterion, stated as a proposition; its proof is a separate theorem.
Breakdown.Periodic.GlueUnbounded.summary: If continuous pieces $u_n=\bar u_n+\theta^nz_n$ have $\|\bar u_n\|\ge c_0$ and $\sup\|z_n\|\le Z$, the joined curve $U(t)=\mu_n^{-1/4}u_n((t-a_n)/\mu_n)$ with $\mu_n=T\lambda^n$ has $\|U(t)\|$ unbounded on $[0,T)$. Neither continuity of $U$ nor a mild equation is part of this.

Breakdown.Periodic.HeatDivFreeComparison.text: For a field $f$ with the indicated local integrability, write $\mathcal R_bf=(1_{\overline B_b}\partial_1f,1_{\overline B_b}\partial_2f,1_{\overline B_b}\partial_3f,1_{\overline B_b}f)$ and use the norm $\max\{\max_i\|\partial_if\|_{L^2(B_b)},\|f\|_{L^6(B_b)}\}$. The restrictions are extended by zero outside the ball. For a unit-periodic field $z$, its scaled restriction consists of $\mu^{3/4}\partial_i z(a+\sqrt\mu\,y)$ and $\mu^{1/4}z(a+\sqrt\mu\,y)$ on the same ball, where $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$. It is assigned zero unless $0<\mu\le1$, $b>0$ and $\sqrt\mu b\le1/8$. For sufficiently small positive $\mu$ these inequalities hold. For $A\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ vanishing almost everywhere outside $\overline B_{b'}$, periodically extend $A((x-a)/\sqrt\mu)$ from the unit cell and apply $e^{\mu\tau\Delta_{\mathbb T^3}}\mathbb P$. The formal assertion is: for every $b,b',\varepsilon,\delta>0$ there exists $\mu_0>0$ such that for $0<\mu<\mu_0$ and every $\tau\in[\varepsilon,\varepsilon^{-1}]$, the scaled restriction of $\mu^{-1/4}$ times this field differs from $\mathcal R_b(e^{\tau\Delta_{\mathbb R^3}}\mathbb PA)$ by at most $\delta\|A\|_{L^{3/2}}$. Compact support and $A\in L^2$ ensure that the $L^{3/2}$ norm is finite. The threshold is uniform over all such $A$. When $\varepsilon>1$ the displayed time interval is empty. The statement is a local operator convergence estimate away from zero heat time; it states no explicit power of $L$. Equation (6.2) concerns $\mathbb P\operatorname{div}F$, for a compactly supported tensor $F\in W^{1,1}$, and bounds the error on $Q_L$ by $CL^{-7/2}\|F\|_1$. The formal input here is a compactly supported vector $A\in L^2$ and its bound uses $\|A\|_{3/2}$. Applied in the paper to $F=\bar u\otimes\bar u$ with $\|F\|_1=O(L)$, (6.2) yields the $O(L^{-5/2})$ nonlinear-term error quoted in the introduction. Large period corresponds to $L=\mu^{-1/2}$. The target is the full product $(L^2)^3\times L^6$, with the maximum norm. For a general tuple $(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$ it requires neither $A_i=\partial_i v$ nor $\operatorname{div}v=0$. The paper’s local space consists of actual solenoidal fields on a ball and uses the sum of the gradient and velocity norms; identifying these local descriptions is an additional restriction and norm comparison.
Breakdown.Periodic.HeatDivFreeComparison.summary: Defines a local comparison: for small $\mu$ and $\tau\in[\varepsilon,\varepsilon^{-1}]$, the rescaled periodic projected heat flow of a transplanted $A\in L^2$ supported in $\overline B_{b'}$ is within $\delta\|A\|_{3/2}$ of $e^{\tau\Delta}\mathbb PA$ on $B_b$. Paper (6.2) has $CL^{-7/2}\|F\|_1$.

Breakdown.Periodic.InverseAlgebra.Intern.text: Let $Y$ be a real Banach space, $A:Y\to Y$ a bounded linear operator, and $q\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $\|A\|\le q<1$. The formal statement proves $\|(I-A)^{-1}\|\le(1-q)^{-1}$. In particular $q\ge0$ follows from $\|A\|\ge0$, and the denominator $1-q$ is strictly positive, so the convention that division by zero is zero is irrelevant here. The inverse is bounded and linear. For the Volterra equation of Lemma 3.4, this estimate is applicable after the integral operator has been made small. The formal statement does not supply the exponentially weighted norm argument that treats an arbitrary interval and an arbitrary continuous background.
Breakdown.Periodic.InverseAlgebra.Intern.summary: If $A$ is bounded linear on a real Banach space with $\|A\|\le q<1$, then $\|(I-A)^{-1}\|\le(1-q)^{-1}$. It does not supply the weighted-norm argument for arbitrary intervals in Lemma 3.4.

Breakdown.Periodic.InverseAlgebra.Intern.text: Let $Y$ be any real Banach space and let $A:Y\to Y$ be bounded and linear with $\|A\|<1$. For every $g\in Y$, the formal statement proves that $h=(I-A)^{-1}g$ satisfies $h-Ah=g$. Here the inverse is the bounded linear inverse supplied by the norm-smallness hypothesis. The convention of assigning zero to a noninvertible operator's inverse has no effect because $\|A\|<1$ makes $I-A$ invertible. Taking $Y=C([a,b];\mathcal X)$ and $Ah(t)=2\int_a^tK(t-s)(f(s),h(s))\,ds$ gives the local inverse used for a linearized equation once $\|A\|<1$ has been proved. This formal statement contains no assertion that the integral operator has norm less than one for every $a,b,f$.
Breakdown.Periodic.InverseAlgebra.Intern.summary: If $\|A\|<1$ on a real Banach space, then $h=(I-A)^{-1}g$ satisfies $h-Ah=g$ for every $g$. It does not assert that the linearized integral operator has norm less than one.

Breakdown.Periodic.IsMildOn.text: The formal periodic space represents real divergence-free fields of period one by sequences $a(n)\in\mathbb C^3$, $n\in\mathbb Z^3$, with $\sum_n|a(n)|^2<\infty$, $a(-n)=\overline{a(n)}$ and $n\cdot a(n)=0$. The physical Fourier coefficient is $c(n)=a(n)/(1+4\pi^2|n|^2)^{1/2}$. Its squared norm is $\|u\|^2=\sum_n(1+4\pi^2|n|^2)|c(n)|^2$, the inhomogeneous $H^1$ norm; the mean $c(0)$ may be nonzero. For finite real numbers $a,b$, a curve $u$ defined for all real times with values in this periodic space is a mild solution on $[a,b)$ if it is continuous there and, for every $t\in[a,b)$, the integral $\int_a^tK_{\mathbb T}(t-s)(u(s),u(s))\,ds$ is Bochner integrable in the formal periodic space and $u(t)=e^{(t-a)\Delta}u(a)+\int_a^tK_{\mathbb T}(t-s)(u(s),u(s))\,ds$. Here the heat operator has Fourier multiplier $e^{-4\pi^2(t-a)|n|^2}$, and $K_{\mathbb T}(\tau)$ is the symmetrized projected transport operator for $\tau>0$, with value zero for $\tau\le0$. No behavior at $b$ or outside $[a,b)$ is required. This definition concerns the unit torus with its inhomogeneous norm, whereas §3.6 works in mean-zero homogeneous spaces at arbitrary period.
Breakdown.Periodic.IsMildOn.summary: A curve in the period-one space with inhomogeneous $H^1$ norm (nonzero mean allowed) is mild on $[a,b)$ if continuous there and satisfies $u(t)=e^{(t-a)\Delta}u(a)+\int_a^tK_{\mathbb T}(t-s)(u(s),u(s))\,ds$ with Bochner integrability. §3.6 uses mean-zero homogeneous spaces at any period.

Breakdown.Periodic.IsMildOnIcc.text: The formal periodic space represents real divergence-free fields of period one by sequences $a(n)\in\mathbb C^3$, $n\in\mathbb Z^3$, with $\sum_n|a(n)|^2<\infty$, $a(-n)=\overline{a(n)}$ and $n\cdot a(n)=0$. The physical Fourier coefficient is $c(n)=a(n)/(1+4\pi^2|n|^2)^{1/2}$. Its squared norm is $\|u\|^2=\sum_n(1+4\pi^2|n|^2)|c(n)|^2$, the inhomogeneous $H^1$ norm; the mean $c(0)$ may be nonzero. For finite real numbers $a,b$, the formal condition on a curve $u$ defined for all real times with values in this periodic space requires continuity on $[a,b]$ and the identity $u(t)=e^{(t-a)\Delta}u(a)+\int_a^tK_{\mathbb T}(t-s)(u(s),u(s))\,ds$ for every $t\in[a,b]$, including both endpoints. Each integral must be Bochner integrable in the formal periodic space. The heat multiplier is $e^{-4\pi^2(t-a)|n|^2}$, and the bilinear operator is the Fourier form of $K_{\mathbb T}(\tau)(u,v)=-\tfrac12e^{\tau\Delta}\mathbb P[(u\cdot\nabla)v+(v\cdot\nabla)u]$ for $\tau>0$. Its assigned value zero for $\tau\le0$ has no effect at the integration endpoint. The curve is defined for all real times, with no conditions outside $[a,b]$. The norm and mean convention differ from the homogeneous spaces of §3.6.
Breakdown.Periodic.IsMildOnIcc.summary: A curve in the period-one space with inhomogeneous $H^1$ norm is mild on $[a,b]$ if continuous there and $u(t)=e^{(t-a)\Delta}u(a)+\int_a^tK_{\mathbb T}(t-s)(u(s),u(s))\,ds$ with Bochner integrability for every $t\in[a,b]$. The norm and mean convention differ from §3.6.

Breakdown.Periodic.IsPeriodic.text: For any function $f:\mathbb R^3\to E$, with arbitrary target set $E$, the formal condition is $f(x+e_i)=f(x)$ for every $x\in\mathbb R^3$ and each of the three coordinate unit vectors $e_i$. No regularity or integrability is included. The function remains defined on all of $\mathbb R^3$; the condition identifies values at integer translates and therefore represents a function on $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$. The period is fixed at one. For a field of period $L>0$ in the paper, the change of variables $x=Lz$ makes $z\mapsto f(Lz)$ period one, but $L$ is not a parameter of this formal condition.
Breakdown.Periodic.IsPeriodic.summary: A function $f$ on $\mathbb R^3$ satisfies $f(x+e_i)=f(x)$ for all $x$ and each coordinate unit vector $e_i$, so it represents a function on $\mathbb T^3$. The period is fixed at one; a general period $L$ is not a parameter.

Breakdown.Periodic.KernelSharpBound.text: The formal periodic space represents real divergence-free fields of period one by sequences $a(n)\in\mathbb C^3$, $n\in\mathbb Z^3$, with $\sum_n|a(n)|^2<\infty$, $a(-n)=\overline{a(n)}$ and $n\cdot a(n)=0$. The physical Fourier coefficient is $c(n)=a(n)/(1+4\pi^2|n|^2)^{1/2}$. Its squared norm is $\|u\|^2=\sum_n(1+4\pi^2|n|^2)|c(n)|^2$, the inhomogeneous $H^1$ norm; the mean $c(0)$ may be nonzero. The assertion is that one constant $C>0$ satisfies $\|K_{\mathbb T}(\tau)(u,v)\|\le C\tau^{-3/4}\|u\|\|v\|$ for all inputs and $0<\tau\le1$. Equivalently it bounds the norm of the bounded bilinear map by $C\tau^{-3/4}$. The map has Fourier coefficients of $-\tfrac12e^{\tau\Delta}\mathbb P[(u\cdot\nabla)v+(v\cdot\nabla)u]$. The constant is independent of the two fields and of $\tau$ in this interval. Equation (3.20) instead quantifies all $\tau>0$ and all torus periods $L>0$, with homogeneous mean-zero norms. The formal statement of the bound supplies neither those additional quantifiers nor the separate linear-forcing estimate (3.19).
Breakdown.Periodic.KernelSharpBound.summary: States that one $C>0$ gives $\|K_{\mathbb T}(\tau)(u,v)\|\le C\tau^{-3/4}\|u\|\|v\|$ for $0<\tau\le1$ in the period-one inhomogeneous $H^1$ space. (3.20) instead covers all $\tau>0$ and all periods $L$ with homogeneous mean-zero norms.

Breakdown.Periodic.R3Factor.text:
The whole-space norm is $\|v\|_X=\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3)}$ on solenoidal velocities in $L^6(\mathbb R^3)$.

Local data are a tuple $(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$ with $A_j\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ and $v\in L^6(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$, measured by $\max\{\max_j\|A_j\|_2,\|v\|_6\}$. No compatibility condition $A_j=\partial_jv$ or divergence condition is part of this data space.

Let $\varphi\in C^\infty_{c,\mathrm{div}}(\mathbb R^3)$ have support in $\bar B_b$, let $\tau>0$, and let $v\in X$.

The formal statement asserts $2K(\tau)(\varphi,v)=-e^{\tau\Delta}\mathbb P[1_{\bar B_b}\sum_j(\varphi_j\partial_jv+v_j\partial_j\varphi)]$. On the right the derivative and velocity entries are supplied by restriction to the ball. This is the fixed-lag bilinear identity underlying the first formula of (6.9); the displayed formula in the paper has also been integrated in time. The assertion has no time-dependent curve as an input.

This declaration records the assertion; its proof is a separate declaration.
Breakdown.Periodic.R3Factor.summary: States that for a test field $\varphi$ supported in $\bar B_b$, $\tau>0$ and $v\in X$, $2K(\tau)(\varphi,v)=-e^{\tau\Delta}\mathbb P[1_{\bar B_b}\sum_j(\varphi_j\partial_jv+v_j\partial_j\varphi)]$. This fixed-lag identity underlies the first formula of (6.9), which also integrates in time.

Breakdown.Periodic.RestrictR3Bound.text:
The whole-space norm is $\|v\|_X=\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3)}$ on solenoidal velocities in $L^6(\mathbb R^3)$.

Local data are a tuple $(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$ with $A_j\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ and $v\in L^6(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$, measured by $\max\{\max_j\|A_j\|_2,\|v\|_6\}$. No compatibility condition $A_j=\partial_jv$ or divergence condition is part of this data space.

The restriction of a whole-space velocity to a radius $b$ is encoded by the three fields $1_{\bar B_b}\partial_jv$ and the field $1_{\bar B_b}v$.

The formal statement asserts that there is $C\ge0$ with operator norm at most $C$ for every real $b$. This includes $b\le0$, where the restriction is zero as an equivalence class for Lebesgue measure.

The paper uses $\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(B)}+\|v\|_{L^6(B)}$; the finite product norm here is a maximum of component norms. These norms are equivalent with constants depending only on the three spatial directions.

This declaration records the assertion; its proof is a separate declaration.
Breakdown.Periodic.RestrictR3Bound.summary: States that one $C\ge0$ bounds the operator norm of restriction $v\mapsto(1_{\bar B_b}\partial_jv,1_{\bar B_b}v)$ for every real $b$. The norm is a maximum of components, equivalent to the paper's $\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(B)}+\|v\|_{L^6(B)}$.

Breakdown.Periodic.SeqPerturbation.text:
Let $X,E$ be real Banach spaces. For each integer $n\ge0$, let $G_n$ be a strongly continuous contraction heat semigroup and $K_n$ a continuous symmetric bilinear kernel satisfying $G_n(s)K_n(\tau)=K_n(s+\tau)$ for $s\ge0$, $\tau>0$, with $\|K_n(\tau)\|\le C_K\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$, where $C_K\ge0$ is independent of $n$. Fix $0<\ell\le1$, $0<\theta<1$, a real endpoint factor $c$, bounded linear $J:E\to X$, and continuous interval curves $a_n,r_n:[0,\ell]\to X$. Assume $\|a_n\|_\infty\le M$, $a_{n+1}(0)=c\,a_n(\ell)$, $a_n=G_n(\cdot)a_n(0)+\mathcal B_n(a_n,a_n)+r_n$, and $\|r_n\|_\infty\le\theta^n\rho$. Here $\mathcal B_n(f,g)(s)=\int_0^sK_n(s-\sigma)(f(\sigma),g(\sigma))\,d\sigma$.

Suppose a bounded linear map $R$ takes each bounded interval sequence $g$ to $(e,z)$ satisfying $z_n-2\mathcal B_n(a_n,z_n)-G_n(\cdot)Je=g_0$ for $n=0$, and $z_n-2\mathcal B_n(a_n,z_n)-(c/\theta)G_n(\cdot)z_{n-1}(\ell)=g_n$ for $n\ge1$.

For a datum displacement $\xi\in X$, assume $64\|R\|^2C_K\ell^{1/4}(\rho+\|\xi\|)\le1$.

The formal statement asserts an $e$ and curves $z_n$ with $\|e\|,\sup_n\|z_n\|_\infty\le2\|R\|(\rho+\|\xi\|)$, such that, on writing $v_n=a_n+\theta^nz_n$, each $v_n$ satisfies $v_n(s)=G_n(s)v_n(0)+\mathcal B_n(v_n,v_n)(s)$ on the closed interval, with an integrable nonlinear term. Moreover $v_{n+1}(0)=c\,v_n(\ell)$ and $z_0(0)=\xi+Je$. The sequence norm is the supremum over the interval index and time, and the product norm is the maximum of its two factor norms. The positive hypotheses exclude zero denominators.

This formal statement specifies an implication. Defining the implication does not prove it.

Finite dimensionality of $E$ is not assumed. The separate bounds on the residual and datum displacement do not retain possible cancellation in the paper's combined forcing $e^{t\Delta}\chi-F^{\mathrm a}$.
Breakdown.Periodic.SeqPerturbation.summary: States that if approximate curves $a_n$ have residuals at most $\theta^n\rho$ and the linear interval equations have a bounded right inverse $R$ with $64\|R\|^2C_K\ell^{1/4}(\rho+\|\xi\|)\le1$, then corrections $z_n$ make $v_n=a_n+\theta^nz_n$ exact matched mild curves with $z_0(0)=\xi+Je$.

Breakdown.Periodic.ShellData.text:
Local data are a tuple $(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$ with $A_j\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ and $v\in L^6(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$, measured by $\max\{\max_j\|A_j\|_2,\|v\|_6\}$. No compatibility condition $A_j=\partial_jv$ or divergence condition is part of this data space.

The entries are equivalence classes modulo equality almost everywhere for Lebesgue measure. In the paper they come from restricting a single $H^1(B)$ velocity to the ball and then extending its value and derivative entries by zero. The formal space also allows tuples that are not derivatives of one common field. Whenever the zero extension is used, its first three entries record the extended derivatives inside the ball; they are not asserted to be distributional derivatives of the zero-extended velocity.
Breakdown.Periodic.ShellData.summary: Local data are tuples $(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$ with $A_j\in L^2$ and $v\in L^6$, normed by $\max\{\max_j\|A_j\|_2,\|v\|_6\}$. Unlike the paper's restriction of one $H^1(B)$ velocity, the tuples need not satisfy $A_j=\partial_jv$ or any divergence condition.

Breakdown.Periodic.ShellInverseTransfer.text:
Let $E,Y,Y_{\mathbb T},Z$ be real Banach spaces. Take bounded linear maps $S:Y\to Y$, $G:E\to Y$, $B:Z\to Y$, $R:Y\to Z$, and corresponding bounded linear periodic maps $S_{\mathbb T},G_{\mathbb T},B_{\mathbb T},R_{\mathbb T}$. Define $\mathcal L(e,y)=y-Sy-Ge-BRy$ and its periodic counterpart. Assume $0\le q<1$, $\|S\|,\|S_{\mathbb T}\|\le q$, and a bounded linear right inverse $F:Y\to E\times Y$ with $\mathcal LF=I$ and $\|F\|\le K$. Suppose the two operator differences $R_{\mathbb T}(I-S_{\mathbb T})^{-1}B_{\mathbb T}-R(I-S)^{-1}B$ and $R_{\mathbb T}(I-S_{\mathbb T})^{-1}G_{\mathbb T}-R(I-S)^{-1}G$ each have norm at most $\delta$, and $4\delta[1+K\|B\|(1+\|R\|)]\le1$.

The formal statement asserts an exact periodic right inverse $F_{\mathbb T}$ with norm at most $(1-q)^{-1}\{1+2(\|B_{\mathbb T}\|+\|G_{\mathbb T}\|+1)[1+K\|B\|(1+\|R\|)]\|R_{\mathbb T}\|(1-q)^{-1}\}$. Product spaces use the maximum norm.

The strict contraction hypotheses make the displayed inverses ordinary bounded inverses and make $1-q$ nonzero. This transfers an inverse through local comparisons; it does not assert the paper’s formula (6.12) or its explicit defect rate.

This declaration records the assertion; its proof is a separate declaration.
Breakdown.Periodic.ShellInverseTransfer.summary: States that if $\|S\|,\|S_{\mathbb T}\|\le q<1$, $\mathcal L$ has a right inverse of norm at most $K$, and both localized operator differences are at most $\delta$ with $4\delta[1+K\|B\|(1+\|R\|)]\le1$, the periodic operator has an exact right inverse with explicit bound. Not (6.12).

Breakdown.Periodic.ShellTorus.Internal.s.text: Assume there is $C_S>0$ such that $\|\sum_{n\in F}e^{2\pi in\cdot x}c_n\|_{L^6([0,1]^3)}\le C_S(\sum_{n\in F}(1+4\pi^2|n|^2)|c_n|^2)^{1/2}$ for every finite $F\subset\mathbb Z^3$ and every $c_n\in\mathbb C^3$. The formal statement then supplies one $C\ge0$ such that the following holds. Let $0<\mu\le1$, $b>0$, $\sqrt\mu\,b\le1/8$, $\tau>0$ and $\mu\tau\le1$. Let $A\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ vanish almost everywhere outside the closed ball of radius $b$. Place $A$ in the unit cell by $f_\mu(x)=A((x-c)/\sqrt\mu)$, $c=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$, and extend it periodically. The support restriction ensures that the copy lies inside the cell. Then $\|e^{\mu\tau\Delta}\mathbb P f_\mu\|_{H^1(\mathbb T^3)}\le C\mu^{1/4}\tau^{-3/4}\|A\|_{L^{3/2}(\mathbb R^3)}$. Compact support of $A\in L^2$ gives the finite $L^{3/2}$ norm. The output norm is inhomogeneous and no mean-zero assumption is made. The constant is independent of $\mu,b,\tau,A$ under these hypotheses. This is a localized, rescaled forcing estimate; (3.19) is asserted for all mean-zero $L^{3/2}$ forces on every torus and every positive time.
Breakdown.Periodic.ShellTorus.Internal.s.summary: Assuming the finite Fourier-sum $L^6$ bound, one $C$ gives $\|e^{\mu\tau\Delta}\mathbb Pf_\mu\|_{H^1(\mathbb T^3)}\le C\mu^{1/4}\tau^{-3/4}\|A\|_{3/2}$ for a transplant of $A\in L^2$ supported in $B_b$, when $\sqrt\mu b\le1/8$ and $\mu\tau\le1$. (3.19) covers all mean-zero forces on every torus.

Breakdown.Periodic.SourceCont.Internal.f.text: Set $P_nz=z-n(n\cdot z)/|n|^2$ for $n\ne0$ and $P_0=I$. For a fixed field $f:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$, let $F(\tau)$ have Fourier coefficients $e^{-4\pi^2\tau|n|^2}P_n\hat f(n)$ for $\tau>0$, with $\hat f$ integrated on $[0,1]^3$, and use the inhomogeneous unit-torus norm $(\sum_n(1+4\pi^2|n|^2)|\hat F(n)|^2)^{1/2}$. The formal statement proves continuity of $\tau\mapsto F(\tau)$ on $(0,\infty)$. It imposes no regularity assumption on $f$ because the Fourier integrals are assigned zero if they are not Bochner integrable. For integrable fields it is continuity of the projected heat flow. There is no assertion of continuity at $\tau=0$, nor of a norm estimate uniform over arbitrary torus periods. The retained zero Fourier mode allows nonzero means, while Lemma 3.7 imposes zero mean and also treats every spatial period.
Breakdown.Periodic.SourceCont.Internal.f.summary: For a fixed field $f$, $\tau\mapsto F(\tau)$ with coefficients $e^{-4\pi^2\tau|n|^2}P_n\hat f(n)$ is continuous on $(0,\infty)$ in the inhomogeneous unit-torus norm. Continuity at $\tau=0$ is not asserted.

Breakdown.Periodic.TestLiftExists.text:
The whole-space norm is $\|v\|_X=\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3)}$ on solenoidal velocities in $L^6(\mathbb R^3)$.

Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real normed space and let $J:E\to X$ be bounded linear. Assume every $Je$ belongs to the linear span of the embedded fields in $C^\infty_{c,\mathrm{div}}(\mathbb R^3)$.

The formal statement asserts the existence of $b>0$ and a linear assignment $e\mapsto\psi_e:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ such that every $\psi_e$ is smooth, compactly supported and solenoidal, $\operatorname{supp}\psi_e\subset\bar B_b$, and its whole-space Fourier representation equals $Je$. The conclusion provides a common support and exact representation. It does not state an $L^1$ norm bound.

This declaration records the assertion; its proof is a separate declaration.
Breakdown.Periodic.TestLiftExists.summary: States that if $E$ is finite-dimensional and every $Je$ lies in the span of embedded test fields, there are $b>0$ and a linear $e\mapsto\psi_e$ of smooth compactly supported solenoidal fields supported in $\bar B_b$ representing $Je$. No $L^1$ bound is stated.

Breakdown.Periodic.TorusBlowup.text: The formal statement defines an existence assertion on the unit torus. There are a smooth field $u_0:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ with period one in each coordinate and zero divergence, a real $T>0$, and a continuous mild curve $u$ on $[0,T)$ whose initial state is the Fourier representation of $u_0$, such that $\sup_{0\le t<T}\|u(t)\|=\infty$. The periodic state has coordinates $\sqrt{1+4\pi^2|k|^2}\,\widehat u(k)$, $k\in\mathbb Z^3$, with conjugate symmetry and $k\cdot\widehat u(k)=0$; its norm is the inhomogeneous $H^1$ norm on the unit cell. The zero coefficient is allowed, so this state space does not impose zero mean. The initial-field map returns zero outside its admissible Fourier class; smooth periodic solenoidal data belong to that class. Mild means the heat-plus-quadratic Bochner equation for every $0\le t<T$, with convergent time integrals. The assertion imposes neither $T\le1$ nor either estimate in (2.6), gives no local comparison on $B_{1/16}$, and states unboundedness rather than a specified limit or rate at $T$. It contains no smooth velocity-pressure representative of the curve. This declaration states the existence condition; a separate construction proves it from a profile.
Breakdown.Periodic.TorusBlowup.summary: Defines the assertion that some smooth period-one divergence-free $u_0$, some $T>0$ and a continuous mild curve on $[0,T)$ from $u_0$ have $\sup_{0\le t<T}\|u(t)\|=\infty$ in inhomogeneous $H^1$. It imposes neither $T\le1$ nor (2.6), and gives no rate.

Breakdown.Periodic.TorusFactor.text:
The periodic space is the real solenoidal Fourier realization of $H^1(\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3)$, with squared norm $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+4\pi^2|k|^2)|\widehat v(k)|^2$. Its zero Fourier coefficient is allowed to be nonzero.

Local data are a tuple $(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$ with $A_j\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ and $v\in L^6(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$, measured by $\max\{\max_j\|A_j\|_2,\|v\|_6\}$. No compatibility condition $A_j=\partial_jv$ or divergence condition is part of this data space.

Write $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$ and let $w(x)$ reduce each coordinate of $x$ modulo integers to the cell centered at $a$. For $\mu>0$, the transplanted field is $g_\mu(x)=\mu^{-1/2}g((w(x)-a)/\sqrt\mu)$.

Whole-space restriction to $\bar B_b$ consists of $1_{\bar B_b}\partial_jv$ and $1_{\bar B_b}v$. At an admissible periodic scale $0<\mu\le1$, $b>0$, $\sqrt\mu\,b\le1/8$, periodic restriction consists of $1_{\bar B_b}\mu^{3/4}\partial_jz(a+\sqrt\mu\,y)$ and $1_{\bar B_b}\mu^{1/4}z(a+\sqrt\mu\,y)$, interpreted almost everywhere. It is defined to be zero if these scale conditions fail.

Let $\varphi\in C^\infty_{c,\mathrm{div}}(\mathbb R^3)$ have support in $\bar B_b$, suppose $0<\mu\le1$, $b>0$, $\sqrt\mu b\le1/8$, and let $\tau>0$ and $z\in H^1_{\mathrm{div}}(\mathbb T^3)$.

The formal statement asserts $2\mu^{3/4}K_{\mathbb T}(\mu\tau)(\mu^{1/4}\varphi_\mu,z)=\Lambda_{\mathbb T}(\tau)(R_{\mu,b}z)$. Here $R_{\mu,b}$ is the scaled local restriction just described, and $\Lambda_{\mathbb T}(\tau)\zeta=-\mu^{-1/4}e^{\mu\tau\Delta}\mathbb P[f_\zeta((w(x)-a)/\sqrt\mu)]$, with $f_\zeta=1_{\bar B_b}\sum_j(\varphi_jA_j+v_j\partial_j\varphi)$. This is a fixed-lag identity; the second identity in (6.9) also integrates in time.

This declaration records the assertion; its proof is a separate declaration.
Breakdown.Periodic.TorusFactor.summary: States that for a test field $\varphi$ in $\bar B_b$, admissible $\mu$, $\tau>0$ and $z\in H^1_{\mathrm{div}}(\mathbb T^3)$, $2\mu^{3/4}K_{\mathbb T}(\mu\tau)(\mu^{1/4}\varphi_\mu,z)=\Lambda_{\mathbb T}(\tau)(R_{\mu,b}z)$. It is fixed-lag; the second identity in (6.9) also integrates in time.

Breakdown.Periodic.TorusLiftExists.text:
The whole-space norm is $\|v\|_X=\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3)}$ on solenoidal velocities in $L^6(\mathbb R^3)$.

The periodic space is the real solenoidal Fourier realization of $H^1(\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3)$, with squared norm $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+4\pi^2|k|^2)|\widehat v(k)|^2$. Its zero Fourier coefficient is allowed to be nonzero.

Write $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$ and let $w(x)$ reduce each coordinate of $x$ modulo integers to the cell centered at $a$. For $\mu>0$, the transplanted field is $g_\mu(x)=\mu^{-1/2}g((w(x)-a)/\sqrt\mu)$.

Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real normed space, let $J:E\to X$ be bounded linear, and let $e\mapsto\psi_e$ be a linear assignment of smooth compactly supported solenoidal fields, all supported in $\bar B_b$, whose whole-space representations equal $Je$. If $b>0$, $0<T\le1$ and $\sqrt T b\le1/8$, the formal statement asserts a bounded linear map $J_{\mathbb T}:E\to H^1_{\mathrm{div}}(\mathbb T^3)$ with $J_{\mathbb T}e=T^{1/4}(\psi_e)_T$ for every $e$. The amplitude factor and unit-periodic dilation differ from the paper’s unscaled map $\gamma\mapsto\Pi_L\gamma$. No equality of the whole-space and periodic norms is asserted.

This declaration records the assertion; its proof is a separate declaration.
Breakdown.Periodic.TorusLiftExists.summary: States that for $b>0$, $0<T\le1$ and $\sqrt Tb\le1/8$, there is a bounded linear $J_{\mathbb T}:E\to H^1_{\mathrm{div}}(\mathbb T^3)$ with $J_{\mathbb T}e=T^{1/4}(\psi_e)_T$. The amplitude factor and unit-periodic dilation differ from the paper's unscaled $\gamma\mapsto\Pi_L\gamma$.

Breakdown.Periodic.TransplantNorm.text:
Write $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$ and let $w(x)$ reduce each coordinate of $x$ modulo integers to the cell centered at $a$. For $\mu>0$, the transplanted field is $g_\mu(x)=\mu^{-1/2}g((w(x)-a)/\sqrt\mu)$.

The periodic space is the real solenoidal Fourier realization of $H^1(\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3)$, with squared norm $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+4\pi^2|k|^2)|\widehat v(k)|^2$. Its zero Fourier coefficient is allowed to be nonzero.

For every smooth solenoidal $g$ supported in $\bar B_b$, with $0<\mu\le1$, $b>0$ and $\sqrt\mu b\le1/8$, the formal statement asserts $\|\mu^{1/4}g_\mu\|_{H^1(\mathbb T^3)}^2=\int_{\mathbb R^3}|\nabla g|^2+\mu\int_{\mathbb R^3}|g|^2$. The gradient square is the sum of the squares of the three directional derivatives. Compact support and smoothness make these integrals finite. This identity includes an $L^2$ term and an amplitude normalization, whereas (6.1) concerns unscaled periodization and the homogeneous norm.

This declaration records the assertion; its proof is a separate declaration.
Breakdown.Periodic.TransplantNorm.summary: For smooth solenoidal $g$ supported in $\bar B_b$, $0<\mu\le1$, $\sqrt\mu b\le1/8$, the transplant satisfies $\|\mu^{1/4}g_\mu\|_{H^1(\mathbb T^3)}^2=\int|\nabla g|^2+\mu\int|g|^2$. Unlike (6.1), it includes an $L^2$ term and amplitude normalization; this records the assertion only.

Breakdown.Periodic.TrigHs.text: The assertion says that there is $C>0$ such that for every finite set $F\subset\mathbb Z^3$ and every family of coefficients $c(n)\in\mathbb C^3$, the polynomial $p(x)=\sum_{n\in F}e^{2\pi in\cdot x}c(n)$ satisfies $\|p\|_{L^6([0,1]^3)}\le C(\sum_{n\in F}(1+4\pi^2|n|^2)|c(n)|^2)^{1/2}$. The constant is independent of $F$ and the coefficients. There is no reality, divergence-free or mean-zero hypothesis. Both integrals and finite sums are ordinary ones, and the fractional powers are positive real powers. This is an inhomogeneous unit-torus estimate for finite Fourier sums. Equation (3.18) concerns all mean-zero fields with the homogeneous gradient norm, uniformly for every period $L>0$; that assertion is not the conclusion written here.
Breakdown.Periodic.TrigHs.summary: States that one $C>0$ gives $\|p\|_{L^6([0,1]^3)}\le C(\sum_{n\in F}(1+4\pi^2|n|^2)|c(n)|^2)^{1/2}$ for every finite Fourier sum $p$, with no reality, divergence or mean-zero hypothesis. (3.18) is a homogeneous estimate uniform in the period.

Breakdown.Periodic.V.text: The formal periodic space represents real divergence-free fields of period one by sequences $a(n)\in\mathbb C^3$, $n\in\mathbb Z^3$, with $\sum_n|a(n)|^2<\infty$, $a(-n)=\overline{a(n)}$ and $n\cdot a(n)=0$. The physical Fourier coefficient is $c(n)=a(n)/(1+4\pi^2|n|^2)^{1/2}$. Its squared norm is $\|u\|^2=\sum_n(1+4\pi^2|n|^2)|c(n)|^2$, the inhomogeneous $H^1$ norm; the mean $c(0)$ may be nonzero. The conjugate symmetry is the reality condition and $n\cdot a(n)=0$ is the divergence-free condition. At $n=0$ the latter gives no restriction, which is why nonzero constants are included. The space is a closed real subspace of $\ell^2(\mathbb Z^3;\mathbb C^3)$ and is complete. A nonzero constant has positive formal norm and zero gradient norm, so the mean-zero restriction is essential in (3.16). Equation (3.15) instead uses the homogeneous norm on mean-zero fields of arbitrary period $L$. The distinction matters: the zero Fourier mode contributes to the formal norm, and no variable spatial period is a parameter of an element of the formal space.
Breakdown.Periodic.V.summary: The period-one space of sequences $a(n)\in\mathbb C^3$, square summable, with $a(-n)=\overline{a(n)}$ and $n\cdot a(n)=0$, with inhomogeneous $H^1$ norm; nonzero constants are included. (3.15) instead uses the homogeneous norm on mean-zero fields of any period.

Breakdown.Periodic.advectShell.text:
Local data are a tuple $(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$ with $A_j\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ and $v\in L^6(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$, measured by $\max\{\max_j\|A_j\|_2,\|v\|_6\}$. No compatibility condition $A_j=\partial_jv$ or divergence condition is part of this data space.

Let $\varphi\in C^\infty_{c,\mathrm{div}}(\mathbb R^3)$ and $b\in\mathbb R$. For $\zeta=(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$, the formal definition forms $1_{\bar B_b}\sum_{j=1}^3(\varphi_jA_j+v_j\partial_j\varphi)$ as an $L^2$ vector field. Smoothness and compact support of $\varphi$ give bounded coefficients and make this construction meaningful. For restrictions of a field $v\in H^1(B)$ with $A_j=\partial_jv$ it is the paper’s $(\varphi\cdot\nabla)v+(v\cdot\nabla)\varphi$, extended by zero. General local data need not satisfy the compatibility or divergence assumptions used to write this as the divergence of a tensor.
Breakdown.Periodic.advectShell.summary: For a test field $\varphi$ and local data $\zeta=(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$, defines the $L^2$ field $1_{\bar B_b}\sum_j(\varphi_jA_j+v_j\partial_j\varphi)$. When $A_j=\partial_jv$ it is the paper's $(\varphi\cdot\nabla)v+(v\cdot\nabla)\varphi$ extended by zero.

Breakdown.Periodic.approxFieldProperties.text:

abla)W-\Delta W+(W\cdot
abla)W+
abla q=0$ and $
abla\cdot W=0$ for every $(s,y)$. Assume, uniformly in $s,y$, $\|D_y^jW(s,y)\|_{m op}\le C(1+|y|)^{-j-1}$ for the three integer orders $j=0,1,2$, and $|
abla_yq(s,y)|\le C(1+|y|)^{-3}$. These assumptions imply $C\ge0$; recurrence and nonvanishing are not required here. The norm on a first derivative is its operator norm; the paper's pointwise matrix norm is the square root of the sum of the squared column lengths, which is at most $\sqrt3$ times this norm.

Put $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$ and let $\chi$ be the fixed smooth cutoff with $0\le\chi\le1$, equal to one for $|x-a|\le1/16$ and zero for $|x-a|\ge1/8$. For $T>0$, $t<T$, set $\ell=T-t$, $s=-\log(\ell/T)$ and $g(x)=\ell^{-1/2}W(s,(x-a)/\sqrt\ell)$. Define $A_g(x)=\int_0^1\sigma\,g(a+\sigma(x-a))	imes(x-a)\,d\sigma$, $ ar u(x)=\chi(x)g(x)+
abla\chi(x)	imes A_g(x)$, and $f(y)=\sqrt\ell\, ar u(a+\sqrt\ell\,y)$. Thus $f$ is the cutoff expressed in similarity coordinates; its inner and outer radii are $1/(16\sqrt\ell)$ and $1/(8\sqrt\ell)$. Put $x_a=a+(3/32)e_1$ and $ ar p(x)=\chi(x)\ell^{-1}[q(s,(x-a)/\sqrt\ell)-q(s,(x_a-a)/\sqrt\ell)]$.

For every $T>0$, the formal statement proves that $(t,x)\mapsto ar u(t,x)$ is smooth on $(-\infty,T)	imes\mathbb R^3$, is divergence-free, vanishes for $|x-a|\ge1/8$, and equals $g$ for $|x-a|\le1/16$. It also proves smoothness and the same outer support for $ ar p(t,x)=\chi(x)[\ell^{-1}q(s,(x-a)/\sqrt\ell)-\ell^{-1}q(s,(x_a-a)/\sqrt\ell)]$, where $x_a=a+(3/32)e_1$ is fixed. Thus each spatial cutoff is in $C^\infty_{c,\mathrm{div}}$. The centre, radii, time interval and pressure normalization are fixed as stated; an arbitrary radius $r$ is absent from the assertion. All logarithms, square roots and quotients used for $t<T$, $T>0$ have their ordinary positive arguments. The result gives no quantitative norm estimate.
Breakdown.Periodic.approxFieldProperties.summary: For a profile with the decay bounds and every $T>0$, the cutoff $\bar u=\chi g+\nabla\chi\times A_g$ is smooth on $(-\infty,T)\times\mathbb R^3$, divergence-free, zero for $|x-a|\ge1/8$ and equal to $g$ for $|x-a|\le1/16$; $\bar p$ is smooth with the same support. No norm estimate is given.

Breakdown.Periodic.approxLinks_holds.text:
Assume that $W:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ and $q:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ are smooth, that $\operatorname{div}W=0$, and that $\partial_sW+\tfrac12W+\tfrac12(y\cdot\nabla)W-\Delta W+(W\cdot\nabla)W+\nabla q=0$ for every $(s,y)$. A single constant $C$ bounds $\|D^jW(s,y)\|\le C(1+|y|)^{-j-1}$ for the integer orders $j=0,1,2$, and $|\nabla q(s,y)|\le C(1+|y|)^{-3}$, uniformly in $s$. The norms of $D^jW$ are multilinear operator norms; for $j=1$ the paper’s Frobenius norm is between the operator norm and $\sqrt3$ times that norm.

The periodic space is the real solenoidal Fourier realization of $H^1(\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3)$, with squared norm $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+4\pi^2|k|^2)|\widehat v(k)|^2$. Its zero Fourier coefficient is allowed to be nonzero.

For $T>0$ and $t<T$, put $s=\log(T/(T-t))$ and $u_T^*(t,x)=(T-t)^{-1/2}W(s,(x-a)/\sqrt{T-t})$, where $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$. Choose a fixed smooth cutoff $\chi$, equal to one on $\bar B_{1/16}(a)$ and zero when $|x-a|\ge1/8$. Put $A_g(x)=\int_0^1\tau g(a+\tau(x-a))\times(x-a)\,d\tau$. The cutoff is $\bar u_T=\chi u_T^*+\nabla\chi\times A_{u_T^*}$, which equals $\operatorname{curl}(\chi A_{u_T^*})$ when $u_T^*$ is solenoidal.

Write $\mu_n=T\lambda^n$, $t_n=T-\mu_n$, $\ell=1-\lambda$, and $a_n(s)=\mu_n^{1/4}u^{\mathrm a}(t_n+\mu_ns)$ for $0\le s\le\ell$, where $u^{\mathrm a}$ is the unit-periodic extension of the solenoidal cutoff of the centered self-similar field. The index $n$ is a nonnegative integer and the interval norm is the supremum norm.

For $0<T\le1$ and $0<\lambda<1$, the formal statement proves the defining formula for every $a_n$ throughout $[0,\ell]$ and the endpoint identity $a_{n+1}(0)=\lambda^{1/4}a_n(\ell)$. The time intervals are $[T-T\lambda^n,T-T\lambda^{n+1}]$, and the factor in the endpoint identity comes from their amplitude normalizations. Values used outside a closed interval are extended by the endpoint values. This supplies the matching needed to assemble continuous physical curves.
Breakdown.Periodic.approxLinks_holds.summary: For $0<T\le1$ and $0<\lambda<1$, each $a_n$ has its defining formula on $[0,\ell]$ and $a_{n+1}(0)=\lambda^{1/4}a_n(\ell)$, on the intervals $[T-T\lambda^n,T-T\lambda^{n+1}]$. This supplies the matching needed to assemble continuous curves.

Breakdown.Periodic.approxPeriodic.text:
For $T>0$ and $t<T$, put $s=\log(T/(T-t))$ and $u_T^*(t,x)=(T-t)^{-1/2}W(s,(x-a)/\sqrt{T-t})$, where $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$. Choose a fixed smooth cutoff $\chi$, equal to one on $\bar B_{1/16}(a)$ and zero when $|x-a|\ge1/8$. Put $A_g(x)=\int_0^1\tau g(a+\tau(x-a))\times(x-a)\,d\tau$. The cutoff is $\bar u_T=\chi u_T^*+\nabla\chi\times A_{u_T^*}$, which equals $\operatorname{curl}(\chi A_{u_T^*})$ when $u_T^*$ is solenoidal.

The definition is $u^{\mathrm a}(t,x)=\bar u_T(t,w(x))$, where $w$ reduces coordinates modulo integers to the cell centered at $a$. It defines a function for every real $T,t$ and every field $W$. For smooth solenoidal similarity profiles and $T>0$, $t<T$, the cutoff is supported in $\bar B_{1/8}(a)$, so this formula periodizes a field that vanishes near the cell boundary. Its physical interpretation is therefore the paper’s approximate velocity after passage to the unit torus. Values outside $t<T$ are not part of that interpretation; the definition alone does not assert an evolution equation.
Breakdown.Periodic.approxPeriodic.summary: Defines $u^{\mathrm a}(t,x)=\bar u_T(t,w(x))$, the unit-periodic extension of the cutoff self-similar field, with $w$ reducing coordinates to the cell centred at $a$. For smooth profiles and $t<T$ it is the paper's approximate velocity on the unit torus; no evolution equation is asserted.

Breakdown.Periodic.approxResidualSmall.text:
This proof assumes four properties of the constructions for every smooth similarity profile satisfying the equation and derivative bounds stated below. The cutoff velocity and pressure are smooth for $t<T$, supported in the ball of radius $1/8$ about $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$, the velocity is solenoidal and agrees with the self-similar field on radius $1/16$. Its differential residual $F=\partial_t\bar u_T+(\bar u_T\cdot\nabla)\bar u_T-\Delta\bar u_T+\nabla p^{\mathrm a}$ satisfies $|F(t,x)|\le K(T-t)^{-1/2}$ for $0<T\le1$, $0\le t<T$, and vanishes outside $1/16\le|x-a|\le1/8$. The normalized approximate curves have the formula and endpoint matching $a_{n+1}(0)=\lambda^{1/4}a_n(1-\lambda)$. Finally, for every smooth solenoidal $g$ supported in $\bar B_b$ with $0<\mu\le1$, $b>0$ and $\sqrt\mu b\le1/8$, the field $g_\mu(x)=\mu^{-1/2}g((w(x)-a)/\sqrt\mu)$, where $w$ reduces coordinates to the unit cell centered at $a$, is smooth, unit-periodic and solenoidal, and agrees with its unwrapped dilation within radius $1/4$ about $a$. Here $p^{\mathrm a}(t,x)=\chi(x)[p^*(t,x)-p^*(t,a+(3/32)e_1)]$, with $p^*(t,x)=(T-t)^{-1}q(\log(T/(T-t)),(x-a)/\sqrt{T-t})$. The theorem proves the following interval residual estimate from these premises.

Assume that $W:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ and $q:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ are smooth, that $\operatorname{div}W=0$, and that $\partial_sW+\tfrac12W+\tfrac12(y\cdot\nabla)W-\Delta W+(W\cdot\nabla)W+\nabla q=0$ for every $(s,y)$. A single constant $C$ bounds $\|D^jW(s,y)\|\le C(1+|y|)^{-j-1}$ for the integer orders $j=0,1,2$, and $|\nabla q(s,y)|\le C(1+|y|)^{-3}$, uniformly in $s$. The norms of $D^jW$ are multilinear operator norms; for $j=1$ the paper’s Frobenius norm is between the operator norm and $\sqrt3$ times that norm.

The periodic space is the real solenoidal Fourier realization of $H^1(\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3)$, with squared norm $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+4\pi^2|k|^2)|\widehat v(k)|^2$. Its zero Fourier coefficient is allowed to be nonzero.

For $T>0$ and $t<T$, put $s=\log(T/(T-t))$ and $u_T^*(t,x)=(T-t)^{-1/2}W(s,(x-a)/\sqrt{T-t})$, where $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$. Choose a fixed smooth cutoff $\chi$, equal to one on $\bar B_{1/16}(a)$ and zero when $|x-a|\ge1/8$. Put $A_g(x)=\int_0^1\tau g(a+\tau(x-a))\times(x-a)\,d\tau$. The cutoff is $\bar u_T=\chi u_T^*+\nabla\chi\times A_{u_T^*}$, which equals $\operatorname{curl}(\chi A_{u_T^*})$ when $u_T^*$ is solenoidal.

Write $\mu_n=T\lambda^n$, $t_n=T-\mu_n$, $\ell=1-\lambda$, and $a_n(s)=\mu_n^{1/4}u^{\mathrm a}(t_n+\mu_ns)$ for $0\le s\le\ell$, where $u^{\mathrm a}$ is the unit-periodic extension of the solenoidal cutoff of the centered self-similar field. The index $n$ is a nonnegative integer and the interval norm is the supremum norm.

Assume the periodic heat-bilinear estimate $\|K_{\mathbb T}(\tau)\|\le C_{\mathbb T}\tau^{-3/4}$ for $0<\tau\le1$, $0<\lambda<1$, and $\theta>\lambda^{1/4}$. On interval $n$ use $G_n(s)=e^{\mu_ns\Delta}$ and $K_n(\tau)=\mu_n^{3/4}K_{\mathbb T}(\mu_n\tau)$, and let $\mathcal B_n$ be the resulting Duhamel integral.

The formal statement proves that there is $K\ge0$ such that, for every $0<T\le1$ and $n\ge0$, $\|a_n-G_n(\cdot)a_n(0)-\mathcal B_n(a_n,a_n)\|_{C([0,\ell];H^1)}\le\theta^nKT^{1/4}$. The assertion itself has no hypothesis $\theta<1$; that further inequality is needed when this is used as decay in $n$. This is a sequence estimate, rather than the paper’s single $C_\kappa$ estimate with an explicit large-period constant.
Breakdown.Periodic.approxResidualSmall.summary: Assuming four properties of the cutoff, residual, interval matching and transplant, and given the periodic kernel estimate, $0<\lambda<1$, $\theta>\lambda^{1/4}$, some $K\ge0$ bounds the Duhamel residual of $a_n$ by $\theta^nKT^{1/4}$ for $0<T\le1$. It has no hypothesis $\theta<1$.

Breakdown.Periodic.approxSizes.text:
The proof assumes five analytic properties, each for all inputs of the indicated class. For every smooth solenoidal field supported in $\bar B_b$ at an admissible scale $0<\mu\le1$, $b>0$, $\sqrt\mu b\le1/8$, the field $\mu^{1/4}g_\mu$, with $g_\mu(x)=\mu^{-1/2}g((w(x)-a)/\sqrt\mu)$, $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$ and coordinate reduction $w$ to the unit cell, has squared periodic norm $\|\nabla g\|_2^2+\mu\|g\|_2^2$. For every similarity profile with the smoothness, equation and decay bounds stated below, its cutoff velocity and the pressure $p^{\mathrm a}(t,x)=\chi(x)[p^*(t,x)-p^*(t,a+(3/32)e_1)]$, where $p^*(t,x)=(T-t)^{-1}q(\log(T/(T-t)),(x-a)/\sqrt{T-t})$, are smooth for $t<T$, supported in $\bar B_{1/8}(a)$, the velocity is solenoidal, and it agrees with the centered self-similar field on $\bar B_{1/16}(a)$. Its normalized interval curves have their defining formula and satisfy $a_{n+1}(0)=\lambda^{1/4}a_n(1-\lambda)$ for $0<T\le1$ and $0<\lambda<1$. Finally, for every smooth solenoidal field with $|g(x)|\le C/(1+|x|)$ and $\|Dg(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C/(1+|x|)^2$, its whole-space Fourier embedding is linear under addition, subtraction and real scalar multiplication and has squared norm $\int|\nabla g|^2$. These are the five extra premises of this proof theorem. Its conclusion is the uniform approximate-interval bound below.

Assume that $W:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ and $q:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ are smooth, that $\operatorname{div}W=0$, and that $\partial_sW+\tfrac12W+\tfrac12(y\cdot\nabla)W-\Delta W+(W\cdot\nabla)W+\nabla q=0$ for every $(s,y)$. A single constant $C$ bounds $\|D^jW(s,y)\|\le C(1+|y|)^{-j-1}$ for the integer orders $j=0,1,2$, and $|\nabla q(s,y)|\le C(1+|y|)^{-3}$, uniformly in $s$. The norms of $D^jW$ are multilinear operator norms; for $j=1$ the paper’s Frobenius norm is between the operator norm and $\sqrt3$ times that norm.

The periodic space is the real solenoidal Fourier realization of $H^1(\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3)$, with squared norm $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+4\pi^2|k|^2)|\widehat v(k)|^2$. Its zero Fourier coefficient is allowed to be nonzero.

For $T>0$ and $t<T$, put $s=\log(T/(T-t))$ and $u_T^*(t,x)=(T-t)^{-1/2}W(s,(x-a)/\sqrt{T-t})$, where $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$. Choose a fixed smooth cutoff $\chi$, equal to one on $\bar B_{1/16}(a)$ and zero when $|x-a|\ge1/8$. Put $A_g(x)=\int_0^1\tau g(a+\tau(x-a))\times(x-a)\,d\tau$. The cutoff is $\bar u_T=\chi u_T^*+\nabla\chi\times A_{u_T^*}$, which equals $\operatorname{curl}(\chi A_{u_T^*})$ when $u_T^*$ is solenoidal.

Write $\mu_n=T\lambda^n$, $t_n=T-\mu_n$, $\ell=1-\lambda$, and $a_n(s)=\mu_n^{1/4}u^{\mathrm a}(t_n+\mu_ns)$ for $0\le s\le\ell$, where $u^{\mathrm a}$ is the unit-periodic extension of the solenoidal cutoff of the centered self-similar field. The index $n$ is a nonnegative integer and the interval norm is the supremum norm.

Assume $0<\lambda<1$ and $c>0$ with $c\le\|W(s)\|_X$ for every real $s$.

The formal statement proves the existence of $T_0>0$ and $M\in\mathbb R$ such that, for every $0<T<T_0$ and every $n\ge0$, $\|a_n\|_{C([0,\ell];H^1)}\le M$ and $c/2\le\|a_n(s)\|_{H^1}$ for every $0\le s\le\ell$. Here $\|W(s)\|_X=\|\nabla W(s)\|_2$. The curve is represented by its continuous restriction; the general construction uses zero if continuity fails, while the profile hypotheses ensure continuity here. The statement gives no equality with a whole-space homogeneous norm and no explicit factor $c_*-CL^{-1/2}$.
Breakdown.Periodic.approxSizes.summary: Assuming five properties of the transplant, cutoff, matching and embedding, if $c\le\|W(s)\|_X$ for all $s$ there are $T_0>0$ and $M$ with $\|a_n\|_{C([0,\ell];H^1)}\le M$ and $\|a_n(s)\|_{H^1}\ge c/2$ for $0<T<T_0$. There is no explicit factor $c_*-CL^{-1/2}$.

Breakdown.Periodic.breakdownOnTorus_of_p.text:
Let $W:\mathbb R	imes\mathbb R^3	o\mathbb R^3$ and $q:\mathbb R	imes\mathbb R^3	o\mathbb R$ be jointly smooth. For every $s\in\mathbb R$ and $y\in\mathbb R^3$, assume $\partial_sW+ rac12W+ rac12(y\cdot
abla)W-\Delta W+(W\cdot
abla)W+
abla q=0$ and $\operatorname{div}W=0$. Assume one real constant $C$ gives $\|D_y^jW(s,y)\|\le C(1+|y|)^{-j-1}$ for the integers $j=0,1,2$, and $|
abla_yq(s,y)|\le C(1+|y|)^{-3}$, uniformly in all $s,y$. Here $D_y^0W=W$, while for $j=1,2$ the derivative is a linear or bilinear map with its operator norm. The paper uses the square root of the sum of squared coordinate derivatives. These norms are equivalent in dimension three, with fixed factors; an unspecified bound transfers after enlarging $C$, but the same numerical constant is not asserted. In addition, there are $S>0$ and an orthogonal linear map $R:\mathbb R^3	o\mathbb R^3$ such that $W(s+S,y)=RW(s,R^{-1}y)$ for every $s,y$, and $W(s,y)
e0$ for at least one pair $(s,y)$. Both rotations and orientation-reversing orthogonal maps are admitted. No recurrence condition is imposed on $q$ itself. Under these assumptions the formal statement concludes the following. For each viscosity $
u>0$ there is a smooth field $u_0:\mathbb R^3	o\mathbb R^3$ with $u_0(x+e_i)=u_0(x)$ for each coordinate vector $e_i$ and $\operatorname{div}u_0=0$, such that no pair of globally defined functions $u(t,x),p(t,x)$ is jointly smooth on $[0,\infty)	imes\mathbb R^3$, has $u(0)=u_0$, satisfies $\partial_tu+(u\cdot
abla)u=
u\Delta u-
abla p$ and $\operatorname{div}u=0$ for every $t>0$, and has $u(t,x+e_i)=u(t,x)$ for every $t\ge0$. These periodic fields represent fields on $\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$. Periodicity is required of the velocity only. The excluded pressure may be any smooth scalar field on $\mathbb R^3$, including a nonperiodic one. There is no separate energy condition, prescribed mean, blow-up time, two-sided rate, or comparison on a ball. Values at negative times have no role. Relative to Theorem 1.1, the smooth finite-time trajectory and both estimates in (1.7) are absent, while the profile premise explicitly includes extra derivative and pressure-gradient decay. Allowing nonperiodic pressures makes the excluded class of global solutions larger than the paper's definition of a torus solution.
Breakdown.Periodic.breakdownOnTorus_of_p.summary: A smooth recurrent nonzero profile with the stated decay implies, for each $\nu>0$, a smooth period-one divergence-free $u_0$ with no global smooth periodic-velocity solution. The trajectory and (1.7) are absent, the premise has extra decay, and nonperiodic pressures enlarge the excluded class.

Breakdown.Periodic.cell.text: The formal integration cell is $[0,1]^3\subset\mathbb R^3$, with ordinary three-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Including both faces of this cube changes no integral because its boundary has measure zero. For a period-one integrand this cell gives the same integral as the paper's centered cell $[-1/2,1/2)^3$. The formal statement defines only this fixed cell; the family $Q_L=[-L/2,L/2)^3$ for arbitrary $L>0$ is not a parameterized object here. Its volume is one, so the period-one Fourier coefficient has no extra normalization factor.
Breakdown.Periodic.cell.summary: The integration cell $[0,1]^3$ with Lebesgue measure, which gives the same integral for period-one integrands as the paper's $[-1/2,1/2)^3$. The family $Q_L$ for general $L$ is not parameterized here.

Breakdown.Periodic.chainOp.text:
Let $E,Y,Z$ be real normed spaces. Given bounded linear maps $S:Y\to Y$, $G:E\to Y$, $B:Z\to Y$ and $R:Y\to Z$, the formal definition is $\mathcal L(e,y)=y-Sy-Ge-BRy$.

In the application $Y$ is a space of bounded sequences of continuous time intervals, $Z$ records local values and derivatives, $S$ propagates data from the preceding interval, $G$ inserts the initial correction, and $BR$ is the interaction with the approximate field. No invertibility or smallness is asserted by this definition. The paper’s identity (6.13) concerns the defect of a particular candidate inverse, which requires further substitutions.
Breakdown.Periodic.chainOp.summary: Defines $\mathcal L(e,y)=y-Sy-Ge-BRy$ for bounded linear $S,G,B,R$, the factored interval linearization with propagation $S$, datum insertion $G$ and interaction $BR$. No invertibility is asserted; (6.13) concerns a particular candidate inverse.

Breakdown.Periodic.coeff.text: The formal periodic space represents real divergence-free fields of period one by sequences $a(n)\in\mathbb C^3$, $n\in\mathbb Z^3$, with $\sum_n|a(n)|^2<\infty$, $a(-n)=\overline{a(n)}$ and $n\cdot a(n)=0$. The physical Fourier coefficient is $c(n)=a(n)/(1+4\pi^2|n|^2)^{1/2}$. Its squared norm is $\|u\|^2=\sum_n(1+4\pi^2|n|^2)|c(n)|^2$, the inhomogeneous $H^1$ norm; the mean $c(0)$ may be nonzero. The formal operation recovers $c(n)$ by dividing the weighted coefficient $a(n)$ by $\sqrt{1+4\pi^2|n|^2}$. The denominator is at least one, including at $n=0$; division by zero is therefore irrelevant. Thus a coordinate of the representing sequence is a weighted coefficient, whereas the paper's $\hat u(n)$ is the unweighted coefficient. There is no assumption that this coefficient vanishes at zero and no spatial period parameter.
Breakdown.Periodic.coeff.summary: Given the weighted sequence $a(n)$, defines the physical Fourier coefficient $\hat u(n)=a(n)/\sqrt{1+4\pi^2|n|^2}$, whose denominator is at least one. The paper uses $\hat u(n)$ directly.

Breakdown.Periodic.comparisonSmall.text: The comparison becomes smaller than any prescribed tolerance when the blow-up time is sufficiently small. The explicit powers of the large period in the digest are conclusions of the paper’s comparison estimates.

Breakdown.Periodic.cutoffDivergenceFree.text: Assume the radial-potential assertion that every smooth solenoidal $g$ has a smooth potential $A_{x_0,g}$ with $\operatorname{curl}A_{x_0,g}=g$. For every smooth scalar function $\chi:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$, every centre $x_0$ and every smooth solenoidal vector field $g$, the formal statement then proves that $\bar g=\chi g+\nabla\chi\times A_{x_0,g}$ is smooth and $\nabla\cdot\bar g=0$ at every point. Here $A_{x_0,g}(x)=\int_0^1\sigma\,g(x_0+\sigma(x-x_0))\times(x-x_0)\,d\sigma$. In §5 take $x_0=0$, $g=u^*(t)$ and $\chi(x)=\eta(x/r)$ with $r>0$. This theorem assumes no support or size conditions on $\chi$ and therefore gives no support radius, no equality on an inner ball, and no norm bound. Its radial-potential premise is proved in the preceding curl theorem.
Breakdown.Periodic.cutoffDivergenceFree.summary: Assuming every smooth solenoidal $g$ has $\operatorname{curl}A_{x_0,g}=g$, for any smooth $\chi$, centre $x_0$ and smooth solenoidal $g$, $\bar g=\chi g+\nabla\chi\times A_{x_0,g}$ is smooth with $\nabla\cdot\bar g=0$. It gives no support radius or norm bound.

Breakdown.Periodic.cutoffField.text: For a scalar function $\chi:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$, a centre $x_0$ and a vector field $g:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$, the formal definition is $\bar g=\chi g+\nabla\chi\times A_{x_0,g}$, where $A_{x_0,g}(x)=\int_0^1\sigma\,g(x_0+\sigma(x-x_0))\times(x-x_0)\,d\sigma$. With $x_0=0$, $g=u^*(t)$ and $\chi(x)=\eta(x/r)$ for $r>0$, this is the expanded formula $\eta(x/r)u^*(t,x)+r^{-1}\nabla\eta(x/r)\times A(t,x)$ in the proof of Lemma 5.1. When $\chi$ and $g$ are smooth and $g$ is solenoidal, the identity $\operatorname{curl}A_{x_0,g}=g$ and the product rule identify this definition with $\operatorname{curl}(\chi A_{x_0,g})$. The definition itself requires none of these hypotheses and asserts neither smoothness nor support. Derivatives and the integral are total operations: a derivative is zero where the required derivative does not exist, and a nonintegrable integral is zero. The smoothness hypotheses in the applications eliminate these conventions.
Breakdown.Periodic.cutoffField.summary: Defines $\bar g=\chi g+\nabla\chi\times A_{x_0,g}$ with $A_{x_0,g}(x)=\int_0^1\sigma g(x_0+\sigma(x-x_0))\times(x-x_0)\,d\sigma$, the expanded formula in the proof of Lemma 5.1. It assumes no smoothness and asserts neither smoothness nor support.

Breakdown.Periodic.cutoffGradientClose.text:
Let $W:\mathbb R	imes\mathbb R^3	o\mathbb R^3$ and $q:\mathbb R	imes\mathbb R^3	o\mathbb R$ be smooth and satisfy $\partial_sW+ rac12W+ rac12(y\cdot
abla)W-\Delta W+(W\cdot
abla)W+
abla q=0$ and $
abla\cdot W=0$ for every $(s,y)$. Assume, uniformly in $s,y$, $\|D_y^jW(s,y)\|_{m op}\le C(1+|y|)^{-j-1}$ for the three integer orders $j=0,1,2$, and $|
abla_yq(s,y)|\le C(1+|y|)^{-3}$. These assumptions imply $C\ge0$; recurrence and nonvanishing are not required here. The norm on a first derivative is its operator norm; the paper's pointwise matrix norm is the square root of the sum of the squared column lengths, which is at most $\sqrt3$ times this norm.

Put $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$ and let $\chi$ be the fixed smooth cutoff with $0\le\chi\le1$, equal to one for $|x-a|\le1/16$ and zero for $|x-a|\ge1/8$. For $T>0$, $t<T$, set $\ell=T-t$, $s=-\log(\ell/T)$ and $g(x)=\ell^{-1/2}W(s,(x-a)/\sqrt\ell)$. Define $A_g(x)=\int_0^1\sigma\,g(a+\sigma(x-a))	imes(x-a)\,d\sigma$, $ ar u(x)=\chi(x)g(x)+
abla\chi(x)	imes A_g(x)$, and $f(y)=\sqrt\ell\, ar u(a+\sqrt\ell\,y)$. Thus $f$ is the cutoff expressed in similarity coordinates; its inner and outer radii are $1/(16\sqrt\ell)$ and $1/(8\sqrt\ell)$. Put $x_a=a+(3/32)e_1$ and $ ar p(x)=\chi(x)\ell^{-1}[q(s,(x-a)/\sqrt\ell)-q(s,(x_a-a)/\sqrt\ell)]$.

Assume, for every profile satisfying the displayed hypotheses and every $T>0$, that $ ar u, ar p$ are smooth on $(-\infty,T)	imes\mathbb R^3$, the velocity is solenoidal, both vanish for $|x-a|\ge1/8$, and the velocity equals $g$ on $|x-a|\le1/16$; this property is proved separately. For every $\varepsilon>0$, the formal statement gives $\ell_0>0$ such that, for every $T>0$ and $t<T$ with $T-t<\ell_0$, $\int_{\mathbb R^3}\sum_{i=1}^3|\partial_i(W(s,y)-f(y))|^2\,dy\le\varepsilon$. The integral is the squared homogeneous $H^1$ norm with Lebesgue measure, using the same sum of squared column lengths as the paper. The threshold is uniform in $T,t$ for the fixed profile. This is convergence as the cutoff radius in similarity coordinates tends to infinity. The exported conclusion gives no power-law rate, no estimate for every prescribed $r>0$, and no bound by the particular constant in (5.2). It uses the ordinary integral of the squared gradient under the smoothness and decay assumptions, despite the general formal integral being assigned zero for nonintegrable functions.
Breakdown.Periodic.cutoffGradientClose.summary: Assuming the cutoff support property, for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $\ell_0>0$ with $\int\sum_i|\partial_i(W(s,y)-f(y))|^2dy\le\varepsilon$ whenever $T-t<\ell_0$, uniformly in $T,t$. It gives no power-law rate and no bound by the constant in (5.2).

Breakdown.Periodic.cutoffMassBound.text:
Let $W:\mathbb R	imes\mathbb R^3	o\mathbb R^3$ and $q:\mathbb R	imes\mathbb R^3	o\mathbb R$ be smooth and satisfy $\partial_sW+ rac12W+ rac12(y\cdot
abla)W-\Delta W+(W\cdot
abla)W+
abla q=0$ and $
abla\cdot W=0$ for every $(s,y)$. Assume, uniformly in $s,y$, $\|D_y^jW(s,y)\|_{m op}\le C(1+|y|)^{-j-1}$ for the three integer orders $j=0,1,2$, and $|
abla_yq(s,y)|\le C(1+|y|)^{-3}$. These assumptions imply $C\ge0$; recurrence and nonvanishing are not required here. The norm on a first derivative is its operator norm; the paper's pointwise matrix norm is the square root of the sum of the squared column lengths, which is at most $\sqrt3$ times this norm.

Put $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$ and let $\chi$ be the fixed smooth cutoff with $0\le\chi\le1$, equal to one for $|x-a|\le1/16$ and zero for $|x-a|\ge1/8$. For $T>0$, $t<T$, set $\ell=T-t$, $s=-\log(\ell/T)$ and $g(x)=\ell^{-1/2}W(s,(x-a)/\sqrt\ell)$. Define $A_g(x)=\int_0^1\sigma\,g(a+\sigma(x-a))	imes(x-a)\,d\sigma$, $ ar u(x)=\chi(x)g(x)+
abla\chi(x)	imes A_g(x)$, and $f(y)=\sqrt\ell\, ar u(a+\sqrt\ell\,y)$. Thus $f$ is the cutoff expressed in similarity coordinates; its inner and outer radii are $1/(16\sqrt\ell)$ and $1/(8\sqrt\ell)$. Put $x_a=a+(3/32)e_1$ and $ ar p(x)=\chi(x)\ell^{-1}[q(s,(x-a)/\sqrt\ell)-q(s,(x_a-a)/\sqrt\ell)]$.

Assume, for every profile satisfying the displayed hypotheses and every $T>0$, that $ ar u, ar p$ are smooth on $(-\infty,T)	imes\mathbb R^3$, the velocity is solenoidal, both vanish for $|x-a|\ge1/8$, and the velocity equals $g$ on $|x-a|\le1/16$. The formal statement gives a real constant $K$, depending on the fixed profile and cutoff and independent of $T,t$, such that $\int_{\mathbb R^3}|f(y)|^2\,dy\le K/\sqrt\ell$ whenever $T>0$, $t<T$ and $0<\ell=T-t\le1$. It asserts a bound for the squared $L^2$ norm in similarity coordinates. In terms of the outer radius $r_\ell=1/(8\sqrt\ell)$ this is $\|f\|_2^2\le8Kr_\ell$, and taking a square root gives a constant times $r_\ell^{1/2}$. The explicit hypothesis $\ell\le1$ restricts this reading to $r_\ell\ge1/8$. The statement does not directly give the arbitrary-radius physical cutoff of Lemma 5.1. Since $\ell>0$, the denominator is nonzero; the source proves the needed ordinary integrability from the compact support and smoothness.
Breakdown.Periodic.cutoffMassBound.summary: Assuming the cutoff support property, one constant $K$ gives $\int|f(y)|^2dy\le K/\sqrt\ell$ for $0<\ell=T-t\le1$, a squared $L^2$ norm bound in similarity coordinates. It does not directly give the arbitrary-radius cutoff of Lemma 5.1.

Breakdown.Periodic.divFree.text: For $k\in\mathbb Z^3$ and $c\in\mathbb C^3$, the result is $c$ if $k=0$ and $c-(\sum_i k_ic_i)|k|^{-2}k$ otherwise. This is the orthogonal projection onto the plane perpendicular to the real vector $k$, extended to complex coefficients, so it is the matrix $\mathbb P_k=I-|k|^{-2}k\otimes k$. The zero coefficient is left unchanged, as the paper specifies. The nonzero branch has $|k|^2>0$, and no ambiguous division occurs. This algebraic definition alone does not provide a bounded projection on any particular function space or require a field to have zero mean.
Breakdown.Periodic.divFree.summary: For $k\in\mathbb Z^3$ and $c\in\mathbb C^3$, gives $c$ if $k=0$ and $c-(k\cdot c)|k|^{-2}k$ otherwise, the matrix $\mathbb P_k=I-|k|^{-2}k\otimes k$ with the zero coefficient unchanged, as the paper specifies.

Breakdown.Periodic.forceV.text: For a field $f:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ and $\tau>0$, the formal construction has Fourier coefficient $e^{-4\pi^2\tau|n|^2}P_n\hat f(n)$ on the unit torus, where $\hat f(n)=\int_{[0,1]^3}e^{-2\pi in\cdot x}f(x)\,dx$ and $P_nc=c-n(n\cdot c)/|n|^2$ for $n\ne0$. At $n=0$, $P_0=I$, so the mean is retained. The representing sequence entry is this coefficient multiplied by $\sqrt{1+4\pi^2|n|^2}$, and the output belongs to the inhomogeneous periodic space. The construction is set to zero for $\tau\le0$. It is defined for every $f$, with zero assigned to a Fourier integral lacking Bochner integrability; for $f\in L^1([0,1]^3)$ it has the ordinary projected heat-flow meaning. The definition supplies neither the uniform arbitrary-period estimate nor the $L^{3/2}$ bound in (3.19).
Breakdown.Periodic.forceV.summary: For $\tau>0$, the unit-torus field with coefficients $e^{-4\pi^2\tau|n|^2}P_n\hat f(n)$, keeping the mean, in the inhomogeneous periodic space; zero for $\tau\le0$. It supplies neither the arbitrary-period estimate nor the $L^{3/2}$ bound in (3.19).

Breakdown.Periodic.freeHeatComparison.text:
This theorem assumes the following analytic representation facts. On the unit torus, every $C^1$ periodic vector field satisfies $\widehat{\partial_jf}(k)=2\pi i k_j\widehat f(k)$. A smooth compactly supported solenoidal field transplanted at $0<\mu\le1$, $b>0$, $\sqrt\mu b\le1/8$ is smooth, unit-periodic, solenoidal, and agrees with its unwrapped dilation on the ball of radius $1/4$ about $(1/2,1/2,1/2)$. The whole-space heat operators form a strongly continuous self-adjoint contraction semigroup for nonnegative time and act by the multiplier $e^{-4\pi^2\max(t,0)|\xi|^2}$ on their Fourier representatives.

The proof also assumes: uniformly bounded measurable matrix multipliers after any invertible real linear frequency change have their stated almost-everywhere $L^2$ action; the direct and inverse $L^2$ Fourier transforms agree with the corresponding integrals on $L^1\cap L^2$; real $L^2$ fields have conjugate-symmetric Fourier transforms; and, when $h(\xi)=2\pi|\xi|g(\xi)$ almost everywhere for solenoidal representatives, the velocity reconstructed from $h$ equals the real inverse Fourier transform of $g$. The main construction supplies these analytic facts before using this theorem.

The whole-space norm is $\|v\|_X=\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3)}$ on solenoidal velocities in $L^6(\mathbb R^3)$.

Local data are a tuple $(A_1,A_2,A_3,v)$ with $A_j\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ and $v\in L^6(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$, measured by $\max\{\max_j\|A_j\|_2,\|v\|_6\}$. No compatibility condition $A_j=\partial_jv$ or divergence condition is part of this data space.

Write $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$ and let $w(x)$ reduce each coordinate of $x$ modulo integers to the cell centered at $a$. For $\mu>0$, the transplanted field is $g_\mu(x)=\mu^{-1/2}g((w(x)-a)/\sqrt\mu)$.

Whole-space restriction to $\bar B_b$ consists of $1_{\bar B_b}\partial_jv$ and $1_{\bar B_b}v$. At an admissible periodic scale $0<\mu\le1$, $b>0$, $\sqrt\mu\,b\le1/8$, periodic restriction consists of $1_{\bar B_b}\mu^{3/4}\partial_jz(a+\sqrt\mu\,y)$ and $1_{\bar B_b}\mu^{1/4}z(a+\sqrt\mu\,y)$, interpreted almost everywhere. It is defined to be zero if these scale conditions fail.

For every smooth compactly supported solenoidal field $\varphi$, and every $b,\varepsilon,\delta>0$, the formal statement asserts the existence of $\mu_0>0$ such that, for $0<\mu<\mu_0$ and $0\le\tau\le\varepsilon^{-1}$, the local-data norm of the difference between the restrictions of $e^{\tau\Delta}\varphi$ and $\mu^{1/4}e^{\mu\tau\Delta}\varphi_\mu$ is at most $\delta$. This is uniform convergence on a bounded time interval, including time zero. The threshold can depend on $\varphi$ and no bound proportional to $\|\varphi\|_1$ is asserted. Formula (6.3) instead gives a uniform explicit $L^{-5/2}$ estimate for all $t>0$.
Breakdown.Periodic.freeHeatComparison.summary: Assuming the listed Fourier facts, for each test field $\varphi$, small $\mu$ and $0\le\tau\le\varepsilon^{-1}$, the local restrictions of $e^{\tau\Delta}\varphi$ and $\mu^{1/4}e^{\mu\tau\Delta}\varphi_\mu$ differ by at most $\delta$. (6.3) instead gives an explicit $L^{-5/2}$ estimate.

Breakdown.Periodic.freqTrCoef.text: For a vector field $f:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ and $n\in\mathbb Z^3$, the formal coefficient is $\int_{[0,1]^3}e^{-2\pi i n\cdot x}f(x)\,dx\in\mathbb C^3$, with the real components of $f$ viewed as complex numbers. On integrable period-one fields this is the paper's Fourier coefficient at $L=1$. The inverse series uses $e^{2\pi i n\cdot x}$. The definition itself imposes neither periodicity nor integrability; an integral without Bochner integrability is assigned zero. At general period $L>0$, the paper's frequency is $k=n/L$ and its coefficient includes $L^{-3}$. That general-period coefficient can be expressed using $f(L\,\cdot)$, but the formal definition has no variable $L$.
Breakdown.Periodic.freqTrCoef.summary: Defines $\int_{[0,1]^3}e^{-2\pi in\cdot x}f(x)\,dx$, the paper's Fourier coefficient at $L=1$ for integrable period-one fields; a nonintegrable integral is taken as zero. There is no period variable $L$.

Breakdown.Periodic.glueUnbounded.text:
